        "text":"Diagnosed. Here's what's actually happening — the external exporter is **architecturally wrong for our use case**.\n\n## What the external tool actually does\n\n**It was designed for projects living under `/home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/`**, where the assumption is:\n- Each \"project\" is both a Claude conversation source (lookup-by-name) and a render destination\n- A \"project dir\" has its own `llm-transcripts/` already populated by a separate backup script\n- The exporter then re-renders those .md files into combined output at the requested verbosity\n\n**Bugs as applied to soramech:**\n\n1. **Wrong source for v0–v4**: The exporter doesn't read `~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/`. It reads `$project_dir/llm-transcripts/*.md` — meaning it picked up our **old** `2029ad16-*` per-conversation files (from May 8) and re-bundled those as \"the conversations.\" Brand-new conversations from May 23 are invisible because they aren't in our `llm-transcripts/` dir.\n\n2. **Wrong source for v5 (raw)**: The `process_raw_conversation()` function loops over `~/.claude/projects/*` and **breaks on the first dir with JSONL files** — alphabetical order, which gave us `-mnt-cmdo-ritz-games-tq-my-games-cyoa` (a CYOA game project). That's why v5 is 70KB — it's exporting a completely different project's tiny conversation.\n\n3. **Global CLAUDE.md spam in v5**: confirmed, the raw mode prepends global CLAUDE.md as a \"context file.\" Pure noise.\n\n4. **No incremental support**: re-runs every conversation top-to-bottom, every time. Sluggish.\n\n## Issue files\n\nThe closest ones I found are in *other* projects' issues dirs — `scripts/issues/009-batch-transcript-backup-with-tui.md` and `delta-version/issues/completed/035g-transcript-to-commit-provenance.md`. The exporter doesn't appear to have a dedicated spec issue file in the scripts repo itself — it grew organically.\n\n## Recommended fix: write our own local script\n\nThe external tool isn't worth fixing for our case. It was built for a different shape of project; layering compatibility patches would be more code than just doing it right. A local script in `scripts/export-llm-transcripts.sh` should:\n\n- **Read directly from `~/.claude/projects/-mnt-mtwo-programs-sora-soramech/*.jsonl`** — hardcoded for this project (matches CLAUDE.md \"all scripts should have hard-coded `${DIR}`\" convention).\n- **One file per conversation per verbosity level** — organized as `llm-transcripts/v{N}/<conv-id>.md`. Easier to find a specific conversation; easier for incremental refresh.\n- **Six well-defined detail levels** — distinct semantics each:\n  - **v0** code blocks only (extracted from assistant messages)\n  - **v1** user prompts + assistant text replies (no tool calls)\n  - **v2** v1 + tool call summaries (Bash command lines, Edit paths)\n  - **v3** v2 + tool results (truncated)\n  - **v4** full assistant + tool call/result content\n  - **v5** raw JSONL pretty-printed (one entry per line, json formatted)\n- **Incremental** — compare each JSONL's `mtime` against each output's `mtime`; skip the conversion if the output is newer than the source.\n- **No global CLAUDE.md spam** — never inject context files; the conversation itself is what we want.\n- **Fast** — running over 14 JSONLs at 6 levels with incremental should finish in seconds, not minutes.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nThe external tool's bugs all trace back to one architectural choice: it tries to be a *general* exporter for many possible project layouts, which forces it into discovery heuristics (\"guess where the conversations are\"). A *project-local* script can hardcode the answer, which is both simpler and more correct. CLAUDE.md's \"hard-coded ${DIR} with override\" convention is the same principle — knowing-instead-of-guessing wins.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n**Before I rewrite:** want me to proceed with this plan, or would you rather adjust the verbosity-level scheme first? My six-level proposal is a guess at what would be useful — you might want different breakpoints (e.g. \"just code\", \"decisions only\", \"full text\", and \"raw\" — four levels instead of six). What feels right?",

        "text":"# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt\n\nParse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.\n\n## Parsing (in priority order)\n\n1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.\n2. **Trailing \"every\" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows \"every\" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.\n3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see \"Dynamic mode\" below).\n\nIf the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.\n\nExamples:\n- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)\n- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)\n- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)\n- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)\n- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — \"every\" not followed by time)\n- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage\n\n## Offer cloud first\n\nBefore any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:\n- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or\n- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing (\"every morning\", \"daily\", \"every day\", \"each night\", \"every weekday\")\n\nIf either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:\n- `question`: \"This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?\"\n- `header`: \"Schedule\"\n- `options`: `[{label: \"Cloud schedule (recommended)\", description: \"Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session\"}, {label: \"This session only\", description: \"Runs in this terminal until you exit\"}]`\n\nIf they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: \"schedule\", args: \"every morning tell me a joke\"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no \"execute the prompt now\").\nIf they pick **This session only**:\n- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.\n- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.\nIf neither trigger condition was met: continue below.\n\n## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)\n\nConvert the interval to a cron expression:\n\n| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |\n|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|\n| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |\n| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|\n| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |\n| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |\n| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |\n\n**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.\n\nThen:\n1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.\n2. Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.\n3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.\n\n## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)\n\nThe user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.\n\n1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.\n2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.\n3. **At the end of this turn, call ScheduleWakeup** with:\n   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks past the 5-minute cache window are pure overhead). Head/tail track FIFO position; head == tail\n * means the ring is empty. No filled_size field — the order ring is\n * plain FIFO (no lowest-tag pop semantics), so head/tail are\n * sufficient to detect emptiness. */\n#define ORDER_CELL_RECORD ((uint32_t)8)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Internal store */\nstruct slot_store {\n    slot_rec_t **slots;        /* dynamic array, indexed by slot_id_t */\n    int32_t      count;\n    int32_t      capacity;\n\n    /* The unified allocator. Owns the cell-array memory for every\n     * ring slot in this store, plus the payload bytes for every\n     * LARGE_VALUE cell. Created in slot_store_create; destroyed\n     * alongside the store. Any chunks still parked in cells at\n     * destroy time are reclaimed in bulk when the allocator's\n     * regions are freed. */\n    ua_t        *heap;\n};\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — locking */\nstatic inline void lock_slot(slot_rec_t *r)\n{\n    while (atomic_flag_test_and_set_explicit(&r->lock, memory_order_acquire)) {\n        /* spin — contention is expected to be brief because the\n         * locked section is just a header update plus a memcpy. */\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline void unlock_slot(slot_rec_t *r)\n{\n    atomic_flag_clear_explicit(&r->lock, memory_order_release);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helpers — cell layout */\n/* Pointer to the i-th cell within the slot's flexible array. The cell\n * record layout for ring slots is:\n *\n *   bytes 0..3   : filled_size (uint32_t; 0 means empty)\n *   bytes 4..7   : tag         (uint32_t; SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED *or*\n *                               SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE — the latter\n *                               keeps the 8-byte payload offset\n *                               consistent so the inline pointer is\n *                               always aligned)\n *   bytes (4|8)..: payload     (cell_capacity bytes; for LARGE_VALUE\n *                               this is a stable lvh-heap pointer)\n */\nstatic inline uint8_t *cell_ptr(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    /* r->cells is now a pointer into an allocator chunk, not a\n     * flexible array on the slot record itself — same indexing\n     * arithmetic. */\n    return r->cells + (size_t)i * r->cell_record;\n}\n\nstatic inline uint32_t cell_filled(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    uint32_t v;\n    memcpy(&v, cell_ptr(r, i), sizeof v);\n    return v;\n}\n\nstatic inline uint32_t cell_tag(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    uint32_t v;\n    memcpy(&v, cell_ptr(r, i) + 4, sizeof v);\n    return v;\n}\n\n/* The payload offset within a cell is 8 if there's a tag header OR\n * if the slot is LARGE_VALUE (we always reserve 4 bytes of pad for\n * LARGE_VALUE so the inline pointer is 8-byte aligned). Otherwise\n * it's 4. */\nstatic inline uint8_t *cell_data(slot_rec_t *r, uint32_t i)\n{\n    int has_8b_header = (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED)\n                     || (r->flags & SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE);\n    return cell_ptr(r, i) + (has_8b_header ? 8 : 4);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_create() */\nslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);\n    if (!s) return NULL;\n    s->capacity = 16;\n    s->slots    = calloc((size_t)s->capacity, sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n    if (!s->slots) { free(s); return NULL; }\n\n    /* Eagerly create the unified allocator. Earlier in this issue\n     * the allocator was lazy-created on the first LARGE_VALUE slot;\n     * since the cell arrays of ordinary ring slots also live in the\n     * allocator now, every slot allocation needs the allocator\n     * present from the start. No pre-warmed classes — they accrete\n     * on first use until the graph loader is wired to declare\n     * sizes up front. */\n    s->heap = ua_create(NULL, 0);\n    if (!s->heap) { free(s->slots); free(s); return NULL; }\n\n    return s;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_destroy() */\nvoid slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    if (!s) return;\n    /* Release each slot's cell-array chunk before tearing down the\n     * allocator. We don't strictly need to (ua_destroy frees all\n     * regions in bulk) but the unref'ed-then-destroyed path leaves\n     * the allocator's stats coherent if anything inspects them on\n     * the way out. The slot record itself was allocated via plain\n     * malloc and is freed here. */\n    for (int32_t i = 0; i < s->count; i++) {\n        slot_rec_t *r = s->slots[i];\n        if (!r) continue;\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n    }"
    },

    "newString":"## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Full design in parent issue\n319's \"Q1\" resolution.\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`src/009-slot-store.c` uses a flat `slot_rec_t **slots` array\nwith `realloc()`-based growth (`grow_store_if_needed`). This\nworks at graph load (single-threaded) but is unsafe at runtime\nbecause `realloc()` can MOVE the array, invalidating any slot\npointer a worker has cached.\n\nThe slot RECORDS themselves are already heap-allocated\nseparately (per-slot `malloc`), so their addresses are stable.\nOnly the `slots[]` array of POINTERS is the problem.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nReplace the flat `slots[]` array with a two-level chunked-append\nstructure:\n\n- **Chunk size**: 64 slot-pointers per chunk (cache-friendly).\n- **Top-level array**: holds chunk pointers; starts at 16\n  entries (1024 slots without top-level growth). Doubles via\n  copy-and-publish with defer-free when it fills.\n- **Atomic count**: tracks total slots ever allocated. Readers\n  use acquire-load to see slots published with release-store.\n- **`pthread_mutex_t alloc_lock`**: serializes `slot_alloc`.\n  Readers (push/pop via `get_slot`) take no lock here — the\n  per-slot spinlock is still the only hot-path synchronization.\n- **Stale-top free list**: top-level arrays from prior growth\n  events stay alive on a linked list until `slot_store_destroy`.\n  Any worker that cached a stale top-pointer mid-growth can\n  finish its lookup safely; the chunks the stale top points to\n  are still valid because chunks never move.\n\nSlot lookup: `top[id/64][id%64]`. One extra indirection per\naccess vs the old flat array, in exchange for the runtime-safe\ngrowth.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Change the `slot_store` struct definition (private in the\n   .c file; header has only the opaque forward declaration so\n   no public API change).\n2. Add `SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE` (64) and `INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY` (16).\n3. Rewrite `slot_store_create` to allocate the initial top-level\n   array, init the mutex, init the atomic count.\n4. Rewrite `slot_store_destroy` to iterate over chunks, free\n   slot records and each chunk, then free the stale-top list.\n5. Replace `grow_store_if_needed` with `grow_top_level` (called\n   under `alloc_lock`).\n6. Rewrite `slot_alloc`: take the lock, claim id, ensure chunk\n   exists, publish slot, release-store the count.\n7. Rewrite `get_slot` to walk the chunked structure.\n8. Rewrite `slot_store_size` to acquire-load the atomic count.\n9. Add a test that forces multiple top-level growth events\n   (allocate ≥ 2048 slots to require at least one growth).\n10. Run the full slot-store unit suite and the integration\n    suite — all 22 + 12 must still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/009-slot-store.c` — the structure change.\n- `src/009-slot-store.h` — header stays unchanged (opaque type).\n- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — add growth test.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nRing buffer cell growth (when a single slot's ring fills with\npushed values waiting for consumption) — separate concern, same\ndouble-buffer pattern but under the per-slot lock. Tracked\nimplicitly under the slot store's roadmap; punt to a follow-on\nsub-issue.",

          "old_string":"## Status\nopen — planning stub. Full design in parent issue 319's \"Q1\"\nresolution.",
          "new_string":"## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Full design in parent issue\n319's \"Q1\" resolution.\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`src/009-slot-store.c` uses a flat `slot_rec_t **slots` array\nwith `realloc()`-based growth (`grow_store_if_needed`). This\nworks at graph load (single-threaded) but is unsafe at runtime\nbecause `realloc()` can MOVE the array, invalidating any slot\npointer a worker has cached.\n\nThe slot RECORDS themselves are already heap-allocated\nseparately (per-slot `malloc`), so their addresses are stable.\nOnly the `slots[]` array of POINTERS is the problem.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nReplace the flat `slots[]` array with a two-level chunked-append\nstructure:\n\n- **Chunk size**: 64 slot-pointers per chunk (cache-friendly).\n- **Top-level array**: holds chunk pointers; starts at 16\n  entries (1024 slots without top-level growth). Doubles via\n  copy-and-publish with defer-free when it fills.\n- **Atomic count**: tracks total slots ever allocated. Readers\n  use acquire-load to see slots published with release-store.\n- **`pthread_mutex_t alloc_lock`**: serializes `slot_alloc`.\n  Readers (push/pop via `get_slot`) take no lock here — the\n  per-slot spinlock is still the only hot-path synchronization.\n- **Stale-top free list**: top-level arrays from prior growth\n  events stay alive on a linked list until `slot_store_destroy`.\n  Any worker that cached a stale top-pointer mid-growth can\n  finish its lookup safely; the chunks the stale top points to\n  are still valid because chunks never move.\n\nSlot lookup: `top[id/64][id%64]`. One extra indirection per\naccess vs the old flat array, in exchange for the runtime-safe\ngrowth.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Change the `slot_store` struct definition (private in the\n   .c file; header has only the opaque forward declaration so\n   no public API change).\n2. Add `SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE` (64) and `INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY` (16).\n3. Rewrite `slot_store_create` to allocate the initial top-level\n   array, init the mutex, init the atomic count.\n4. Rewrite `slot_store_destroy` to iterate over chunks, free\n   slot records and each chunk, then free the stale-top list.\n5. Replace `grow_store_if_needed` with `grow_top_level` (called\n   under `alloc_lock`).\n6. Rewrite `slot_alloc`: take the lock, claim id, ensure chunk\n   exists, publish slot, release-store the count.\n7. Rewrite `get_slot` to walk the chunked structure.\n8. Rewrite `slot_store_size` to acquire-load the atomic count.\n9. Add a test that forces multiple top-level growth events\n   (allocate ≥ 2048 slots to require at least one growth).\n10. Run the full slot-store unit suite and the integration\n    suite — all 22 + 12 must still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/009-slot-store.c` — the structure change.\n- `src/009-slot-store.h` — header stays unchanged (opaque type).\n- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — add growth test.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nRing buffer cell growth (when a single slot's ring fills with\npushed values waiting for consumption) — separate concern, same\ndouble-buffer pattern but under the per-slot lock. Tracked\nimplicitly under the slot store's roadmap; punt to a follow-on\nsub-issue."
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01NcxgyWVFzwFSYgJ5b5dMqz",
        "type":"tool_use"
      }],

Owns the cell-array memory for every\n     * ring slot in this store, plus the payload bytes for every\n     * LARGE_VALUE cell. Created in slot_store_create; destroyed\n     * alongside the store. Any chunks still parked in cells at\n     * destroy time are reclaimed in bulk when the allocator's\n     * regions are freed. */\n    ua_t        *heap;\n};\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ Internal store — two-level chunked-append index (issue 319b)\n *\n * Slot pointers are looked up via top-level chunk pointer table:\n *\n *     slot N lives at chunks[N / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE][N % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE]\n *\n * Why two levels: a flat realloc'd array (the original design) moves\n * its base address on growth, invalidating any slot pointer a worker\n * has cached. The two-level shape lets the slot RECORDS themselves\n * stay at their original heap addresses forever (they always were —\n * each is a separate malloc) AND lets the index that maps id → record\n * grow without invalidating cached records.\n *\n * Growth happens in three layers, each rarer than the last:\n *   Layer 1 — append a slot pointer inside an existing chunk\n *             (every slot_alloc — the common case)\n *   Layer 2 — allocate a new chunk when crossing a chunk boundary\n *             (every SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE alloc — uncommon)\n *   Layer 3 — grow the top-level chunk-pointer array when it fills\n *             (logarithmic in total slot count — rare)\n *\n * Concurrency: slot_alloc is serialized by alloc_lock. The hot\n * read/write path (slot_push, slot_pop, slot_peek, slot_flags) takes\n * no allocator-wide lock — only the per-slot atomic_flag spinlock on\n * the slot itself. Readers acquire-load `count` to know how many\n * slots exist; the matching release-store at the end of slot_alloc\n * pairs with this so a reader seeing count = N also sees the slot N-1\n * record published.\n *\n * Layer 3 (top-level growth) uses copy-on-grow with defer-free: the\n * new top-level array is malloc'd at 2x size, the old chunk pointers\n * are memcpy'd in, the new top is atomically published, and the OLD\n * top is parked on the stale_tops list to be freed at destroy time.\n * A worker that loaded the old top pointer right before the swap can\n * finish its lookup against it — every chunk the old top points to\n * is still alive. */\n#define SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE      64u\n#define INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY 16u\n\nstruct stale_top {\n    slot_rec_t      ***ptr;\n    struct stale_top  *next;\n};\n\nstruct slot_store {\n    /* Top-level chunk-pointer table. Atomic because layer-3 growth\n     * publishes a new table while readers are still walking the old\n     * one. */\n    _Atomic(slot_rec_t ***) chunks;\n    _Atomic uint32_t        top_capacity;   /* in chunk-pointer slots */\n\n    /* Total slots ever allocated. Atomic; readers see released\n     * slot publications via the release-store at the end of\n     * slot_alloc. */\n    _Atomic uint32_t        count;\n\n    /* Serializes layer-2 chunk creation and layer-3 top growth.\n     * Readers don't take this — they walk the atomic structure. */\n    pthread_mutex_t         alloc_lock;\n\n    /* Defer-free list for stale top-level arrays. At most\n     * log2(final_top_capacity) entries — typically 0–3 over an\n     * entire run. Walked once at destroy. */\n    struct stale_top       *stale_tops;\n\n    /* The unified allocator. Owns the cell-array memory for every\n     * ring slot in this store, plus the payload bytes for every\n     * LARGE_VALUE cell. Created in slot_store_create; destroyed\n     * alongside the store. Any chunks still parked in cells at\n     * destroy time are reclaimed in bulk when the allocator's\n     * regions are freed. */\n    ua_t                   *heap;\n};\n/* }}} */"

      "content":"/* src/009-slot-store.c — per-input-port slot store, implementation.\n *\n * Three slot shapes coexist behind one set of APIs:\n *\n *   - Ring-buffer slots (peek and pop modes) — a header followed by\n *     n_cells cells laid out contiguously. Each cell is a 4-byte\n *     filled_size, optionally a 4-byte tag (for SLOT_FLAG_TAGGED),\n *     then cell_capacity bytes of payload. Untagged slots use the\n *     standard head/tail ring discipline; tagged slots use head/tail\n *     for the bookkeeping of \"where to put the next push\" but pop\n *     scans for the lowest-tag filled cell.\n *\n *   - Atomic-counter slots — no header bookkeeping, no payload cells;\n *     just one atomic_uint that slot_read_inc fetches-and-adds. No\n *     lock needed.\n *\n * Per-slot concurrency is a single atomic_flag spinlock for the\n * ring-buffer slots. Inside the lock the header and cells are mutated\n * without atomics; outside the lock no header bytes are touched.\n *\n * The store itself owns a flat array of slot pointers indexed by\n * slot_id_t. The array grows on demand. Ids are never reused — there\n * is no slot_free; slots live for the run.\n *\n * Variable-size payloads (SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE) used to point into a\n * monotonically-growing arena. That arena was a memory leak by design\n * — every push consumed bytes that were never reclaimed until run end.\n * The 2026-05-19 retraction in issue 302 commits to the unified\n * allocator (016) instead: every variable-size payload is a\n * reference-counted chunk, popped values release their reference, and\n * freed chunks rejoin the allocator's free-lists with eager\n * neighbor-merge. The cell layout is unchanged — the 8-byte payload\n * slot that used to hold a raw arena pointer now holds an opaque\n * chunk handle.\n *\n * Designed in issue 302. This file implements the API declared in\n * 009-slot-store.h. Free-list optimization for the fixed-size cell\n * arrays themselves is still deferred.\n */\n"

Chunks themselves are\n     * allocated lazily on first crossing of each chunk boundary. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = calloc((size_t)INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY,\n                               sizeof(slot_rec_t **));\n    if (!top) { free(s); return NULL; }\n\n    atomic_init(&s->chunks,       top);\n    atomic_init(&s->top_capacity, INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY);\n    atomic_init(&s->count,        0u);\n    pthread_mutex_init(&s->alloc_lock, NULL);\n    s->stale_tops = NULL;\n\n    /* Eagerly create the unified allocator.           "old_string":"/* {{{ slot_store_create() */\nslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);\n    if (!s) return NULL;\n    s->capacity = 16;\n    s->slots    = calloc((size_t)s->capacity, sizeof(slot_rec_t *));\n    if (!s->slots) { free(s); return NULL; }\n\n    /* Eagerly create the unified allocator. Earlier in this issue\n     * the allocator was lazy-created on the first LARGE_VALUE slot;\n     * since the cell arrays of ordinary ring slots also live in the\n     * allocator now, every slot allocation needs the allocator\n     * present from the start. No pre-warmed classes — they accrete\n     * on first use until the graph loader is wired to declare\n     * sizes up front. */\n    s->heap = ua_create(NULL, 0);\n    if (!s->heap) { free(s->slots); free(s); return NULL; }\n\n    return s;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_destroy() */\nvoid slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    if (!s) return;\n    /* Release each slot's cell-array chunk before tearing down the\n     * allocator. We don't strictly need to (ua_destroy frees all\n     * regions in bulk) but the unref'ed-then-destroyed path leaves\n     * the allocator's stats coherent if anything inspects them on\n     * the way out. The slot record itself was allocated via plain\n     * malloc and is freed here. */\n    for (int32_t i = 0; i < s->count; i++) {\n        slot_rec_t *r = s->slots[i];\n        if (!r) continue;\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n    }\n    free(s->slots);",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ slot_store_create() */\nslot_store_t *slot_store_create(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);\n    if (!s) return NULL;\n\n    /* Initial top-level chunk-pointer table. 16 entries means we\n     * can hold 16 * SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024 slots before any\n     * top-level growth fires; growth doubles thereafter and there\n     * is no upper ceiling (issue 319b). Chunks themselves are\n     * allocated lazily on first crossing of each chunk boundary. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = calloc((size_t)INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY,\n                               sizeof(slot_rec_t **));\n    if (!top) { free(s); return NULL; }\n\n    atomic_init(&s->chunks,       top);\n    atomic_init(&s->top_capacity, INITIAL_TOP_CAPACITY);\n    atomic_init(&s->count,        0u);\n    pthread_mutex_init(&s->alloc_lock, NULL);\n    s->stale_tops = NULL;\n\n    /* Eagerly create the unified allocator. Earlier in this issue\n     * the allocator was lazy-created on the first LARGE_VALUE slot;\n     * since the cell arrays of ordinary ring slots also live in the\n     * allocator now, every slot allocation needs the allocator\n     * present from the start. No pre-warmed classes — they accrete\n     * on first use until the graph loader is wired to declare\n     * sizes up front. */\n    s->heap = ua_create(NULL, 0);\n    if (!s->heap) {\n        free(top);\n        pthread_mutex_destroy(&s->alloc_lock);\n        free(s);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    return s;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ slot_store_destroy() */\nvoid slot_store_destroy(slot_store_t *s)\n{\n    if (!s) return;\n    /* Release each slot's cell-array chunk before tearing down the\n     * allocator. We don't strictly need to (ua_destroy frees all\n     * regions in bulk) but the unref'ed-then-destroyed path leaves\n     * the allocator's stats coherent if anything inspects them on\n     * the way out. The slot record itself was allocated via plain\n     * malloc and is freed here. */\n    uint32_t count   = atomic_load_explicit(&s->count,        memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t top_cap = atomic_load_explicit(&s->top_capacity, memory_order_relaxed);\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,      memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n        uint32_t ci = i / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n        uint32_t si = i % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n        if (ci >= top_cap || !top[ci]) continue;\n        slot_rec_t *r = top[ci][si];\n        if (!r) continue;\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n    }\n\n    /* Free each chunk (those that were ever allocated). */\n    for (uint32_t ci = 0; ci < top_cap; ci++) {\n        if (top[ci]) free(top[ci]);\n    }\n    free(top);\n\n    /* Free any stale top-level arrays that growth left behind.\n     * Their chunks were the same chunks the current top points to\n     * (we only copied the pointers in, didn't deep-copy), so\n     * they've already been freed above. Just drop the array\n     * memory. */\n    struct stale_top *st = s->stale_tops;\n    while (st) {\n        struct stale_top *next = st->next;\n        free(st->ptr);\n        free(st);\n        st = next;\n    }\n\n    pthread_mutex_destroy(&s->alloc_lock);"

          "old_string":"    if (grow_store_if_needed(s) != 0) {\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n        return SLOT_INVALID;\n    }\n    slot_id_t id = s->count++;\n    s->slots[id] = r;\n    return id;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — get_slot() */\nstatic slot_rec_t *get_slot(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    if (!s || id < 0 || id >= s->count) return NULL;\n    return s->slots[id];\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"    /* Publish into the two-level chunked index. The hot read path\n     * is lock-free; only this rare allocation path takes the lock,\n     * and only to serialize structural changes to the index\n     * (layer-2 chunk creation, layer-3 top growth, count bump).\n     * Workers' get_slot calls walk the atomic structure without\n     * contending here. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&s->alloc_lock);\n\n    uint32_t id = atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t ci = id / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    uint32_t si = id % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n\n    /* Layer 3: top-level grows if the chunk index is past current\n     * capacity. */\n    if (ci >= atomic_load_explicit(&s->top_capacity, memory_order_relaxed)) {\n        if (grow_top_level(s, ci) != 0) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n            if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n            if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n            if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n            free(r);\n            return SLOT_INVALID;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Layer 2: allocate the chunk if it's the first slot inside it. */\n    if (ensure_chunk(s, ci) != 0) {\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n        return SLOT_INVALID;\n    }\n\n    /* Layer 1: publish the slot pointer into the chunk. The count\n     * bump that follows is the release-store readers acquire-load\n     * to know the slot exists. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_relaxed);\n    top[ci][si] = r;\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&s->count, id + 1u, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n    return (slot_id_t)id;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — get_slot() */\nstatic slot_rec_t *get_slot(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    if (!s || id < 0) return NULL;\n    uint32_t uid = (uint32_t)id;\n    /* Acquire-load count pairs with the release-store in slot_alloc.\n     * If we see count = N then the slot at id = N-1 (and all earlier)\n     * is fully published — the chunk pointer and the slot pointer\n     * inside it. */\n    if (uid >= atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_acquire)) {\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    uint32_t ci = uid / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    uint32_t si = uid % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    /* Acquire-load the top so we see the chunk publishes that the\n     * release-store in grow_top_level orders before its top swap.\n     * After top growth, both the old and new top arrays point to\n     * the same chunks — either is safe to read from. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_acquire);\n    return top[ci][si];\n}\n/* }}} */"

The hot read path\n     * is lock-free; only this rare allocation path takes the lock,\n     * and only to serialize structural changes to the index\n     * (layer-2 chunk creation, layer-3 top growth, count bump).\n     * Workers' get_slot calls walk the atomic structure without\n     * contending here. */\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&s->alloc_lock);\n\n    uint32_t id = atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t ci = id / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    uint32_t si = id % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n\n    /* Layer 3: top-level grows if the chunk index is past current\n     * capacity. */\n    if (ci >= atomic_load_explicit(&s->top_capacity, memory_order_relaxed)) {\n        if (grow_top_level(s, ci) != 0) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n            if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n            if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n            if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n            free(r);\n            return SLOT_INVALID;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Layer 2: allocate the chunk if it's the first slot inside it. */\n    if (ensure_chunk(s, ci) != 0) {\n        pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n        if (r->cells_chunk)       ua_unref(s->heap, r->cells_chunk);\n        if (r->json_cells_chunk)  ua_unref(s->heap, r->json_cells_chunk);\n        if (r->order_cells_chunk) ua_unref(s->heap, r->order_cells_chunk);\n        free(r);\n        return SLOT_INVALID;\n    }\n\n    /* Layer 1: publish the slot pointer into the chunk. The count\n     * bump that follows is the release-store readers acquire-load\n     * to know the slot exists. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_relaxed);\n    top[ci][si] = r;\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&s->count, id + 1u, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&s->alloc_lock);\n    return (slot_id_t)id;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Local helper — get_slot() */\nstatic slot_rec_t *get_slot(slot_store_t *s, slot_id_t id)\n{\n    if (!s || id < 0) return NULL;\n    uint32_t uid = (uint32_t)id;\n    /* Acquire-load count pairs with the release-store in slot_alloc.\n     * If we see count = N then the slot at id = N-1 (and all earlier)\n     * is fully published — the chunk pointer and the slot pointer\n     * inside it. */\n    if (uid >= atomic_load_explicit(&s->count, memory_order_acquire)) {\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    uint32_t ci = uid / SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    uint32_t si = uid % SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE;\n    /* Acquire-load the top so we see the chunk publishes that the\n     * release-store in grow_top_level orders before its top swap.\n     * After top growth, both the old and new top arrays point to\n     * the same chunks — either is safe to read from. */\n    slot_rec_t ***top = atomic_load_explicit(&s->chunks,\n                                             memory_order_acquire);\n    return top[ci][si];\n}\n/* }}} */",

      "content":"/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_large_value_push_pop() */\n/* SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE accepts any size on push, regardless of\n * cell_capacity (which is ignored). Bytes live in the slot store's\n * lazy-created lvh heap; the cell holds a stable pointer. Peek\n * and pop both copy from the heap back into the caller buffer. */\nstatic int test_large_value_push_pop(void)\n{\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 0, 4, SLOT_FLAG_LARGE_VALUE);\n    ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n\n    /* 100 KB push — well beyond any sane fixed cell size. */\n    int payload_size = 100 * 1024;\n    unsigned char *src = malloc((size_t)payload_size);\n    for (int i = 0; i < payload_size; i++) src[i] = (unsigned char)(i & 0xFF);\n    ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, src, payload_size, 0) == 0);"
    },

  },

          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_chunked_index_growth_preserves_early_slots() — issue 319b\n *\n * Forces multiple top-level chunk-pointer-table growth events and\n * verifies that slots allocated BEFORE growth remain reachable AND\n * functional afterward. This is the load-bearing invariant of the\n * 319b two-level chunked-append index: slots and chunks never move,\n * so handles cached early in the run keep working forever.\n *\n * Initial top capacity is 16 * SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE (= 1024) slots. We\n * allocate 5000 slots, which forces at least two top-level growth\n * events (1024 → 2048 → 4096 → 8192). We push a sentinel into each\n * slot AT ALLOC TIME and read it back AFTER all allocations finish —\n * any growth-related corruption would scramble the sentinel. */\nstatic int test_chunked_index_growth_preserves_early_slots(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n\n    /* Each slot is a 1-cell ring of 4 bytes; we push the slot's id\n     * as its sentinel value. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id == i);\n        uint32_t v = (uint32_t)i;\n        ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, &v, sizeof v, 0) == 0);\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == N);\n\n    /* Read each slot's sentinel back. Slot 0 was allocated before\n     * any growth; if growth invalidated its pointer or moved its\n     * chunk, this peek would return garbage. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        uint32_t got = 0xDEADBEEF;\n        int32_t  rc  = slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)i, &got, sizeof got);\n        ASSERT(rc == (int32_t)sizeof got);\n        ASSERT(got == (uint32_t)i);\n    }\n\n    /* Out-of-range ids still rejected cleanly. */\n    uint32_t scratch = 0;\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)N,     &scratch, sizeof scratch) < 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)(N+1), &scratch, sizeof scratch) < 0);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */"
        },

    "newString":"/* {{{ test_store_size_growth() */\nstatic int test_store_size_growth(void)\n{\n    /* Allocate enough slots to cross the initial capacity boundary\n     * (16) and verify slot_id_t stays monotonic. */\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n    slot_id_t prev = -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id != SLOT_INVALID);\n        ASSERT(id == prev + 1);\n        prev = id;\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == 50);\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_chunked_index_growth_preserves_early_slots() — issue 319b\n *\n * Forces multiple top-level chunk-pointer-table growth events and\n * verifies that slots allocated BEFORE growth remain reachable AND\n * functional afterward. This is the load-bearing invariant of the\n * 319b two-level chunked-append index: slots and chunks never move,\n * so handles cached early in the run keep working forever.\n *\n * Initial top capacity is 16 * SLOT_CHUNK_SIZE (= 1024) slots. We\n * allocate 5000 slots, which forces at least two top-level growth\n * events (1024 → 2048 → 4096 → 8192). We push a sentinel into each\n * slot AT ALLOC TIME and read it back AFTER all allocations finish —\n * any growth-related corruption would scramble the sentinel. */\nstatic int test_chunked_index_growth_preserves_early_slots(void)\n{\n    enum { N = 5000 };\n    slot_store_t *s = slot_store_create();\n\n    /* Each slot is a 1-cell ring of 4 bytes; we push the slot's id\n     * as its sentinel value. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        slot_id_t id = slot_alloc(s, 4, 1, SLOT_FLAG_NONE);\n        ASSERT(id == i);\n        uint32_t v = (uint32_t)i;\n        ASSERT(slot_push(s, id, &v, sizeof v, 0) == 0);\n    }\n    ASSERT(slot_store_size(s) == N);\n\n    /* Read each slot's sentinel back. Slot 0 was allocated before\n     * any growth; if growth invalidated its pointer or moved its\n     * chunk, this peek would return garbage. */\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        uint32_t got = 0xDEADBEEF;\n        int32_t  rc  = slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)i, &got, sizeof got);\n        ASSERT(rc == (int32_t)sizeof got);\n        ASSERT(got == (uint32_t)i);\n    }\n\n    /* Out-of-range ids still rejected cleanly. */\n    uint32_t scratch = 0;\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)N,     &scratch, sizeof scratch) < 0);\n    ASSERT(slot_peek(s, (slot_id_t)(N+1), &scratch, sizeof scratch) < 0);\n\n    slot_store_destroy(s);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

    "originalFile":"# 319b — Slot store growth primitive\n\n## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Full design in parent issue\n319's \"Q1\" resolution.\n\n## Current behavior\n\n`src/009-slot-store.c` uses a flat `slot_rec_t **slots` array\nwith `realloc()`-based growth (`grow_store_if_needed`). This\nworks at graph load (single-threaded) but is unsafe at runtime\nbecause `realloc()` can MOVE the array, invalidating any slot\npointer a worker has cached.\n\nThe slot RECORDS themselves are already heap-allocated\nseparately (per-slot `malloc`), so their addresses are stable.\nOnly the `slots[]` array of POINTERS is the problem.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nReplace the flat `slots[]` array with a two-level chunked-append\nstructure:\n\n- **Chunk size**: 64 slot-pointers per chunk (cache-friendly).\n- **Top-level array**: holds chunk pointers; starts at 16\n  entries (1024 slots without top-level growth). Doubles via\n  copy-and-publish with defer-free when it fills.\n- **Atomic count**: tracks total slots ever allocated. Readers\n  use acquire-load to see slots published with release-store.\n- **`pthread_mutex_t alloc_lock`**: serializes `slot_alloc`.\n  Readers (push/pop via `get_slot`) take no lock here — the\n  per-slot spinlock is still the only hot-path synchronization.\n- **Stale-top free list**: top-level arrays from prior growth\n  events stay alive on a linked list until `slot_store_destroy`.\n  Any worker that cached a stale top-pointer mid-growth can\n  finish its lookup safely; the chunks the stale top points to\n  are still valid because chunks never move.\n\nSlot lookup: `top[id/64][id%64]`. One extra indirection per\naccess vs the old flat array, in exchange for the runtime-safe\ngrowth.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Rewrite `slot_store_destroy` to iterate over chunks, free\n   slot records and each chunk, then free the stale-top list.\n5. Replace `grow_store_if_needed` with `grow_top_level` (called\n   under `alloc_lock`).\n6. Rewrite `slot_alloc`: take the lock, claim id, ensure chunk\n   exists, publish slot, release-store the count.\n7. Rewrite `get_slot` to walk the chunked structure.\n8. Rewrite `slot_store_size` to acquire-load the atomic count.\n9. Add a test that forces multiple top-level growth events\n   (allocate ≥ 2048 slots to require at least one growth).\n10. Run the full slot-store unit suite and the integration\n    suite — all 22 + 12 must still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/009-slot-store.c` — the structure change.\n- `src/009-slot-store.h` — header stays unchanged (opaque type).\n- `tests/009-slot-store-test.c` — add growth test.\n\n## Not in scope\n\nRing buffer cell growth (when a single slot's ring fills with\npushed values waiting for consumption) — separate concern, same\ndouble-buffer pattern but under the per-slot lock. The header explicitly\nstates: \"Lifetime is the run. Slots are freed when the store is\ndestroyed at the end of the run.\"\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe slot store grows at runtime via a three-layer chunked-append\n+ RCU-swap structure (see 319's Q1 resolution for the full\ndiagram and rationale). Slots themselves never move; chunks\nthemselves never move; only the top-level index array swaps when\nit fills, and the swap uses double-buffer-with-defer-free.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nTo be expanded when this sub-issue is picked up.           "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n319b — closeout: the slot store grows without moving its slots\n\nThe slot pointer index is now a two-level chunked-append table.\nSlots live at chunks[id/64][id%64]; both the chunk pointer in\nthe top-level table and the slot pointer inside the chunk are\npublished atomically by slot_alloc, and any slot a worker has\ncached keeps its address forever — chunks never move, slot\nrecords never move, only the top-level table itself ever moves\nand only via copy-then-atomic-swap with the prior version parked\non a defer-free list so in-flight readers finish safely.\n\nWhy the change: the old flat realloc'd index let the slot\npointers move on growth, which is fine when growth only happens\nat graph load but breaks the moment slot_alloc fires from a\nrunning worker. The runtime self-construction feature (issue\n319's create_box, sub-issue 319d) needs that to work; this\nlanding is the foundation that makes the rest of 319 safe.\n\nHot read path unchanged: slot_push / slot_pop / slot_peek take\nno allocator-wide lock. The per-slot atomic_flag spinlock\nremains the only serialization on value movement. A\npthread_mutex serializes slot_alloc itself, which is rare and\nalready off the critical path.\n\nThe 5000-slot growth test forces multiple top-level grow events\n(1024 → 2048 → 4096 → 8192) and verifies every slot allocated\nbefore any growth event remains readable with its original\nsentinel value intact afterward. The full slot-store unit\nsuite is now 23 passing (up from 22); the 12 integration test\nmaps all still pass.\n\nNo public API change — slot_store_t is opaque in the header.\nThe new internal layer is invisible to every caller.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5"
        },

    "newString":"## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Scope reduced from the original\nplan (see \"Reduced scope\" below). Design in parent issue 319's\n\"Q4\" resolution.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Provides the box id generator that\n`create_box` (319d) returns when the caller doesn't supply an\nexplicit `id`.\n\n## Reduced scope — compile cache not needed as a separate module\n\nIssue 319's Q5 resolution called for a content-hash-keyed\ncompile cache under `tmp/` that shells out to\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on miss. Investigation while\nstarting this sub-issue found that **the language specs already\ndo this work internally**:\n\n- `langs/c/spec.c` has `maybe_lazy_compile` (line 228) that\n  detects a `.c` source path, compiles it to `.so` on first\n  use, and caches the resulting handle in the per-worker dlopen\n  table.\n- Lua and Bash have no compile step — `langs/lua/spec.c` loads\n  via `luaL_loadfile` and caches the Lua module; Bash's spec\n  hands the source path to a persistent subprocess.\n\nSo `create_box(spec)` for any language can resolve via the\nexisting per-spec invocation path. No separate cache layer\npreserves more concept-purity than it saves work — the runner\nalready stays ignorant of the compiler because each language\nspec encapsulates its own loading discipline. The Q5\n\"compile cache\" idea is therefore folded into existing spec\nmachinery rather than implemented as a new module.\n\nIf a future need surfaces for a unified content-hash cache\nabove the spec layer (e.g. for pre-warming or shared\nartifacts across workers), revisit; for now, defer.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThere is no box id generator. The graph loader currently expects\nevery box's `id` field to be supplied by the caller (from JSON\non disk). `create_box` callers (issue 319d) need a way to\nproduce unique ids when they don't want to name a box themselves.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA small utility module that exposes one function:\n\n```c\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size);\n```\n\nFills `buf` with a string of the form `auto_<8 hex chars>` (a\nprocess-wide atomic counter rendered as hex). Returns 0 on\nsuccess, -1 if `buf_size` is insufficient (the required size\nis 14 bytes: 5 prefix chars + 8 hex chars + null terminator).\n\nUniqueness is guaranteed within a single process run via the\natomic counter. Cross-run uniqueness is not a goal — ids are\nruntime-only constructs; persistent ids come from the on-disk\nbox JSON files.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Create `src/017-box-id.h` — declaration of `box_id_generate`.\n2. Create `src/017-box-id.c` — atomic counter + snprintf\n   formatting.\n3. Create `src/017-box-id.info.md` — function listing per the\n   project's documentation convention.\n4. Create `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — verify format, uniqueness\n   across many calls, rejection on too-small buffer, and\n   uniqueness under concurrent access from multiple threads.\n5. Add Makefile dependency line for the new test.\n6. Initialize `file-index-counter` at 17.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/017-box-id.{h,c}` — new module.\n- `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — new test.\n- `Makefile` — add per-test dependency line.",
    "originalFile":"# 319c — Box id generator and compile cache\n\n## Status\nopen — planning stub. Full design in parent issue 319's \"Q4\" and\n\"Q5\" resolutions.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Combines two small independent utilities that\nboth gate `create_box`:\n\n- **Box id generator** — auto-generates UUID-style box_id strings\n  for `create_box` callers who don't supply an explicit `id`.\n  Design: 319 Q4.\n- **Compile cache** — content-hash-keyed lookup under `tmp/`,\n  shell-out to `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on cache miss,\n  dlopen the resulting artifact. Preserves the runner-doesn't-know-\n  about-compiler separation. Design: 319 Q5.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n- A `box_id_generate()` utility returns a string like\n  `auto_8f3c2a1e9b4d`. Collision-free within a run.\n- A `compile_cache_resolve(source_path, lang_spec)` utility\n  returns a dlopen-ready artifact path. Cache hit returns\n  immediately; cache miss invokes the compile script and waits.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nTo be expanded when picked up. Both utilities are independent of\nthe slot store work and can land before 319b if convenient.\n",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false,

    "oldString":"## Status\nopen — planning stub. Full design in parent issue 319's \"Q4\" and\n\"Q5\" resolutions.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Combines two small independent utilities that\nboth gate `create_box`:\n\n- **Box id generator** — auto-generates UUID-style box_id strings\n  for `create_box` callers who don't supply an explicit `id`.\n  Design: 319 Q4.\n- **Compile cache** — content-hash-keyed lookup under `tmp/`,\n  shell-out to `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on cache miss,\n  dlopen the resulting artifact. Preserves the runner-doesn't-know-\n  about-compiler separation. Design: 319 Q5.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n- A `box_id_generate()` utility returns a string like\n  `auto_8f3c2a1e9b4d`. Collision-free within a run.\n- A `compile_cache_resolve(source_path, lang_spec)` utility\n  returns a dlopen-ready artifact path. Cache hit returns\n  immediately; cache miss invokes the compile script and waits.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nTo be expanded when picked up. Both utilities are independent of\nthe slot store work and can land before 319b if convenient."

          "old_string":"## Status\nopen — planning stub. Full design in parent issue 319's \"Q4\" and\n\"Q5\" resolutions.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Combines two small independent utilities that\nboth gate `create_box`:\n\n- **Box id generator** — auto-generates UUID-style box_id strings\n  for `create_box` callers who don't supply an explicit `id`.\n  Design: 319 Q4.\n- **Compile cache** — content-hash-keyed lookup under `tmp/`,\n  shell-out to `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on cache miss,\n  dlopen the resulting artifact. Preserves the runner-doesn't-know-\n  about-compiler separation. Design: 319 Q5.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n- A `box_id_generate()` utility returns a string like\n  `auto_8f3c2a1e9b4d`. Collision-free within a run.\n- A `compile_cache_resolve(source_path, lang_spec)` utility\n  returns a dlopen-ready artifact path. Cache hit returns\n  immediately; cache miss invokes the compile script and waits.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nTo be expanded when picked up. Both utilities are independent of\nthe slot store work and can land before 319b if convenient.",
          "new_string":"## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Scope reduced from the original\nplan (see \"Reduced scope\" below). Design in parent issue 319's\n\"Q4\" resolution.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Provides the box id generator that\n`create_box` (319d) returns when the caller doesn't supply an\nexplicit `id`.\n\n## Reduced scope — compile cache not needed as a separate module\n\nIssue 319's Q5 resolution called for a content-hash-keyed\ncompile cache under `tmp/` that shells out to\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on miss. Investigation while\nstarting this sub-issue found that **the language specs already\ndo this work internally**:\n\n- `langs/c/spec.c` has `maybe_lazy_compile` (line 228) that\n  detects a `.c` source path, compiles it to `.so` on first\n  use, and caches the resulting handle in the per-worker dlopen\n  table.\n- Lua and Bash have no compile step — `langs/lua/spec.c` loads\n  via `luaL_loadfile` and caches the Lua module; Bash's spec\n  hands the source path to a persistent subprocess.\n\nSo `create_box(spec)` for any language can resolve via the\nexisting per-spec invocation path. No separate cache layer\npreserves more concept-purity than it saves work — the runner\nalready stays ignorant of the compiler because each language\nspec encapsulates its own loading discipline. The Q5\n\"compile cache\" idea is therefore folded into existing spec\nmachinery rather than implemented as a new module.\n\nIf a future need surfaces for a unified content-hash cache\nabove the spec layer (e.g. for pre-warming or shared\nartifacts across workers), revisit; for now, defer.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThere is no box id generator. The graph loader currently expects\nevery box's `id` field to be supplied by the caller (from JSON\non disk). `create_box` callers (issue 319d) need a way to\nproduce unique ids when they don't want to name a box themselves.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA small utility module that exposes one function:\n\n```c\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size);\n```\n\nFills `buf` with a string of the form `auto_<8 hex chars>` (a\nprocess-wide atomic counter rendered as hex). Returns 0 on\nsuccess, -1 if `buf_size` is insufficient (the required size\nis 14 bytes: 5 prefix chars + 8 hex chars + null terminator).\n\nUniqueness is guaranteed within a single process run via the\natomic counter. Cross-run uniqueness is not a goal — ids are\nruntime-only constructs; persistent ids come from the on-disk\nbox JSON files.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Create `src/017-box-id.h` — declaration of `box_id_generate`.\n2. Create `src/017-box-id.c` — atomic counter + snprintf\n   formatting.\n3. Create `src/017-box-id.info.md` — function listing per the\n   project's documentation convention.\n4. Create `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — verify format, uniqueness\n   across many calls, rejection on too-small buffer, and\n   uniqueness under concurrent access from multiple threads.\n5. Add Makefile dependency line for the new test.\n6. Initialize `file-index-counter` at 17.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/017-box-id.{h,c}` — new module.\n- `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — new test.\n- `Makefile` — add per-test dependency line."
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },

    "content":[{
        "name":"Write",
        "input":{
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/017-box-id.h",
          "content":"/* src/017-box-id.h — auto-generated box id strings, public API.\n *\n * What it does, in one sentence: hands out unique short string\n * identifiers of the form \"auto_<8 hex chars>\", suitable for use as\n * the `id` field of a runtime-created box.\n *\n * Designed in issue 319 (Q4 resolution); landed in issue 319c.\n *\n * Why a string and not an opaque handle: the rest of SoraMech\n * already identifies boxes by `id` string everywhere (box JSON\n * filenames, connection entries, dispatch log lines, the\n * `last-run.jsonl` event stream). Returning a string keeps\n * runtime-created boxes interchangeable with on-disk-defined ones.\n * No special \"handle\" type needs to cross language boundaries via\n * the JSON wire format.\n *\n * Uniqueness is process-wide: a single atomic counter feeds the\n * hex suffix, so no two calls within one process run return the\n * same string.           "content":"/* src/017-box-id.c — auto-generated box id strings, implementation.\n *\n * The whole story: one atomic uint32 counter, fetch-add it, format\n * the result as \"auto_%08x\". 4 billion ids per process run is more\n * than any reasonable workload needs; if a run somehow burns through\n * that many runtime-created boxes the counter wraps and we'd start\n * seeing collisions — but at that point the wrap is the smallest\n * problem the run has.\n *\n * Designed in issue 319 (Q4); landed in issue 319c.\n */\n#include \"017-box-id.h\"\n\n#include <stdatomic.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n\n/* {{{ box_id_counter — process-wide unique-id source */\n/* Starts at 0; first id minted is \"auto_00000000\". The counter is\n * intentionally zero-initialized rather than seeded from time(NULL)\n * or any other entropy source: same-shape ids across runs are\n * easier to grep for in transcripts and last-run.jsonl, and we\n * don't need cross-run uniqueness here. */\nstatic _Atomic uint32_t box_id_counter = 0;\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ box_id_generate() */\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size)\n{\n    if (!buf || buf_size < BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) return -1;\n\n    /* relaxed memory order: the counter has no synchronization\n     * relationship with any other memory; only its own atomicity\n     * matters. */\n    uint32_t id = atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&box_id_counter, 1u,\n                                            memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    int n = snprintf(buf, buf_size, \"auto_%08x\", (unsigned)id);\n    /* snprintf returns the number it would have written if the\n     * buffer were unlimited; n == 13 is success at buf_size >= 14. */\n    if (n < 0 || (size_t)n + 1u > buf_size) return -1;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n"

          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/tests/017-box-id-test.c",
          "content":"/* tests/017-box-id-test.c — unit tests for src/017-box-id.\n *\n * Covers: output format, monotonic uniqueness in single-threaded\n * use, rejection on undersized buffer, and concurrent uniqueness\n * across multiple threads.\n */\n#include \"017-box-id.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Tiny test harness */\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\nstatic int tests_run = 0, tests_passed = 0;\n\n#define RUN(name) do { \\\n    tests_run++; \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s \", #name); \\\n    fflush(stdout); \\\n    if (test_##name()) { \\\n        printf(\"ok\\n\"); \\\n        tests_passed++; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_format() — output matches \"auto_XXXXXXXX\" */\nstatic int test_format(void)\n{\n    char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(buf, sizeof buf) == 0);\n    ASSERT(strlen(buf) == 13);\n    ASSERT(strncmp(buf, \"auto_\", 5) == 0);\n    /* Suffix is 8 chars of [0-9a-f]. */\n    for (int i = 5; i < 13; i++) {\n        char c = buf[i];\n        int hex = (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f');\n        ASSERT(hex);\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_monotonic_uniqueness() — successive calls produce\n *                                   distinct strings */\nstatic int test_monotonic_uniqueness(void)\n{\n    char a[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE], b[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(a, sizeof a) == 0);\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(b, sizeof b) == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(a, b) != 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_buf_too_small() — rejected with -1, no write */\nstatic int test_buf_too_small(void)\n{\n    char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE - 1] = \"preserve\";\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(buf, sizeof buf) == -1);\n    /* The function should not have written anything; the leading\n     * \"preserve\" bytes remain. */\n    ASSERT(strncmp(buf, \"preserve\", 8) == 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_buf() — rejected with -1 */\nstatic int test_null_buf(void)\n{\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(NULL, BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) == -1);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_uniqueness() — many threads, all ids unique\n *\n * Spawns 8 worker threads, each generates IDS_PER_THREAD ids and\n * stashes them in a per-thread array. Main thread collects them,\n * sorts, and verifies no duplicates. If the atomic counter had\n * been a plain int with a race window, this would surface\n * collisions on contended runs. */\nenum { N_THREADS = 8, IDS_PER_THREAD = 1024 };\n\nstruct gen_ctx {\n    char ids[IDS_PER_THREAD][BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n};\n\nstatic void *gen_worker(void *arg)\n{\n    struct gen_ctx *ctx = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < IDS_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n        if (box_id_generate(ctx->ids[i], BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) != 0) {\n            /* Shouldn't happen — flag with empty string for the\n             * checker. */\n            ctx->ids[i][0] = '\\0';\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int cmp_strings(const void *a, const void *b)\n{\n    return strcmp((const char *)a, (const char *)b);\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_uniqueness(void)\n{\n    pthread_t       threads[N_THREADS];\n    struct gen_ctx *ctxs = calloc(N_THREADS, sizeof *ctxs);\n    ASSERT(ctxs != NULL);\n\n    for (int t = 0;     "content":"/* tests/017-box-id-test.c — unit tests for src/017-box-id.\n *\n * Covers: output format, monotonic uniqueness in single-threaded\n * use, rejection on undersized buffer, and concurrent uniqueness\n * across multiple threads.\n */\n#include \"017-box-id.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Tiny test harness */\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\nstatic int tests_run = 0, tests_passed = 0;\n\n#define RUN(name) do { \\\n    tests_run++; \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s \", #name); \\\n    fflush(stdout); \\\n    if (test_##name()) { \\\n        printf(\"ok\\n\"); \\\n        tests_passed++; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_format() — output matches \"auto_XXXXXXXX\" */\nstatic int test_format(void)\n{\n    char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(buf, sizeof buf) == 0);\n    ASSERT(strlen(buf) == 13);\n    ASSERT(strncmp(buf, \"auto_\", 5) == 0);\n    /* Suffix is 8 chars of [0-9a-f]. */\n    for (int i = 5; i < 13; i++) {\n        char c = buf[i];\n        int hex = (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f');\n        ASSERT(hex);\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_monotonic_uniqueness() — successive calls produce\n *                                   distinct strings */\nstatic int test_monotonic_uniqueness(void)\n{\n    char a[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE], b[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(a, sizeof a) == 0);\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(b, sizeof b) == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(a, b) != 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_buf_too_small() — rejected with -1, no write */\nstatic int test_buf_too_small(void)\n{\n    char buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE - 1] = \"preserve\";\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(buf, sizeof buf) == -1);\n    /* The function should not have written anything; the leading\n     * \"preserve\" bytes remain. */\n    ASSERT(strncmp(buf, \"preserve\", 8) == 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_null_buf() — rejected with -1 */\nstatic int test_null_buf(void)\n{\n    ASSERT(box_id_generate(NULL, BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) == -1);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ test_concurrent_uniqueness() — many threads, all ids unique\n *\n * Spawns 8 worker threads, each generates IDS_PER_THREAD ids and\n * stashes them in a per-thread array. Main thread collects them,\n * sorts, and verifies no duplicates. If the atomic counter had\n * been a plain int with a race window, this would surface\n * collisions on contended runs. */\nenum { N_THREADS = 8, IDS_PER_THREAD = 1024 };\n\nstruct gen_ctx {\n    char ids[IDS_PER_THREAD][BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n};\n\nstatic void *gen_worker(void *arg)\n{\n    struct gen_ctx *ctx = arg;\n    for (int i = 0; i < IDS_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n        if (box_id_generate(ctx->ids[i], BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) != 0) {\n            /* Shouldn't happen — flag with empty string for the\n             * checker. */\n            ctx->ids[i][0] = '\\0';\n        }\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic int cmp_strings(const void *a, const void *b)\n{\n    return strcmp((const char *)a, (const char *)b);\n}\n\nstatic int test_concurrent_uniqueness(void)\n{\n    pthread_t       threads[N_THREADS];\n    struct gen_ctx *ctxs = calloc(N_THREADS, sizeof *ctxs);\n    ASSERT(ctxs != NULL);\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        pthread_create(&threads[t], NULL, gen_worker, &ctxs[t]);\n    }\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        pthread_join(threads[t], NULL);\n    }\n\n    /* Pack all ids into one flat array for sort-and-check. */\n    int total = N_THREADS * IDS_PER_THREAD;\n    char (*flat)[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE] = malloc((size_t)total * BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE);\n    ASSERT(flat != NULL);\n    int k = 0;\n    for (int t = 0; t < N_THREADS; t++) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < IDS_PER_THREAD; i++) {\n            ASSERT(ctxs[t].ids[i][0] != '\\0');\n            memcpy(flat[k++], ctxs[t].ids[i], BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE);\n        }\n    }\n    qsort(flat, (size_t)total, BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE, cmp_strings);\n    for (int i = 1; i < total; i++) {\n        ASSERT(strcmp(flat[i - 1], flat[i]) != 0);\n    }\n\n    free(flat);\n    free(ctxs);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"017-box-id-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(format);\n    RUN(monotonic_uniqueness);\n    RUN(buf_too_small);\n    RUN(null_buf);\n    RUN(concurrent_uniqueness);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\",\n           tests_passed, tests_run - tests_passed);\n    return tests_run == tests_passed ? 0 : 1;\n}\n"

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines.     "originalFile":"# 319c — Box id generator and compile cache\n\n## Status\nopen — implementation underway. Scope reduced from the original\nplan (see \"Reduced scope\" below). Design in parent issue 319's\n\"Q4\" resolution.\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Provides the box id generator that\n`create_box` (319d) returns when the caller doesn't supply an\nexplicit `id`.\n\n## Reduced scope — compile cache not needed as a separate module\n\nIssue 319's Q5 resolution called for a content-hash-keyed\ncompile cache under `tmp/` that shells out to\n`scripts/soramech-compile.sh` on miss. Investigation while\nstarting this sub-issue found that **the language specs already\ndo this work internally**:\n\n- `langs/c/spec.c` has `maybe_lazy_compile` (line 228) that\n  detects a `.c` source path, compiles it to `.so` on first\n  use, and caches the resulting handle in the per-worker dlopen\n  table.\n- Lua and Bash have no compile step — `langs/lua/spec.c` loads\n  via `luaL_loadfile` and caches the Lua module; Bash's spec\n  hands the source path to a persistent subprocess.\n\nSo `create_box(spec)` for any language can resolve via the\nexisting per-spec invocation path. No separate cache layer\npreserves more concept-purity than it saves work — the runner\nalready stays ignorant of the compiler because each language\nspec encapsulates its own loading discipline. The Q5\n\"compile cache\" idea is therefore folded into existing spec\nmachinery rather than implemented as a new module.\n\nIf a future need surfaces for a unified content-hash cache\nabove the spec layer (e.g. for pre-warming or shared\nartifacts across workers), revisit; for now, defer.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThere is no box id generator. The graph loader currently expects\nevery box's `id` field to be supplied by the caller (from JSON\non disk). `create_box` callers (issue 319d) need a way to\nproduce unique ids when they don't want to name a box themselves.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA small utility module that exposes one function:\n\n```c\nint box_id_generate(char *buf, size_t buf_size);\n```\n\nFills `buf` with a string of the form `auto_<8 hex chars>` (a\nprocess-wide atomic counter rendered as hex). Returns 0 on\nsuccess, -1 if `buf_size` is insufficient (the required size\nis 14 bytes: 5 prefix chars + 8 hex chars + null terminator).\n\nUniqueness is guaranteed within a single process run via the\natomic counter. Cross-run uniqueness is not a goal — ids are\nruntime-only constructs; persistent ids come from the on-disk\nbox JSON files.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\n1. Create `src/017-box-id.h` — declaration of `box_id_generate`.\n2. Create `src/017-box-id.c` — atomic counter + snprintf\n   formatting.\n3. Create `src/017-box-id.info.md` — function listing per the\n   project's documentation convention.\n4. Create `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — verify format, uniqueness\n   across many calls, rejection on too-small buffer, and\n   uniqueness under concurrent access from multiple threads.\n5. Add Makefile dependency line for the new test.\n6. Initialize `file-index-counter` at 17.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/017-box-id.{h,c}` — new module.\n- `tests/017-box-id-test.c` — new test.\n- `Makefile` — add per-test dependency line.\n",
