    "originalFile":"# Phase 3 Progress\n\nGoal: replace the Lua synchronous runner with a C thread pool runner\nthat executes box graphs in parallel.\n\nThe phase is fully designed; implementation is now underway.\nIssues 301–313 are the architectural specification. As each issue\nmoves into implementation, its row is marked \"in progress\"; on\ncompletion it's moved to `issues/completed/`.\n\nImplementation began **2026-05-12** with the 309 build scaffolding.\n\n## Issues\n\n| ID  | Title                                                       | Status   |\n|-----|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------|\n| 301 | thread pool lifecycle and per-worker initialization         | complete · pool + per-worker init/teardown hooks + priority queue |\n| 302 | per-task slot store with wire-held references               | complete · unified allocator + refcounted recycling on every byte path (slot cells, variable-size payloads, dispatch input/output buffers) + eager neighbor-merge + quiescence-trigger deep sweep |\n| 303 | language runtime spec (pluggable per-language invocation)   | complete · registry + per-worker init + pool hook + lang filtering |\n| 304 | task dispatch layer (C, replaces synchronous executor)      | complete · every routing kind, slab-allocated task structs, live_wire_count placeholder; attempt-task rewrite reconsidered |\n| 305 | C graph loader (replaces `003-loader.lua`)                  | complete · all seven phases + entry-box set + size classes + all six routing kinds |\n| 306 | Lua language spec implementation                            | complete · init + invoke + teardown + per-worker module cache + per-edge native/JSON in & out |\n| 307 | C language spec implementation                              | complete · compile + lazy .c→.so + invoke + per-worker dlopen cache + JSON in/out (string-wrap + primitive-passthrough); typed-wrapper generator deferred to future enhancement |\n| 308 | Bash language spec implementation                           | complete · persistent socketpair + line-protocol invoke + dladdr-based server lookup |\n| 309 | build system & Makefile orchestration                       | complete · scaffolding + spec discovery + soramech-compile portable artifact |\n| 310 | priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally                | complete · API + ordering done |\n| 311 | integration tests & run output (`last-run.jsonl`)           | in progress · writer + queue + thread + LOG_VALUES + LOG_SLOTS + run-tests.sh + compile-pipeline check |\n| 312 | same-language wire fast path (skip JSON for Lua→Lua etc.)   | complete · dual-ring slots + per-edge classification + per-cell ordering; spec contract has single invoke + two bridges; Lua native-bytes optimisation tracked as a future slice |\n| 313 | research: whole-program same-language merge                 | research / blocked |\n| 314 | small C JSON parser written for this project                | complete · parser + writer + strict leading-zero |\n| 315 | reference-counted compiled-map artifacts                    | open · design only |\n| 316 | simple test-runner script                                   | folded into 232 |\n| 317 | language spec JSON bridge for data boxes                    | complete · Lua fidelity-preserving, C+Bash pass-through-or-string-wrap, shared test harness |\n| 319 | built-in library for map self-construction (`create_box`, `connect`) | open · design complete; sub-issues 319a–e |\n| 319a | dispatch input cap removal (VLA + named constant)           | complete · 20-input fixture passes end-to-end |\n| 319b | slot store growth (two-level chunked-append index)          | complete · 5000-slot growth test preserves all early pointers |\n\n## Phase goal checklist\n\n- [x] SoraMech-owned task pool builds clean (3d-rts as design reference)\n- [x] Slot store unit-tested (single-value + ring buffer)\n- [x] C graph loader passes the project's existing maps\n- [x] Lua spec runs `tests/maps/hello` end-to-end\n- [x] C spec compiles and runs a fixed-signature box\n- [x] Bash spec runs an out-of-process box via persistent\n      socketpair + line-protocol\n- [x] Pool runner runs a multi-language map with concurrent workers\n- [x] Iterator box routes via dispatch layer (with multi-spawn\n      re-fire via N-cell pop slots and auto-re-spawn)\n- [x] Comparator box routes via dispatch layer (via spec output)\n- [x] Variable-size outputs work via the large-value heap\n- [x] `last-run.jsonl` written for every run\n- [ ] All 11 integration test maps pass\n- [ ] Phase 3 demo map runs and produces expected output\n- [ ] Phase 2 synchronous runner retired (`src/004-executor.lua`,\n      `src/007-runner-main.lua`, `src/003-loader.lua`, `drivers/*.sh`)\n\n## Implementation order suggestion\n\nDesigned to surface concrete artifacts early so subsequent issues can\nbuild on them.\n\n1. **309 (build system)** — top-level Makefile, vendored deps, empty\n   stubs for runner and specs.     "type":"message",
    "id":"msg_01MviCKNdfb9RoyzTAqecTax",
    "content":[{
        "text":"Stepping back before implementation — 319d as fully specified is genuinely a multi-session feature. Three problems converge:\n\n1. **Graph box array** — `box_t *boxes` is a flat realloc'd array; growing it at runtime would invalidate pointers cached by workers.\n2. **Per-box `connections[]` array** — dispatch walks these on the hot push path; growing them concurrently with a fire would race.\n3. **Box record** has ~25 fields that need to be populated correctly for a new box to participate in dispatch.\n\nThe first two are the **same lock-free-growth problem we solved in 319b**, applied to two more structures. The third is a substantial JSON-to-struct marshalling job.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nThe dispatcher's existing event-driven design is actually a gift here — if a new box's connections wire into a producer correctly and the new box has slots allocated, dispatch picks it up automatically via the existing spawn-on-input-ready check. The hard work is making the mutation safe; the dispatch side needs zero changes.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n## Three ways to slice this\n\n**(A) Full 319d in one session.** Aggressive. Likely to ship buggy or incomplete. Not recommended.\n\n**(B) Slice into 319d-foundation + 319d-api.** Foundation does the chunked-append work for boxes + connections (no user-facing change, identical behavior). Next session does the C API + Lua bindings + end-to-end test. Cleanest separation; foundation is meaningfully testable on its own.\n\n**(C) Minimum-concurrency version.** Implement `create_box`/`connect` with simple `realloc` + mutex, **document the restriction \"callers must ensure pool quiescence,\"** and get end-to-end working. Concurrent-safe runtime mutation becomes a follow-up. This ships the API shape and lets us test it; the hard race-safety work is deferred until someone actually needs to call it from a hot dispatcher.\n\n**My recommendation: (C).** Reasons:\n- The use case you described (\"planner box decides what sub-pipeline to build at runtime\") is the eventual goal but isn't on the critical path for anything else. Encapsulated maps (248) and the editor work can land independently.\n- Documented restrictions are a normal stepping stone in C; many real systems start this way (early Python, early Rust async).\n- (B)'s foundation slice has zero observable behavior — it's pure machinery that could rot before being used. (C) at least produces a working `create_box` that can be exercised by an end-to-end test.\n- When the concurrent need actually shows up, the lock-free upgrade is a focused change with clear motivation, not speculative infrastructure.\n\nThe 319d issue file (when it gets its update) would note: \"Phase 1 (this commit): single-threaded mutation, mutex-protected. Phase 2 (follow-on): lock-free hot-path-safe mutation when first concurrent use case arrives.\"\n\nWhich slice do you want? **(B), (C), or do you actually want (A) and accept the risk?**",
        "type":"text"
      }],
    "stop_reason":"end_turn",
    "model":"claude-opus-4-7"
  },

{
  "gitBranch":"master",
  "message":{
    "content":"  1. Graph box array — box_t *boxes is a flat realloc'd array; growing it at runtime would invalidate pointers cached by workers.\n\nwe're using the double-table redirection pattern, remember?\n\n  2. Per-box connections[] array — dispatch walks these on the hot push path; growing them concurrently with a fire would race.\n\nso make access to them atomic. We're going to do an audit of all the atomic accesses later on, and when we do so we'll identify areas that we can increase performance by skipping it. We just want to get the product into user's hands so they can tell us where it feels slow.\n\n  3. Box record has ~25 fields that need to be populated correctly for a new box to participate in dispatch.\n\nand, what are those fields? that feels like a lot to me.\n\n  (A) Full 319d in one session.           "new_string":"/* {{{ Graph struct\n *\n * Box storage uses pointers-to-records so box addresses stay stable\n * across runtime growth (issue 319d). Each box_t is its own malloc;\n * `boxes` is an array of pointers indexed by box id. Growing the\n * pointer array uses copy-and-publish — allocate a new bigger\n * pointer array, memcpy the old pointers in, atomic-store the new\n * array, and stash the old array on stale_box_arrs so any in-flight\n * reader walking the old array completes safely.\n *\n * The hot read path (graph_box, graph_n_boxes) atomic-loads the\n * boxes pointer and n_boxes count; no mutex held. Mutations\n * (graph_add_box for runtime additions, graph_load for initial\n * population) take graph_mu.\n */\nstruct stale_arr {\n    void              *ptr;\n    struct stale_arr  *next;\n};\n\nstruct graph {\n    json_arena_t *arena;\n\n    const char   *name;\n    const char   *description;\n    const char   *entry_box_id;\n    char         *map_dir;     /* malloc'd; remembered for dispatch (read boxes,\n                                 * source-file resolution). */\n\n    _Atomic(box_t **) boxes;        /* array of box pointers; stable per box */\n    _Atomic uint32_t  n_boxes;      /* number of valid entries in `boxes` */\n    _Atomic uint32_t  box_capacity; /* allocated length of `boxes`        */\n    pthread_mutex_t   graph_mu;     /* serializes runtime additions       */\n    struct stale_arr *stale_box_arrs;\n\n    int           n_languages;\n    const char  **languages;   /* arena-owned strings */\n\n    int           n_entry_boxes;\n    int          *entry_box_ids;   /* indices into boxes[] */\n\n    int           n_size_classes;\n    int          *size_classes;    /* distinct input-slot cell widths */\n};\n/* }}} */"
        },

          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"/* {{{ Accessors */\nconst char *graph_name(const graph_t *g)         { return g ? g->name : NULL; }",
          "new_string":"/* {{{ Runtime mutation — graph_add_box() (issue 319d)\n *\n * Appends a pre-built box to the graph's pointer index. The pointer\n * array grows via copy-and-publish (allocate at 2x capacity, memcpy\n * the old pointers in, atomic-store the new array, park the old on\n * stale_box_arrs for destroy-time reclamation). The new box's count\n * is published last with release semantics so a reader seeing\n * count = N also sees box N-1 fully published into the index. */\nint graph_add_box(graph_t *g, box_t *box)\n{\n    if (!g || !box) return -1;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g->graph_mu);\n\n    uint32_t n   = atomic_load_explicit(&g->n_boxes,      memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t cap = atomic_load_explicit(&g->box_capacity, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    if (n + 1u > cap) {\n        uint32_t new_cap = cap == 0 ? 16u : cap * 2u;\n        box_t **new_boxes = calloc((size_t)new_cap, sizeof(box_t *));\n        if (!new_boxes) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box_t **old_boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n        if (old_boxes && n > 0) {\n            memcpy(new_boxes, old_boxes, (size_t)n * sizeof(box_t *));\n        }\n        struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n        if (!st) { free(new_boxes); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n        st->ptr  = old_boxes;\n        st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n        g->stale_box_arrs = st;\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->boxes,        new_boxes, memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->box_capacity, new_cap,   memory_order_release);\n    }\n\n    box_t **boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n    boxes[n] = box;\n    atomic_store_explicit(&g->n_boxes, n + 1u, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n    return (int)n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime mutation — box_add_connection() (issue 319d)\n *\n * Appends one connection to box `b`'s connections array via the\n * same copy-and-publish discipline used for boxes: allocate a\n * new connections[] sized current+1, copy the old in, append the\n * new connection, atomic-store the new connections pointer, then\n * atomic-store the new count. The old connections array is parked\n * on stale_box_arrs (the list is generic, not box-specific) and\n * freed at graph_destroy. */\nint box_add_connection(graph_t *g, box_t *b, connection_t conn)\n{\n    if (!g || !b) return -1;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g->graph_mu);\n\n    int n_old = atomic_load_explicit(&b->n_connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *old = atomic_load_explicit(&b->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    connection_t *new_conns = malloc((size_t)(n_old + 1) * sizeof(connection_t));\n    if (!new_conns) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n    if (old && n_old > 0) {\n        memcpy(new_conns, old, (size_t)n_old * sizeof(connection_t));\n    }\n    new_conns[n_old] = conn;\n\n    if (old) {\n        struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n        if (!st) { free(new_conns); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n        st->ptr  = old;\n        st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n        g->stale_box_arrs = st;\n    }\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&b->connections,   new_conns, memory_order_release);\n    atomic_store_explicit(&b->n_connections, n_old + 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nconst char *graph_name(const graph_t *g)         { return g ? g->name : NULL; }"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"

    "newString":"/* {{{ Runtime mutation — graph_add_box() (issue 319d)\n *\n * Appends a pre-built box to the graph's pointer index. The pointer\n * array grows via copy-and-publish (allocate at 2x capacity, memcpy\n * the old pointers in, atomic-store the new array, park the old on\n * stale_box_arrs for destroy-time reclamation). The new box's count\n * is published last with release semantics so a reader seeing\n * count = N also sees box N-1 fully published into the index. */\nint graph_add_box(graph_t *g, box_t *box)\n{\n    if (!g || !box) return -1;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g->graph_mu);\n\n    uint32_t n   = atomic_load_explicit(&g->n_boxes,      memory_order_relaxed);\n    uint32_t cap = atomic_load_explicit(&g->box_capacity, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    if (n + 1u > cap) {\n        uint32_t new_cap = cap == 0 ? 16u : cap * 2u;\n        box_t **new_boxes = calloc((size_t)new_cap, sizeof(box_t *));\n        if (!new_boxes) {\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n            return -1;\n        }\n        box_t **old_boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n        if (old_boxes && n > 0) {\n            memcpy(new_boxes, old_boxes, (size_t)n * sizeof(box_t *));\n        }\n        struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n        if (!st) { free(new_boxes); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n        st->ptr  = old_boxes;\n        st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n        g->stale_box_arrs = st;\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->boxes,        new_boxes, memory_order_release);\n        atomic_store_explicit(&g->box_capacity, new_cap,   memory_order_release);\n    }\n\n    box_t **boxes = atomic_load_explicit(&g->boxes, memory_order_relaxed);\n    boxes[n] = box;\n    atomic_store_explicit(&g->n_boxes, n + 1u, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n    return (int)n;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Runtime mutation — box_add_connection() (issue 319d)\n *\n * Appends one connection to box `b`'s connections array via the\n * same copy-and-publish discipline used for boxes: allocate a\n * new connections[] sized current+1, copy the old in, append the\n * new connection, atomic-store the new connections pointer, then\n * atomic-store the new count. The old connections array is parked\n * on stale_box_arrs (the list is generic, not box-specific) and\n * freed at graph_destroy. */\nint box_add_connection(graph_t *g, box_t *b, connection_t conn)\n{\n    if (!g || !b) return -1;\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&g->graph_mu);\n\n    int n_old = atomic_load_explicit(&b->n_connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n    connection_t *old = atomic_load_explicit(&b->connections, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    connection_t *new_conns = malloc((size_t)(n_old + 1) * sizeof(connection_t));\n    if (!new_conns) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n    if (old && n_old > 0) {\n        memcpy(new_conns, old, (size_t)n_old * sizeof(connection_t));\n    }\n    new_conns[n_old] = conn;\n\n    if (old) {\n        struct stale_arr *st = malloc(sizeof *st);\n        if (!st) { free(new_conns); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu); return -1; }\n        st->ptr  = old;\n        st->next = g->stale_box_arrs;\n        g->stale_box_arrs = st;\n    }\n\n    atomic_store_explicit(&b->connections,   new_conns, memory_order_release);\n    atomic_store_explicit(&b->n_connections, n_old + 1, memory_order_release);\n\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g->graph_mu);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Accessors */\nconst char *graph_name(const graph_t *g)         { return g ? g->name : NULL; }",

          "content":"/* src/018-runtime-builtins.h — runtime self-construction primitives.\n *\n * Two C functions that language specs (Lua first, C/Bash to follow)\n * wrap and expose to user code, letting a running box construct new\n * boxes and wire them into the live graph:\n *\n *   runtime_create_box(spec_json) -> box_id\n *   runtime_connect(connection_json) -> 0/-1\n *\n * Designed in issue 319 (the headline self-construction feature);\n * landed in issue 319d.\n *\n * Argument shape: the JSON text passed in mirrors the on-disk box\n * JSON schema exactly. Anything you can write\n * as an entry inside that file's `connections[]` array, you can\n * pass to runtime_connect. The contract is: the API is the schema.\n *\n * Plumbing: language specs need access to the graph / slot store /\n * spec registry to call these. Rather than thread those pointers\n * through every spec invocation, we keep them in a thread-local\n * \"active context\" that dispatch_action sets before invoking the\n * spec and clears after. The runtime builtins read the thread-local\n * to find the targets.\n */\n#ifndef SORAMECH_018_RUNTIME_BUILTINS_H\n#define SORAMECH_018_RUNTIME_BUILTINS_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n\nstruct graph;\nstruct slot_store;\nstruct spec_registry;\n\n/* {{{ Active runtime context (thread-local)\n *\n * Set by dispatch_action immediately before invoking a spec, cleared\n * immediately after. Spec code (including the language bindings that\n * call into runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) reads these to find\n * the graph and runtime resources. */\nvoid runtime_set_active_context(struct graph         *g,\n                                struct slot_store    *s,\n                                struct spec_registry *r);\nvoid runtime_clear_active_context(void);\n\nstruct graph         *runtime_active_graph(void);\nstruct slot_store    *runtime_active_slots(void);\nstruct spec_registry *runtime_active_specs(void);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_create_box()\n *\n * Parses `spec_json` as a box schema entry, instantiates the box at\n * runtime, allocates input slots, registers it in the active graph.\n * Fills `out_id` with the new box's id (auto-generated if the JSON\n * didn't supply one). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error with *err\n * set to a malloc'd diagnostic (caller frees).\n *\n * Slice 1 scope (this commit):\n *   - kind: \"call\" only\n *   - lang: \"lua\" only\n *   - routing.kind: \"plain\" only\n *   - inputs: array of { name, type }\n *\n * Other kinds, langs, and routing variants surface clear errors\n * for now; they'll land in 319e. */\nint runtime_create_box(const char *spec_json, int spec_len,\n                       char *out_id, size_t out_id_size,\n                       char **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_connect()\n *\n * Parses `conn_json` as a connection entry, looks up from_box /\n * to_box / to_input, appends the connection to the producer's\n * connections array via box_add_connection. Returns 0 on success,\n * -1 on error with *err set to a malloc'd diagnostic. */\nint runtime_connect(const char *conn_json, int conn_len,\n                    char **err);\n/* }}} */\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_018_RUNTIME_BUILTINS_H */\n"
        },
        "caller":{

Other shapes return an error\n * naming what's not yet supported.\n */\n#include \"018-runtime-builtins.h\"\n#include \"010-graph-loader.h\"\n#include \"009-slot-store.h\"\n#include \"011-spec-registry.h\"\n#include \"017-box-id.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n#include \"langs/lang-spec.h\"\n\n#include <stdarg.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Thread-local active context */\nstatic __thread struct graph         *tls_graph;\nstatic __thread struct slot_store    *tls_slots;\nstatic __thread struct spec_registry *tls_specs;\n\nvoid runtime_set_active_context(struct graph         *g,\n                                struct slot_store    *s,\n                                struct spec_registry *r)\n{\n    tls_graph = g;\n    tls_slots = s;\n    tls_specs = r;\n}\n\nvoid runtime_clear_active_context(void)\n{\n    tls_graph = NULL;\n    tls_slots = NULL;\n    tls_specs = NULL;\n}\n\nstruct graph         *runtime_active_graph(void) { return tls_graph; }\nstruct slot_store    *runtime_active_slots(void) { return tls_slots; }\nstruct spec_registry *runtime_active_specs(void) { return tls_specs; }\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Small error-formatting helper */\n__attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)))\nstatic int set_err(char **err_out, const char *fmt, ...)\n{\n    if (!err_out) return -1;\n    char buf[1024];\n    va_list ap;\n    va_start(ap, fmt);\n    int n = vsnprintf(buf, sizeof buf, fmt, ap);\n    va_end(ap);\n    if (n < 0) { *err_out = NULL; return -1; }\n    size_t len = (size_t)n < sizeof buf ? (size_t)n : sizeof buf - 1;\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (out) { memcpy(out, buf, len); out[len] = '\\0'; }\n    *err_out = out;\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Resolve a language name to its index in the spec registry */\nstatic int find_spec_idx(struct spec_registry *r, const char *lang)\n{\n    int n = spec_registry_size(r);\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        const lang_spec_t *s = spec_registry_at(r, i);\n        if (s && s->name && strcmp(s->name, lang) == 0) return i;\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Strdup-into-arena helper */\nstatic const char *arena_strdup(json_arena_t *a, const char *s)\n{\n    /* The arena exposes parse/value helpers but not a raw strdup;\n     * for runtime-created boxes we don't strictly need the arena\n     * to own the string — graph_destroy doesn't free per-box id /\n     * lang / etc. strings on the runtime path. But to keep\n     * lifetimes uniform we copy via plain malloc and lean on\n     * graph_destroy to free runtime-created boxes' owned strings.\n     *\n     * Slice-1 simplification: we malloc each string individually\n     * and rely on the box's free at graph_destroy. Each string\n     * field that runtime-created boxes own is freed there. */\n    (void)a;\n    size_t len = strlen(s);\n    char  *p   = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n    memcpy(p, s, len + 1);\n    return p;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Build input declarations from the JSON inputs array */\nstatic int build_inputs(const json_node_t *inputs_node,\n                        input_decl_t **out_inputs, int *out_n,\n                        char **err_out)\n{\n    if (!inputs_node) {\n        *out_inputs = NULL;\n        *out_n      = 0;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind((json_node_t *)inputs_node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: 'inputs' must be an array\");\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(inputs_node);\n    if (n == 0) {\n        *out_inputs = NULL;\n        *out_n      = 0;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    input_decl_t *arr = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof *arr);\n    if (!arr) return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory\");\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *e = json_array_get(inputs_node, i);\n        if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            free(arr);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: inputs[%d] is not an object\", i);\n        }\n        json_node_t *name_n = json_object_get(e, \"name\");\n        json_node_t *type_n = json_object_get(e, \"type\");\n        if (!name_n || json_kind(name_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            free(arr);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: inputs[%d].name missing\", i);\n        }\n        arr[i].name = arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(name_n));\n        arr[i].type = (type_n && json_kind(type_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                          ? arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(type_n))\n                          : NULL;\n        arr[i].literal = NULL;\n        arr[i].optional = 0;\n    }\n    *out_inputs = arr;\n    *out_n      = n;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_create_box() */\nint runtime_create_box(const char *spec_json, int spec_len,\n                       char *out_id, size_t out_id_size,\n                       char **err_out)\n{\n    if (err_out) *err_out = NULL;\n\n    struct graph         *g     = runtime_active_graph();\n    struct slot_store    *slots = runtime_active_slots();\n    struct spec_registry *specs = runtime_active_specs();\n    if (!g || !slots || !specs) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: no active runtime context \"\n                                \"(must be called from within a spec invoke)\");\n    }\n    if (!spec_json || spec_len <= 0) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: spec is empty\");\n    }\n    if (!out_id || out_id_size < BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out_id buffer too small \"\n                                \"(need at least %u bytes)\",\n                       (unsigned)BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE);\n    }\n\n    /* Parse the JSON spec. Slice 1 — only \"lua\" is supported. */\n    json_node_t *lang_n = json_object_get(root, \"lang\");\n    if (!lang_n || json_kind(lang_n) != JSON_STRING ||\n        strcmp(json_string_value(lang_n), \"lua\") != 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: only lang='lua' is supported \"\n                                \"in this slice (issue 319d)\");\n    }\n    int spec_idx = find_spec_idx(specs, \"lua\");\n    if (spec_idx < 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: lua spec not registered\");\n    }\n\n    /* Required: ref + fn */\n    json_node_t *ref_n = json_object_get(root, \"ref\");\n    json_node_t *fn_n  = json_object_get(root, \"fn\");\n    if (!ref_n || json_kind(ref_n) != JSON_STRING ||\n        !fn_n  || json_kind(fn_n)  != JSON_STRING) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: 'ref' and 'fn' strings required\");\n    }\n\n    /* Optional id; auto-generate when absent. */\n    char id_buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    const char *id_source;\n    json_node_t *id_n = json_object_get(root, \"id\");\n    if (id_n && json_kind(id_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n        id_source = json_string_value(id_n);\n    } else {\n        if (box_id_generate(id_buf, sizeof id_buf) != 0) {\n            json_arena_destroy(arena);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: id generator failed\");\n        }\n        id_source = id_buf;\n    }\n\n    /* Build inputs. */\n    input_decl_t *inputs = NULL;\n    int           n_inputs = 0;\n    if (build_inputs(json_object_get(root, \"inputs\"),\n                     &inputs, &n_inputs, err_out) != 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Allocate the box record. */\n    box_t *b = calloc(1, sizeof *b);\n    if (!b) {\n        free(inputs);\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory (box)\");\n    }\n    b->id   = arena_strdup(NULL, id_source);\n    b->kind = BOX_CALL;\n    b->lang = arena_strdup(NULL, \"lua\");\n    b->ref  = arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(ref_n));\n    b->fn   = arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(fn_n));\n    b->returns = NULL;\n    b->routing.kind      = ROUTING_PLAIN;\n    b->routing.n_outputs = 1;\n    b->output_capacity = 256;   /* slice-1 default; 0 (variable) not exposed yet */\n    b->n_inputs  = n_inputs;\n    b->inputs    = inputs;\n    atomic_init(&b->n_connections, 0);\n    atomic_init(&b->connections,   NULL);\n    b->spec_idx  = spec_idx;\n    b->counter_slot_id = -1;\n    b->multi_spawn     = 0;\n\n    /* Allocate one input slot per input port. The slot store's\n     * 319b growth machinery handles the runtime-add path. */\n    if (n_inputs > 0) {\n        b->input_slot_ids   = malloc((size_t)n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n        b->input_slot_modes = malloc((size_t)n_inputs * sizeof(int));\n        if (!b->input_slot_ids || !b->input_slot_modes) {\n            free(b->input_slot_ids);\n            free(b->input_slot_modes);\n            free((void *)b->id);\n            free((void *)b->lang);\n            free((void *)b->ref);\n            free((void *)b->fn);\n            free(inputs);\n            free(b);\n            json_arena_destroy(arena);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory (slot arrays)\");\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_inputs; i++) {\n            int sid = slot_alloc(slots, b->output_capacity, 1, 0);\n            if (sid < 0) {\n                /* On failure, free what we've allocated; the slot\n                 * store's earlier-allocated slots stay around until\n                 * graph teardown (no slot_free in this slice — 315\n                 * territory). */\n                free(b->input_slot_ids);\n                free(b->input_slot_modes);\n                free((void *)b->id);\n                free((void *)b->lang);\n                free((void *)b->ref);\n                free((void *)b->fn);\n                free(inputs);\n                free(b);\n                json_arena_destroy(arena);\n                return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: slot_alloc failed for input %d\", i);\n            }\n  if (new_idx < 0) {\n        /* Free the box record but not the slots (no slot_free in\n         * this slice). */\n        free(b->input_slot_ids);\n        free(b->input_slot_modes);\n        free((void *)b->id);\n        free((void *)b->lang);\n        free((void *)b->ref);\n        free((void *)b->fn);\n        free(inputs);\n        free(b);\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: graph_add_box failed\");\n    }\n\n    /* Fill the caller's out_id buffer. */\n    snprintf(out_id, out_id_size, \"%s\", b->id);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(arena);\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_connect() */\nint runtime_connect(const char *conn_json, int conn_len, char **err_out)\n{\n    if (err_out) *err_out = NULL;\n\n    struct graph *g = runtime_active_graph();\n    if (!g) return set_err(err_out, \"connect: no active runtime context\");\n    if (!conn_json || conn_len <= 0) {\n        return return set_err(err_out, \"connect: no box named '%s'\", from_id);\n    }\n    if (to_idx < 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"connect: no box named '%s'\", Each string\n     * field that runtime-created boxes own is freed there. */\n    (void)a;\n    size_t len = strlen(s);\n    char  *p   = malloc(len + 1);\n    if (!p) return NULL;\n    memcpy(p, s, len + 1);\n    return p;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Build input declarations from the JSON inputs array */\nstatic int build_inputs(const json_node_t *inputs_node,\n                        input_decl_t **out_inputs, int *out_n,\n                        char **err_out)\n{\n    if (!inputs_node) {\n        *out_inputs = NULL;\n        *out_n      = 0;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (json_kind((json_node_t *)inputs_node) != JSON_ARRAY) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: 'inputs' must be an array\");\n    }\n    int n = json_array_size(inputs_node);\n    if (n == 0) {\n        *out_inputs = NULL;\n        *out_n      = 0;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    input_decl_t *arr = calloc((size_t)n, sizeof *arr);\n    if (!arr) return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory\");\n\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        json_node_t *e = json_array_get(inputs_node, i);\n        if (!e || json_kind(e) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n            free(arr);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: inputs[%d] is not an object\", i);\n        }\n        json_node_t *name_n = json_object_get(e, \"name\");\n        json_node_t *type_n = json_object_get(e, \"type\");\n        if (!name_n || json_kind(name_n) != JSON_STRING) {\n            free(arr);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: inputs[%d].name missing\", i);\n        }\n        arr[i].name = arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(name_n));\n        arr[i].type = (type_n && json_kind(type_n) == JSON_STRING)\n                          ? arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(type_n))\n                          : NULL;\n        arr[i].literal = NULL;\n        arr[i].optional = 0;\n    }\n    *out_inputs = arr;\n    *out_n      = n;\n    return 0;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ runtime_create_box() */\nint runtime_create_box(const char *spec_json, int spec_len,\n                       char *out_id, size_t out_id_size,\n                       char **err_out)\n{\n    if (err_out) *err_out = NULL;\n\n    struct graph         *g     = runtime_active_graph();\n    struct slot_store    *slots = runtime_active_slots();\n    struct spec_registry *specs = runtime_active_specs();\n    if (!g || !slots || !specs) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: no active runtime context \"\n                                \"(must be called from within a spec invoke)\");\n    }\n    if (!spec_json || spec_len <= 0) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: spec is empty\");\n    }\n    if (!out_id || out_id_size < BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE) {\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out_id buffer too small \"\n                                \"(need at least %u bytes)\",\n                       (unsigned)BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE);\n    }\n\n    /* Parse the JSON spec. We use a scratch arena that we destroy\n     * at the end of the function — the box record's string fields\n     * are deep-copied via malloc above, so the arena's lifetime\n     * doesn't need to outlive the parse. */\n    json_arena_t *arena = json_arena_create();\n    if (!arena) return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory (arena)\");\n\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(arena, spec_json, (size_t)spec_len, NULL);\n    if (!root || json_kind(root) != JSON_OBJECT) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: spec is not a JSON object\");\n    }\n\n    /* Required: kind. Slice 1 — only \"lua\" is supported. */\n    json_node_t *lang_n = json_object_get(root, \"lang\");\n    if (!lang_n || json_kind(lang_n) != JSON_STRING ||\n        strcmp(json_string_value(lang_n), \"lua\") != 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: only lang='lua' is supported \"\n                                \"in this slice (issue 319d)\");\n    }\n    int spec_idx = find_spec_idx(specs, \"lua\");\n    if (spec_idx < 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: lua spec not registered\");\n    }\n\n    /* Required: ref + fn */\n    json_node_t *ref_n = json_object_get(root, \"ref\");\n    json_node_t *fn_n  = json_object_get(root, \"fn\");\n    if (!ref_n || json_kind(ref_n) != JSON_STRING ||\n        !fn_n  || json_kind(fn_n)  != JSON_STRING) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: 'ref' and 'fn' strings required\");\n    }\n\n    /* Optional id; auto-generate when absent. */\n    char id_buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    const char *id_source;\n    json_node_t *id_n = json_object_get(root, \"id\");\n    if (id_n && json_kind(id_n) == JSON_STRING) {\n        id_source = json_string_value(id_n);\n    } else {\n        if (box_id_generate(id_buf, sizeof id_buf) != 0) {\n            json_arena_destroy(arena);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: id generator failed\");\n        }\n        id_source = id_buf;\n    }\n\n    /* Build inputs. */\n    input_decl_t *inputs = NULL;\n    int           n_inputs = 0;\n    if (build_inputs(json_object_get(root, \"inputs\"),\n                     &inputs, &n_inputs, err_out) != 0) {\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    /* Allocate the box record. */\n    box_t *b = calloc(1, sizeof *b);\n    if (!b) {\n        free(inputs);\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory (box)\");\n    }\n    b->id   = arena_strdup(NULL, id_source);\n    b->kind = BOX_CALL;\n    b->lang = arena_strdup(NULL, \"lua\");\n    b->ref  = arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(ref_n));\n    b->fn   = arena_strdup(NULL, json_string_value(fn_n));\n    b->returns = NULL;\n    b->routing.kind      = ROUTING_PLAIN;\n    b->routing.n_outputs = 1;\n    b->output_capacity = 256;            free((void *)b->id);\n            free((void *)b->lang);\n            free((void *)b->ref);\n            free((void *)b->fn);\n            free(inputs);\n            free(b);\n            json_arena_destroy(arena);\n            return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: out of memory (slot arrays)\");\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < n_inputs; i++) {\n            int sid = slot_alloc(slots, b->output_capacity, 1, 0);\n            if (sid < 0) {\n                /* On failure, free what we've allocated; the slot\n                 * store's earlier-allocated slots stay free(b->input_slot_modes);\n                free((void *)b->id);\n                free((void *)b->lang);\n                free((void *)b->ref);\n                free((void *)b->fn);\n                free(inputs);\n                free(b);\n                json_arena_destroy(arena);\n                return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: slot_alloc failed for input %d\", i);\n            }\n            b->input_slot_ids[i]   = sid;\n            b->input_slot_modes[i] = 0;  /* SLOT_MODE_PEEK */\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Append the box to the graph. */\n    int new_idx = graph_add_box(g, b);\n    if (new_idx < 0) {\n        /* Free the box record but not the slots (no slot_free in\n         * this slice). */\n        free(b->input_slot_ids);\n        free(b->input_slot_modes);\n        free((void *)b->id);\n        free((void *)b->lang);\n        free((void *)b->ref);\n        free((void *)b->fn);\n        free(inputs);\n        free(b);\n        json_arena_destroy(arena);\n        return set_err(err_out, \"create_box: graph_add_box failed\");\n    }\n\n    /* Fill the caller's out_id buffer. */\n    snprintf(out_id, out_id_size, \"%s\", b->id);\n\n       "content":"}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_action() — the pool action body */\nvoid dispatch_action(void *arg)\n{\n    dispatch_task_t *t = (dispatch_task_t *)arg;\n    if (!t) return;\n    dispatch_ctx_t *ctx = (dispatch_ctx_t *)t->ctx;\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, t->box_id);\n\n    atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->tasks_dispatched, 1, memory_order_relaxed);\n\n    int task_id    = t->task_id;\n    int worker_idx = pool_current_worker ? pool_current_worker->thread_idx : -1;\n\n    long start_us = mono_us();\n    if (ctx->events)\n        event_queue_task_start(ctx->events, now_secs(), task_id, worker_idx);\n\n    int out_size = 0;\n    int out_capacity = ctx->default_out_capacity > 0\n                        ? ctx->default_out_capacity : 4096;\n    /* The output buffer comes from the slot store's unified\n     * allocator so it participates in the same refcount-driven\n     * recycling as input buffers and slot cells — every byte that\n     * carries a value through the dispatch runs through one heap. */\n    ua_t *heap = slot_store_allocator(ctx->slots);\n    ua_chunk_t *out_chunk = ua_alloc(heap, (size_t)out_capacity);\n    char *out_buf = out_chunk ? ua_data(out_chunk) : NULL;\n    int rc = -1;\n    if (out_buf && b) {\n        switch (b->kind) {\n            case BOX_CALL:\n                rc = do_call_box(ctx, b, task_id, out_buf, out_capacity, &out_size);"

          "new_string":"/* {{{ Soramech runtime-builtins: create_box and connect (issue 319d)\n *\n * Two Lua-callable functions exposed under the global `soramech`\n * table. Both take Lua tables shaped like the on-disk box JSON\n * schema (for create_box) or a single connection entry (for\n * connect, variadic). The tables are encoded to JSON via the same\n * encode_value machinery the spec uses for cross-language wire\n * serialization, then handed to the C runtime API. Errors\n * hard-crash via luaL_error, which propagates as a Lua error and\n * unwinds the spec's invoke. */\nstatic int lua_soramech_create_box(lua_State *L)\n{\n    luaL_checktype(L, 1, LUA_TTABLE);\n\n    /* Stack-allocated 4 KB scratch is big enough for any sane box\n     * spec; if a real workload trips this the buffer becomes a\n     * heap allocation. Slice-1 keeps it simple. */\n    char json_buf[4096];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, json_buf, sizeof json_buf);\n    if (encode_value(L, 1, &w) != 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: failed to encode spec to JSON\");\n    }\n    int json_len = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    if (json_len < 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: JSON encode overflow (spec exceeds %zu bytes)\",\n                          sizeof json_buf);\n    }\n\n    char id_buf[BOX_ID_GEN_BUF_SIZE];\n    char *err = NULL;\n    if (runtime_create_box(json_buf, json_len, id_buf, sizeof id_buf, &err) != 0) {\n        char msg[1024];\n        snprintf(msg, sizeof msg, \"%s\", err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n        free(err);\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.create_box: %s\", msg);\n    }\n    lua_pushstring(L, id_buf);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int lua_soramech_connect(lua_State *L)\n{\n    int n = lua_gettop(L);\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: expected at least one connection\");\n    }\n    char json_buf[2048];\n    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {\n        luaL_checktype(L, i, LUA_TTABLE);\n        json_writer_t w;\n        json_writer_init(&w, json_buf, sizeof json_buf);\n        if (encode_value(L, i, &w) != 0) {\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: failed to encode connection #%d\", i);\n        }\n        int json_len = json_writer_finish(&w);\n        if (json_len < 0) {\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: JSON encode overflow on connection #%d\", i);\n        }\n        char *err = NULL;\n        if (runtime_connect(json_buf, json_len, &err) != 0) {\n            char msg[1024];\n            snprintf(msg, sizeof msg, \"%s\", err ? err : \"(no message)\");\n            free(err);\n            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: %s\", msg);\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\nstatic void register_soramech_builtins(lua_State *L)\n{\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_create_box);\n    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"create_box\");\n    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_connect);\n    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"connect\");\n    lua_setglobal(L, \"soramech\");\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs, seed cache */\nstatic void *lua_init(int worker_idx)\n{\n    (void)worker_idx;\n    lua_State *L = luaL_newstate();\n    if (!L) return NULL;\n    luaL_openlibs(L);\n    /* Seed the empty cache table. */\n    lua_newtable(L);\n    lua_setfield(L, LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, LUA_CACHE_KEY);\n    /* Register the self-construction builtins (issue 319d). They\n     * read the active runtime context from thread-local storage\n     * that dispatch_action sets before each invoke. */\n    register_soramech_builtins(L);\n    return L;\n}\n/* }}} */"

err : \"(no message)\");","+            free(err);","+            return luaL_error(L, \"soramech.connect: %s\", msg);","+        }","+    }","+    return 0;","+}","+","+static void register_soramech_builtins(lua_State *L)","+{","+    lua_newtable(L);","+    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_create_box);","+    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"create_box\");","+    lua_pushcfunction(L, lua_soramech_connect);","+    lua_setfield(L, -2, \"connect\");","+    lua_setglobal(L, \"soramech\");","+}","+/* }}} */","+"," /* {{{ lua_init() — create a state, open standard libs, seed cache */"," static void *lua_init(int worker_idx)"," {"],

Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.",
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises.           "content":"-- 319d fixture — the trigger box uses soramech.create_box +\n-- soramech.connect to spawn a downstream \"echo_dyn\" box at runtime\n-- and wire its own output to it. The runtime then sees the new\n-- connection on the trigger's connections[] array and pushes the\n-- trigger's return value into the freshly-created downstream slot.\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.trigger\nfunction M.trigger(input)\n    -- Build the box spec as a Lua table that mirrors the on-disk\n    -- box JSON schema.\n    local new_id = soramech.create_box{\n        kind = \"call\",\n        lang = \"lua\",\n        ref  = \"src/echo_dyn.lua\",\n        fn   = \"echo\",\n        inputs = {\n            {name = \"x\", type = \"string\"}\n        }\n    }\n    -- Wire this box's output to the new box's \"x\" port.\n    soramech.connect{\n        from_box    = \"trigger\",\n        from_branch = nil,\n        to_box      = new_id,\n        to_input    = \"x\"\n    }\n    -- Return a marker that includes the new box's id so the test\n    -- runner can verify create_box returned something sensible.\n    return \"trigger-fired:\" .. new_id .. \":\" .. input\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01XwCPjtJmWQYP3QfDaa2PJT",

      "content":"/* {{{ dispatch_spawn_if_ready() */\nvoid dispatch_spawn_if_ready(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, int box_id, int priority)\n{\n    if (!ctx) return;\n    if (box_id < 0 || box_id >= ctx->n_boxes) return;\n    if (!box_is_ready(ctx, box_id)) return;\n\n    const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, box_id);\n    /* 244: read boxes are pull-on-demand value sources, not tasks.\n     * They never enter the pool — their consumers read the cached\n     * value directly when they fire. */\n    if (b && b->kind == BOX_READ) return;\n    if (b && b->multi_spawn) {\n        /* Multi-spawn box (iterator or anything downstream of one).\n         * The single-spawn guard doesn't apply: every push that\n         * leaves the box ready spawns a new task, which will drain\n         * one cell from each POP input. The iterator's own\n         * dispatch_action also re-spawns itself while inputs remain\n         * so a single push can wake the chain. */\n        dispatch_spawn(ctx, box_id, priority);\n        return;\n    }\n\n    /* Single-spawn case: CAS the per-box guard. The first push that\n     * finds the consumer ready wins; everyone else short-circuits.\n     * The 1-cell peek model spawns each box at most once per run. */\n    int expected = 0;\n    if (atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&ctx->box_ever_spawned[box_id],\n                                       &expected, 1)) {\n        dispatch_spawn(ctx, box_id, priority);\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ dispatch_push_literals() */\nint dispatch_push_literals(dispatch_ctx_t *ctx, char **err)\n{\n    if (!ctx) {\n        if (err) *err = err_fmt(\"dispatch_push_literals: NULL ctx\");\n        return -1;"
    },

      "content":" * graph via consumer pulls, observed in the consumers' outputs. */\nstatic void print_outputs(const dispatch_ctx_t *ctx)\n{\n    if (!ctx->last_outputs) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ctx->n_boxes; i++) {\n        const box_t *b = graph_box(ctx->graph, i);\n        if (b && b->kind == BOX_READ) continue;\n        const char *out = ctx->last_outputs[i];\n        if (out) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → %s\\n\", b->id, out);\n        } else {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"  %s → (no output)\\n\", b->id);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main() */\nint main(int argc, char **argv)\n{\n    if (argc < 2 || strcmp(argv[1], \"--help\") == 0 || strcmp(argv[1], \"-h\") == 0) {\n        usage(argv[0]);\n        return (argc < 2) ? 2 : 0;\n    }\n    const char *map_dir = argv[1];"

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/run-tests.sh",
    "newString":"check_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\npipeline_output_check",
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

          "content":"# 319d — `create_box` and `connect` runtime built-ins, Lua bindings\n\n## Status\ncomplete (slice 1)\n\n## Parent issue\nSub-issue of 319. Lands the headline self-construction feature\nfor Lua call boxes with plain routing. C and Bash bindings,\nnon-call kinds, comparator / iterator / etc. routing, and\nencapsulated map outputs all roll up under 319e or follow-on\nslices.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo runtime functions exposed to language specs (Lua first):\n\n- **`soramech.create_box(table)` → string** — instantiates a new\n  box at runtime. The `table` argument mirrors the on-disk box\n  JSON schema; anything writable as `boxes/<id>.json` is acceptable.\n  Internally: serializes the Lua table to JSON via the same\n  `encode_value` machinery used for cross-language wire\n  serialization (issue 312); hands the JSON to the C runtime API\n  which parses, allocates a box record, allocates input slots\n  (319b), and appends to the graph's box index via `graph_add_box`.\n  Returns the new box's id (auto-generated via 319c if the spec\n  didn't supply one).\n- **`soramech.connect(table, ...)`** — variadic. Each table is\n  one entry shaped like a `connections[]` entry on disk\n  (`{from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input}`). Appends to the\n  producer's atomic `connections` array via `box_add_connection`.\n\nBoth hard-crash via `luaL_error` on any failure (Q3 resolution).\n\nPlumbing: a thread-local `runtime_active_context` is set by\n`dispatch_action` before each spec invoke and cleared after.\nThe runtime builtins read the TLS to find the active graph,\nslot store, and spec registry — no changes to the spec's\ninvoke signature were required.\n\n## What lands in this slice\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}` — `box_t *boxes` becomes\n  `_Atomic(box_t **)` with copy-and-publish growth via\n  `graph_add_box`; box records are now individual mallocs so\n  their addresses are stable across pointer-array growth.\n  Per-box `connections` becomes `_Atomic(connection_t *)` with\n  the same atomic-publish + stale-list pattern via\n  `box_add_connection`.\n- `src/017-box-id.h/c` — already-shipped 319c utility, reused.\n- `src/018-runtime-builtins.{h,c}` — the `runtime_create_box`\n  and `runtime_connect` C functions plus the TLS active-context\n  setter/getter pair.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — sets and clears the TLS context around\n  each spec invoke. Also: dispatch's per-box arrays\n  (`box_ever_spawned`, `last_outputs`, `last_output_sizes`) get\n  oversized by `RUNTIME_BOX_HEADROOM = 4096` entries at init\n  so runtime-created boxes have room to participate. Proper\n  growable arrays are a follow-on.\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — `print_outputs` now iterates over\n  `graph_n_boxes(ctx->graph)` (which reflects runtime additions)\n  rather than `ctx->n_boxes` (capacity).\n- `langs/lua/spec.c` — `lua_soramech_create_box` /\n  `lua_soramech_connect` wrappers + `register_soramech_builtins`\n  called from `lua_init`.\n- `langs/lua/Makefile` — adds `-I$(DIR)/src` so the lua spec can\n  include the runtime-builtins header.\n- `Makefile` — adds `-rdynamic` to `LDFLAGS` so dlopen'd spec.so\n  binaries can call back into the runner's `runtime_*` symbols.\n- `tests/maps/319d-runtime-create/` — end-to-end fixture: a Lua\n  box uses `soramech.create_box` to spawn an `echo_dyn` box,\n  uses `soramech.connect` to wire to it, then returns a value\n  that pushes through the new connection. The dynamically-\n  created box fires and produces output.\n\n## Restrictions in this slice\n\n- **Lua only.** C and Bash specs don't yet expose `soramech.*`.\n  Their bindings land in 319e.\n- **Call boxes only.** `create_box` rejects `kind != \"call\"`.\n  Read / write / encapsulated-map kinds land later.\n- **Plain routing only.** Comparator / iterator / randomizer /\n  weighted / distributor routing on dynamically-created boxes\n  rejected.\n- **Runtime-headroom cap.** Dispatch's per-box arrays support up\n  to 4096 dynamically-created boxes. Beyond that, spawn checks\n  silently fail. The cap is dispatch-internal; raise it or land\n  growable arrays when needed.\n- **Single-spawn-firing-box assumption.** `connect` is safe when\n  called from the spec of the producer being wired (the common\n  case), since the single-spawn CAS guard means no other worker\n  is reading that box's connections concurrently. Calling\n  `connect` from one box's spec to add a wire FROM a different,\n  potentially-firing box is not race-safe; documented but not\n  enforced.\n\n## Validation\n\n- 13 integration tests pass, including the new\n  `319d-runtime-create` fixture that exercises the full path\n  end-to-end: trigger Lua box's function calls `create_box`,\n  calls `connect`, returns a value; the dispatcher pushes\n  through the new connection; the dynamically-created `echo_dyn`\n  box fires and its output is captured.\n- The slot store's 23 unit tests (including the 319b growth\n  test) still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}`\n- `src/012-dispatch.c`\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c`\n- `src/018-runtime-builtins.{h,c}` (new)\n- `langs/lua/spec.c`\n- `langs/lua/Makefile`\n- `Makefile`\n- `tests/maps/319d-runtime-create/`\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh`\n"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01H75hyTeXBaPff496JquojY",
        "type":"tool_use"
      }],

Each table is\n  one entry shaped like a `connections[]` entry on disk\n  (`{from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input}`). Appends to the\n  producer's atomic `connections` array via `box_add_connection`.\n\nBoth hard-crash via `luaL_error` on any failure (Q3 resolution).\n\nPlumbing: a thread-local `runtime_active_context` is set by\n`dispatch_action` before each spec invoke and cleared after.\nThe runtime builtins read the TLS to find the active graph,\nslot store, and spec registry — no changes to the spec's\ninvoke signature were required.\n\n## What lands in this slice\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}` — `box_t *boxes` becomes\n  `_Atomic(box_t **)` with copy-and-publish growth via\n  `graph_add_box`; box records are now individual mallocs so\n  their addresses are stable across pointer-array growth.\n  Per-box `connections` becomes `_Atomic(connection_t *)` with\n  the same atomic-publish + stale-list pattern via\n  `box_add_connection`.\n- `src/017-box-id.h/c` — already-shipped 319c utility, reused.\n- `src/018-runtime-builtins.{h,c}` — the `runtime_create_box`\n  and `runtime_connect` C functions plus the TLS active-context\n  setter/getter pair.\n- `src/012-dispatch.c` — sets and clears the TLS context around\n  each spec invoke. Also: dispatch's per-box arrays\n  (`box_ever_spawned`, `last_outputs`, `last_output_sizes`) get\n  oversized by `RUNTIME_BOX_HEADROOM = 4096` entries at init\n  so runtime-created boxes have room to participate. Proper\n  growable arrays are a follow-on.\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — `print_outputs` now iterates over\n  `graph_n_boxes(ctx->graph)` (which reflects runtime additions)\n  rather than `ctx->n_boxes` (capacity).\n- `langs/lua/spec.c` — `lua_soramech_create_box` /\n  `lua_soramech_connect` wrappers + `register_soramech_builtins`\n  called from `lua_init`.\n- `langs/lua/Makefile` — adds `-I$(DIR)/src` so the lua spec can\n  include the runtime-builtins header.\n- `Makefile` — adds `-rdynamic` to `LDFLAGS` so dlopen'd spec.so\n  binaries can call back into the runner's `runtime_*` symbols.\n- `tests/maps/319d-runtime-create/` — end-to-end fixture: a Lua\n  box uses `soramech.create_box` to spawn an `echo_dyn` box,\n  uses `soramech.connect` to wire to it, then returns a value\n  that pushes through the new connection. The dynamically-\n  created box fires and produces output.\n\n## Restrictions in this slice\n\n- **Lua only.** C and Bash specs don't yet expose `soramech.*`.\n  Their bindings land in 319e.\n- **Call boxes only.** `create_box` rejects `kind != \"call\"`.\n  Read / write / encapsulated-map kinds land later.\n- **Plain routing only.** Comparator / iterator / randomizer /\n  weighted / distributor routing on dynamically-created boxes\n  rejected.\n- **Runtime-headroom cap.** Dispatch's per-box arrays support up\n  to 4096 dynamically-created boxes. Beyond that, spawn checks\n  silently fail. The cap is dispatch-internal; raise it or land\n  growable arrays when needed.\n- **Single-spawn-firing-box assumption.** `connect` is safe when\n  called from the spec of the producer being wired (the common\n  case), since the single-spawn CAS guard means no other worker\n  is reading that box's connections concurrently. Calling\n  `connect` from one box's spec to add a wire FROM a different,\n  potentially-firing box is not race-safe; documented but not\n  enforced.\n\n## Validation\n\n- 13 integration tests pass, including the new\n  `319d-runtime-create` fixture that exercises the full path\n  end-to-end: trigger Lua box's function calls `create_box`,\n  calls `connect`, returns a value; the dispatcher pushes\n  through the new connection; the dynamically-created `echo_dyn`\n  box fires and its output is captured.\n- The slot store's 23 unit tests (including the 319b growth\n  test) still pass.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}`\n- `src/012-dispatch.c`\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c`\n- `src/018-runtime-builtins.{h,c}` (new)\n- `langs/lua/spec.c`\n- `langs/lua/Makefile`\n- `Makefile`\n- `tests/maps/319d-runtime-create/`\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh`\n"
  },

          "description":"Commit 319d",
          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n319d — closeout: maps build more of themselves at runtime\n\nThe headline feature for 319 lands. A running Lua box can now mint\na new box and wire to it from inside its own function body:\n\n  local id = soramech.create_box{\n    kind = \"call\", lang = \"lua\",\n    ref = \"src/echo.lua\", fn = \"echo\",\n    inputs = {{name = \"x\", type = \"string\"}}\n  }\n  soramech.connect{from_box = \"self\", to_box = id, to_input = \"x\"}\n\nWhen the box's function returns, the dispatcher walks the producer's\nconnections — now including the freshly-added wire — and pushes the\nreturn value into the newly-created box's input slot. The spawn\ncheck fires, the new box runs, its output is captured. End-to-end.\n\nWhat had to grow under the hood. The graph's box index was a flat\nrealloc'd array of box_t structs; that's now a pointer-array of\nindividually-malloc'd box records (so each box's address stays\nstable across pointer-array growth), with copy-and-publish under\na mutex when the index itself needs to grow. The per-box connection\nlist got the same treatment via atomic copy-and-publish, with old\narrays parked on a stale-list and freed at graph teardown. Both\nchanges are invisible above the graph_box / graph_n_boxes accessor\nboundary, so dispatch and the event log didn't have to learn about\nthe shape change.\n\nThe dispatch context's per-box bookkeeping arrays (spawn guards,\noutput-capture buffers) are sized at init time and aren't yet\ngrowable. Slice 1 oversizes them by a generous headroom (4096\nruntime-created boxes) instead of plumbing growable arrays end\nto end. The headroom is documented in the issue file as a known\nlimit; raising it or making the arrays properly growable is a\nfollow-on.\n\nPlumbing for spec → runtime API. The runtime targets (graph, slot\nstore, spec registry) live in a thread-local that dispatch_action\nsets before each spec invoke and clears after. The Lua builtin\nwrappers read the TLS to find them — no change to the spec invoke\nsignature was needed. The runner is linked with -rdynamic so the\ndlopen'd spec.so plugins can call back into the runner's runtime_*\nsymbols at load time.\n\nSlice 1 restrictions, documented in the issue: Lua only (C and\nBash bindings come in 319e), kind=call only, plain routing only,\nand the connect call assumes the from_box is the currently-firing\nspec (the common case is safe under the existing single-spawn CAS;\nthe general concurrent case is deferred).\n\nValidation: 13 integration tests pass, including a new fixture\nwhere the trigger box uses create_box + connect to spawn a\ndownstream echo_dyn box that runs and produces output. The\nslot store's 23 unit tests still pass.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_015m1Vg2WEU8gwr56Artp8ak",
        "type":"tool_use"
      }],

        "text":"319d landed at **`db3fe67`**.\n\n## Recap\n\nIssue 319's headline feature — **runtime self-construction** — is now working end-to-end:\n\n| Sub-issue | Status | What ships |\n|-----------|--------|-----------|\n| 319a | ✓ | Dispatch holds boxes of any width |\n| 319b | ✓ | Slot store grows without moving slots |\n| 319c | ✓ | Box ids minted thread-safely |\n| **319d** | **✓ (slice 1)** | **Lua boxes can `create_box` + `connect` mid-run** |\n| 319e | next | C + Bash bindings + non-call kinds + docs |\n\nThe fixture proves the full path:\n\n```\ntrigger.lua calls soramech.create_box → gets \"auto_00000000\"\n            calls soramech.connect    → wires trigger → auto_00000000\n            returns \"trigger-fired:auto_00000000:hello-from-trigger\"\n            (dispatcher pushes through the new connection)\nauto_00000000 (newly created box) runs\n              returns \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_00000000:hello-from-trigger\"\n```\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nYou were right — I was scaring myself into diminution. The actual changes turned out smaller than I feared because every layer was already shaped right: the dispatch went through `graph_box()` accessors (so changing storage was invisible), the spec contract already had the `box_t *` parameter (so no signature change), and the per-slot lock pattern from 319b was directly reusable for connections. The \"compromise\" I almost made would have foregone the whole headline feature for the sake of avoiding work that turned out to be largely mechanical. **Believing it would work made it tractable.**\n\nThe documented limits in this slice (Lua only, call only, plain routing, 4096-box headroom, single-firing-box assumption for connect) are the right kind of \"ship and audit\" — each is a clear seam for a follow-on, not load-bearing for the feature itself.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nWant to do 319e next, or pause here?",
        "type":"text"
      }],

    "content":[{
        "text":"You're right and I made a wrong call. Let me think through it properly.\n\n## What I did\n\n`runtime_create_box` and `runtime_connect` are language-agnostic C functions in `src/018-runtime-builtins.c` — those are fine. But to make them *callable from user code*, I exposed them as **Lua functions** (`soramech.create_box`, `soramech.connect`) registered in `langs/lua/spec.c`. The plan for 319e was to repeat the same wrapping in `langs/c/spec.c` and `langs/bash/spec.c`.\n\nThat repetition-per-language is the smell you're spotting. Read boxes and write boxes don't get re-implemented per language — they're **box kinds** in the JSON schema, handled by the runtime itself (`do_write_box` in dispatch.c), and user code interacts with them by wiring data in and out.\n\n## What I should have done\n\nMake `create_box` and `connect` **new box kinds**, alongside `read` / `write` / `call` / `comparator` / `iterator`:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"spawn_step\", \"kind\": \"create_box\",\n  \"inputs\": [ { \"name\": \"spec\", \"type\": \"json\" } ],\n  \"connections\": [ ... wire the resulting id somewhere ... ] }\n\n{ \"id\": \"wire_it\",   \"kind\": \"connect\",\n  \"inputs\": [ { \"name\": \"from_box\", \"type\": \"string\" },\n              { \"name\": \"to_box\",   \"type\": \"string\" },\n              { \"name\": \"to_input\", \"type\": \"string\" } ] }\n```\n\nThen a Lua box (or C box, or Bash box) wanting to spawn a downstream pipeline just:\n1. Outputs a JSON spec on its wire\n2. The spec flows into a `create_box` kind box\n3. The `create_box` box outputs the new id\n4. The id flows wherever it's needed (probably into a `connect` box)\n\n**Same machinery for every language. Zero per-language bindings.** Matches the rest of SoraMech's \"the language spec writes data, the runtime moves data, special box kinds do special things\" model.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nWhy I drifted: when I asked \"how does user code invoke this?\" my brain went to \"expose a callback the spec wraps\" because that's the standard FFI pattern in C/Lua/etc. But SoraMech's primary FFI is **wires**, not function calls. The right question was \"what does this look like as a box?\" — same way `read` is the FFI for \"read file\" and `write` is the FFI for \"write file.\" `create_box` should be the FFI for \"create box.\" I skipped a step.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\n## Tradeoff to flag\n\nThere's one thing the box-kind model handles differently from the in-spec-callback model: **getting the new box's id back to the creator synchronously**. With Lua bindings, the planner calls `create_box(spec)` and gets the id on the next line. With box-kinds, the planner outputs a spec, fires once, and the id arrives back via a wire later (potentially in the next iteration).\n\nFor most use cases this is fine — the dataflow shape is natural and async anyway. For some patterns it's awkward, e.g. \"create N boxes in a loop and remember all their ids.\" But those patterns can still be expressed via iterator-style boxes or via batching the spec into an array, so I don't think it's load-bearing.\n\n## What to do about 319d\n\nThree options:\n\n1. **Revert the Lua binding bits of 319d, add `create_box` and `connect` as box kinds in a new sub-issue 319d.2.** Cleanest history. The runtime API + graph mutation infrastructure (the bulk of 319d) stays valuable; only the Lua wrapper layer comes out.\n2. **Leave 319d as-is and add box kinds in 319e (instead of C/Bash bindings).** Keeps the Lua bindings around as a \"fast path\" alongside the box-kind path. Two parallel mechanisms; clutter risk.\n3. **Amend 319d via a follow-up commit that removes the Lua bindings and adds box kinds.** Same end result as (1) but with the messier history of \"added then removed.\"\n\nI'd lean (1). The runtime mutation infrastructure I built (graph_add_box, box_add_connection, slot store growth, dispatch headroom, runtime-builtins.c) is all reusable for the box-kind implementation; only `langs/lua/spec.c`'s `soramech_*` functions and the TLS plumbing become unnecessary.\n\nWant me to do (1)? And does the tradeoff about sync-vs-async id-back-to-creator matter enough to add a \"fast path\" for it, or is async always fine?",
        "type":"text"
      }],
