    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/run-tests.sh",
    "newString":"check_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n\npipeline_output_check",
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

      "content":"local function list_dir_json(dir)\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. dir .. \"/*.json 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return {} end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    local files = {}\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        files[#files + 1] = path\n    end\n    return files\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ list_subdirs\nlocal function list_subdirs(dir)\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls -d \" .. dir .. \"/*/ 2>/dev/null\")\n    if not handle then return {} end\n    local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n    handle:close()\n    local names = {}\n    for path in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n        local name = path:match(\"/([^/]+)/$\")\n        if name then names[#names + 1] = name end\n    end\n    return names\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ safe_path\n-- Returns the resolved path if it is within root, nil otherwise.\n-- Prevents path traversal outside the maps root.\nlocal function safe_path(root, ...)\n    local parts = { root }\n    for _, p in ipairs({...}) do\n        -- reject any component containing \"..\"\n        if tostring(p):find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) then return nil end\n        parts[#parts + 1] = p\n    end\n    return table.concat(parts, \"/\")\nend"
    },
    "type":"text"
  },

      "content":"-- {{{ handle_list_extrasrc\n-- Returns [{index, label, path, files:[]}] for all src_dirs entries.\n-- src/ is no longer special — it is simply the first entry in src_dirs.\nlocal function handle_list_extrasrc(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name = req.parts[2]\n    local meta_path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"meta.json\")\n    if not meta_path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local meta = {}\n    local raw, _ = read_file(meta_path)\n    if raw then\n        local decoded, _, _ = json.decode(raw)\n        if decoded then meta = decoded end\n    end\n\n    local src_dirs = resolve_src_dirs(meta, maps_root, map_name)\n    local result = {}\n    for i, entry in ipairs(src_dirs) do\n        local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. entry.path .. \"/ 2>/dev/null\")\n        local files = {}\n        if handle then\n            local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n            handle:close()\n            for name in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n                if name ~= \"\" then files[#files + 1] = name end\n            end\n        end\n        local label = entry.path:match(\"([^/]+)$\") or entry.path\n        result[#result + 1] = {\n            index = i - 1, label = label,\n            path = entry.path, kind = entry.kind, files = files,\n        }\n    end\n    json_ok(client, result)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ handle_get_extrasrc\n-- Returns the raw text of a file from src_dirs[index].\nlocal function handle_get_extrasrc(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local dir_index = tonumber(req.parts[4])\n    local file_name = req.parts[5]\n    if not dir_index or not file_name then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"missing dir index or filename\")\n    end\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n"
    },
    "type":"text"

          "new_string":"-- {{{ handle_get_src\nlocal function handle_get_src(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"src\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ Translation file CRUD — issue 246\n-- Per-port custom translation shims live at\n--   maps/<name>/translations/<box_id>__<port_name>.<lang_ext>\n-- The handlers below read / write / list those files. Box JSON\n-- references them by relative path in the per-input\n-- `custom_translation` field; the editor uses these endpoints to\n-- create / inspect / replace the shim file contents.\n\n-- List translation files under maps/<name>/translations/.\n-- Returns an array of plain filenames; empty array if the dir\n-- doesn't exist yet (a brand-new map hasn't been forced to create\n-- the directory).\nlocal function handle_list_translations(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name = req.parts[2]\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. dir .. \"/ 2>/dev/null\")\n    local files = {}\n    if handle then\n        local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n        handle:close()\n        for name in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n            if name ~= \"\" then files[#files + 1] = name end\n        end\n    end\n    json_ok(client, files)\nend\n\n-- Read one translation file as plain text.\nlocal function handle_get_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n\n-- Write (create or overwrite) one translation file. Creates the\n-- translations/ directory on demand.\nlocal function handle_put_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    -- Make the directory; mkdir -p is idempotent so existing dirs\n    -- don't error.\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. dir)\n    local path = dir .. \"/\" .. file_name\n    local ok, werr = write_file_atomic(path, req.body or \"\")\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(werr)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true, path = path })\nend\n\n-- Delete a translation file outright. Distinct from the inspector's\n-- \"Delete\" affordance which only clears the box's reference — this\n-- is the file-browser-side hard delete.\nlocal function handle_delete_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    if not file_exists(path) then\n        return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"no such translation file\")\n    end\n    local ok, err = os.remove(path)\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(err)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true })\nend\n-- }}}"

Box JSON\n-- references them by relative path in the per-input\n-- `custom_translation` field; the editor uses these endpoints to\n-- create / inspect / replace the shim file contents.\n\n-- List translation files under maps/<name>/translations/.\n-- Returns an array of plain filenames; empty array if the dir\n-- doesn't exist yet (a brand-new map hasn't been forced to create\n-- the directory).\nlocal function handle_list_translations(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name = req.parts[2]\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local handle = io.popen(\"ls \" .. dir .. \"/ 2>/dev/null\")\n    local files = {}\n    if handle then\n        local listing = handle:read(\"*a\")\n        handle:close()\n        for name in listing:gmatch(\"[^\\n]+\") do\n            if name ~= \"\" then files[#files + 1] = name end\n        end\n    end\n    json_ok(client, files)\nend\n\n-- Read one translation file as plain text.\nlocal function handle_get_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    local raw, err = read_file(path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(err)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", raw, \"text/plain\")\nend\n\n-- Write (create or overwrite) one translation file. Creates the\n-- translations/ directory on demand.\nlocal function handle_put_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local dir = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\")\n    if not dir then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    -- Make the directory; mkdir -p is idempotent so existing dirs\n    -- don't error.\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. dir)\n    local path = dir .. \"/\" .. file_name\n    local ok, werr = write_file_atomic(path, req.body or \"\")\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(werr)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true, path = path })\nend\n\n-- Delete a translation file outright. Distinct from the inspector's\n-- \"Delete\" affordance which only clears the box's reference — this\n-- is the file-browser-side hard delete.\nlocal function handle_delete_translation(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local file_name = req.parts[4]\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n    local path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"translations\", file_name)\n    if not path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n    if not file_exists(path) then\n        return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"no such translation file\")\n    end\n    local ok, err = os.remove(path)\n    if not ok then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", tostring(err)) end\n    json_ok(client, { ok = true })\nend\n-- }}}",

Port names come from the parsed\n        // function signature (file browser populates them); editing\n        // them in the inspector is gone — the original 208 rationale\n        // (prevent typo drift between source and box JSON) holds, and\n        // post-fact rename was just a user tag anyway.\n        const name_el = document.createElement('span');\n        name_el.className   = 'port-name-display';\n        name_el.textContent = p.name || '';\n        top_row.appendChild(name_el);\n\n        if (p.type && p.type !== 'any') {\n          const type_el = document.createElement('span');\n          type_el.className   = 'port-type';\n          type_el.textContent = ':' + p.type;\n          top_row.appendChild(type_el);\n        }\n\n        // Variadic control button. Three states:\n        //   1. Plain port — \"var\" toggle turns it on\n        //   2. First slot of a variadic group — \"var ×\" collapses back\n        //   3. Non-first slot — \"×\" removes that slot\n        const btn_style = 'background:none;border:1px solid #2a2f45;border-radius:3px;' +\n          'color:#6c72a0;cursor:pointer;font-family:monospace;font-size:9px;' +\n          'padding:1px 5px;line-height:1.4;';\n\n        if (!in_var_group) {\n          // Issue 217 part C: the var toggle is offered when the box's\n          // language declares `variadic_shape: 'positional'`. Until\n          // the spec is loaded we default to \"offered\" (every shipped\n          // language is positional) so the first render of a box\n          // doesn't lose the button. Already-variadic groups keep\n          // their collapse + remove controls regardless, so flipping\n          // a language to 'none' later can't trap an existing group.\n          const spec          = spec_for_box(current_box);\n          const var_supported = !spec || spec.variadic_shape === 'positional';\n          if (var_supported) {\n            const var_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            var_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n            var_btn.textContent   = 'var';\n            var_btn.title         = 'mark this input as variadic (grows to N slots)';\n            var_btn.onclick       = () => make_variadic(p.name);\n            top_row.appendChild(var_btn);\n          }\n        } else if (pv.index === 0) {\n          const var_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          var_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#4a9eff;color:#4a9eff;';\n          var_btn.textContent   = 'var ×';\n          var_btn.title         = 'collapse back to a single non-variadic input';\n          var_btn.onclick       = () => unmake_variadic(pv.base);\n          top_row.appendChild(var_btn);\n        } else {\n          const x_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          x_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n          x_btn.textContent   = '×';\n          x_btn.title         = 'remove this slot';\n          x_btn.onclick       = () => remove_variadic_slot(p.name);"
    },
    "type":"text"
  },

      "content":"  // {{{ open_source_view\n  // Public entry point. Fetches the source for `ref` and opens a floating\n  // window. If `anchor_box` is given, the window is centered over that\n  // box's screen position; otherwise it's centered on the canvas.\n  async function open_source_view(ref, anchor_box) {\n    let text;\n    try {\n      text = await fetch_source(ref);\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('view source: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const win  = make_window(ref, text);\n    const size = default_size(text);\n\n    document.body.appendChild(win);\n    win.style.width  = size.w + 'px';\n    win.style.height = size.h + 'px';\n\n    // Default position: centered over anchor_box (if provided) or canvas.\n    const cr = canvas_rect();\n    let cand_left, cand_top;\n    if (anchor_box && anchor_box.ui) {\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(anchor_box.ui.x + Boxes.BOX_W / 2,\n                                       anchor_box.ui.y + Boxes.box_height(anchor_box) / 2);\n      cand_left = cr.left + s.x - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + s.y - size.h / 2;\n    } else {\n      cand_left = cr.left + cr.width  / 2 - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + cr.height / 2 - size.h / 2;\n    }\n    const clamped = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, size.w, size.h);\n    win.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n    win.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n\n    bring_to_front(win);\n    open_windows.push(win);\n  }\n  // }}}"

          "new_string":"  // {{{ put_data\n  async function put_data(filename, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ Translation file CRUD — issue 246\n  // Translation files (per-port custom translation shims) live under\n  // maps/<name>/translations/. The inspector creates them via \"New\"\n  // (PUT), views them via \"View\" (GET), and the file browser can\n  // delete them outright (DELETE). The inspector's own delete\n  // affordance only clears the box's `custom_translation` field — it\n  // does not call delete_translation.\n  async function list_translations() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/translations`);\n  }\n  async function get_translation(filename) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/translations/${filename}`);\n  }\n  async function put_translation(filename, content) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/translations/${filename}`, content);\n  }\n  async function delete_translation(filename) {\n    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/translations/${filename}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { init, list_maps, list_boxes, get_box, put_box, delete_box,\n           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data,\n           list_src_files, get_src_file,\n           list_extra_src, get_extra_src_file,\n           list_translations, get_translation, put_translation, delete_translation,\n           list_dirs };"

          "old_string":"        // `opt` toggle (issue 230). Flips port.optional between true\n        // and undefined (absent = false). An optional port doesn't\n        // require a wire or literal — the compile-time check from\n        // 230 allows it through. Amber styling so it reads as a\n        // different category from the blue `var` family.\n        const opt_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        const opt_on  = ports[i].optional === true;\n        opt_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + (opt_on\n          ? 'border-color:#d4762a;color:#d4762a;'\n          : '');\n        opt_btn.textContent = 'opt';\n        opt_btn.title       = 'mark this input as optional — the box runs even if unwired';\n        opt_btn.onclick     = () => {\n          ports[i].optional = opt_on ? undefined : true;\n          save();\n          show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        };\n        top_row.appendChild(opt_btn);\n\n        block.appendChild(top_row);",
          "new_string":"        // `opt` toggle (issue 230). Flips port.optional between true\n        // and undefined (absent = false). An optional port doesn't\n        // require a wire or literal — the compile-time check from\n        // 230 allows it through. Amber styling so it reads as a\n        // different category from the blue `var` family.\n        const opt_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        const opt_on  = ports[i].optional === true;\n        opt_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + (opt_on\n          ? 'border-color:#d4762a;color:#d4762a;'\n          : '');\n        opt_btn.textContent = 'opt';\n        opt_btn.title       = 'mark this input as optional — the box runs even if unwired';\n        opt_btn.onclick     = () => {\n          ports[i].optional = opt_on ? undefined : true;\n          save();\n          show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n        };\n        top_row.appendChild(opt_btn);\n\n        // {{{ Custom translation shim affordance (issue 246)\n        // Three states:\n        //   - no custom_translation: \"+xlate\" button — creates a\n        //     default shim file matching the box's language and\n        //     sets the port's custom_translation field.\n        //   - custom_translation set: \"xlate\" button opens the shim\n        //     in the source-view window; small \"×\" clears the field\n        //     (file stays on disk per the issue's delete rule).\n        // Suppressed entirely when the box has no language (read /\n        // data / write boxes — shims only make sense on call boxes\n        // whose spec runs the translate callback). */\n        if (current_box && current_box.kind === 'call' && current_box.lang) {\n          const has_shim = !!ports[i].custom_translation;\n          if (!has_shim) {\n            const new_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            new_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n            new_btn.textContent   = '+xlate';\n            new_btn.title         = 'add a per-port custom translation shim (issue 246)';\n            new_btn.onclick       = () => create_shim_for(ports[i]);\n            top_row.appendChild(new_btn);\n          } else {\n            const view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            view_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#e8a317;color:#e8a317;';\n            view_btn.textContent   = 'xlate';\n            view_btn.title         = 'view shim: ' + ports[i].custom_translation;\n            view_btn.onclick       = () =>\n              SourceView.open_source_view(ports[i].custom_translation, current_box);\n            top_row.appendChild(view_btn);\n\n            const clr_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            clr_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#e8a317;color:#e8a317;';\n            clr_btn.textContent   = '×';\n            clr_btn.title         = 'clear shim reference (file stays on disk)';\n            clr_btn.onclick       = () => {\n              ports[i].custom_translation = undefined;\n              save();\n              show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n            };\n            top_row.appendChild(clr_btn);\n          }\n        }\n        // }}}\n\n        block.appendChild(top_row);"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"

    "newString":"  // {{{ create_shim_for — issue 246\n  // Creates a per-port custom translation file with default-spec-\n  // equivalent content (identity pass-through) and sets the port's\n  // `custom_translation` field on the current box. The filename\n  // convention matches issue 246: <box_id>__<port_name>.<lang_ext>.\n  function shim_default_content(lang) {\n    if (lang === 'lua') {\n      return [\n        '-- Per-port custom translation shim (issue 246).',\n        '-- The file returns a single function taking the raw bytes',\n        '-- and a \"raw_native\" flag (true if the bytes came from a',\n        '-- same-language producer, false if from a cross-language',\n        '-- producer via JSON).     "newString":"if [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Issue 246 — per-port custom translation shims. Box JSONs reference\n# them by relative path under translations/; the runtime resolves\n# the path relative to the compiled map dir at dispatch time.\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/translations\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/translations\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/translations/.\" \"$COMPILED/translations/\"\nfi",
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/soramech-compile.sh — produce a self-contained compiled map.\n#\n# What it does, in CEO terms: takes a SoraMech map directory, walks\n# every box file to find the languages and source files it uses,\n# copies everything into a `compiled/` subdirectory alongside the\n# language spec.so plugins and the pool runner binary, and stamps a\n# manifest. The resulting directory is portable — copy or symlink it\n# anywhere on the same machine and it runs the map standalone.\n#\n# Layout produced under <map>/compiled/:\n#   meta.json, boxes/, src/, data/  — verbatim copies from the map\n#   langs/<lang>/spec.so            — copies of the language plugins\n#                                     that the map actually uses\n#   langs/bash/bash-server.sh       — only if bash boxes are present\n#   bin/<box>.so                    — pre-compiled C boxes (informational;\n#                                     the runner still lazy-compiles\n#                                     from src/ but having them here\n#                                     means you can verify the compile\n#                                     step worked without running)\n#   pool-runner                     — symlink to soramech-pool\n#   manifest.json                   — summary stats\n#\n# Run as:\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir>\n#   scripts/soramech-compile.sh <map-dir> --dir <project-root>\n#\n# Convention: scripts run from any directory via a hard-coded ${DIR}\n# path with an override argument; all paths relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\n# {{{ defaults\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nMAP=\"\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ argv parse — map first, --dir <path> optional\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --dir)\n            DIR=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        --help|-h)\n            grep '^#' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\?//'\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            if [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n                MAP=\"$1\"\n            else\n                echo \"soramech-compile: unexpected argument '$1'\" >&2\n                exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\nif [[ -z \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"usage: soramech-compile <map-dir> [--dir <project-root>]\" >&2\n    exit 2\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ resolve paths & sanity-check\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: not a directory: $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nMAP=$(cd \"$MAP\" && pwd)\nif [[ ! -f \"$MAP/meta.json\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing meta.json in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -d \"$MAP/boxes\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: missing boxes/ in $MAP\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\nif [[ ! -x \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: pool runner not built at $DIR/soramech-pool\" >&2\n    echo \"  run 'make' in $DIR first\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nCOMPILED=\"$MAP/compiled\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ box_field — pull a top-level string field from a box JSON file\n# Tolerant of whitespace; returns empty string if the field is missing.\n# We don't have jq in-tree, so a regex over the small box files is\n# fine. Box JSON is hand-written and shallow.\nbox_field() {\n    local file=\"$1\"\n    local field=\"$2\"\n    grep -o \"\\\"$field\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"\" \"$file\" \\\n        | head -n1 \\\n        | sed 's/.*\"\\([^\"]*\\)\"$/\\1/'\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ wipe & lay out the compiled directory\nrm -rf \"$COMPILED\"\nmkdir -p \"$COMPILED\" \"$COMPILED/boxes\" \"$COMPILED/src\" \"$COMPILED/bin\" \"$COMPILED/langs\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy verbatim assets (meta, boxes, src, data, *.txt)\ncp \"$MAP/meta.json\" \"$COMPILED/meta.json\"\ncp -r \"$MAP/boxes/.\" \"$COMPILED/boxes/\"\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/src\" ]]; then\n    cp -r \"$MAP/src/.\" \"$COMPILED/src/\"\nfi\n\nif [[ -d \"$MAP/data\" ]]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/data\"\n    cp -r \"$MAP/data/.\" \"$COMPILED/data/\"\nfi\n\n# Top-level data files (input.txt, names.txt, etc) — the runner\n# resolves file_write/data refs relative to the map root.\nshopt -s nullglob\nfor f in \"$MAP\"/*.txt; do\n    cp \"$f\" \"$COMPILED/\"\ndone\nshopt -u nullglob\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ enumerate the set of languages the map actually uses\n# A box file is in compiled/boxes/. We read `lang` from each.\nLANGS=()\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ -z \"$lang\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    seen=0\n    for known in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$known\" == \"$lang\" ]]; then seen=1; break; fi\n    done\n    if [[ $seen -eq 0 ]]; then\n        LANGS+=(\"$lang\")\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy spec.so for each used language\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    src_spec=\"$DIR/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_spec\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: missing spec.so for language '$lang'\" >&2\n        echo \"  expected at $src_spec — run 'make' in $DIR\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    mkdir -p \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang\"\n    cp \"$src_spec\" \"$COMPILED/langs/$lang/spec.so\"\n    # Bash spec needs its companion server script for runtime.\n    if [[ \"$lang\" == \"bash\" ]] && [[ -f \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" ]]; then\n        cp \"$DIR/langs/bash/bash-server.sh\" \"$COMPILED/langs/bash/\"\n    fi\ndone\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ merge_lua_sources — concatenate all Lua source files into one\n# merged module (issue 313). Each per-file module is wrapped in its\n# own closure so the file's `local` declarations stay file-scoped,\n# and exported under the source file's basename. The Lua spec\n# detects the merged file at init and loads it once per worker\n# instead of per-file lazy-loading every box's ref. The original\n# files stay in src/ unchanged so the existing per-file path still\n# works for callers that haven't been told about the merge.\nmerge_lua_sources() {\n    local out=\"$COMPILED/src/__merged__.lua\"\n    shopt -s nullglob\n    local files=(\"$COMPILED/src\"/*.lua)\n    shopt -u nullglob\n    if [[ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then return; fi\n\n    {\n        echo \"-- soramech merged Lua module (issue 313)\"\n        echo \"-- Generated by soramech-compile.sh; do not hand-edit.\"\n        echo \"-- Each per-file module wraps in its own closure and is\"\n        echo \"-- exported under the source file's basename, so two\"\n        echo \"-- files can both define a local M without colliding.\"\n        echo \"\"\n        echo \"local merged = {}\"\n        echo \"\"\n        local f base\n        for f in \"${files[@]}\"; do\n            base=$(basename \"$f\" .lua)\n            if [[ \"$base\" == \"__merged__\" ]]; then continue; fi\n            echo \"-- {{{ from $(basename \"$f\")\"\n            echo \"merged[\\\"$base\\\"] = (function()\"\n            cat \"$f\"\n            echo \"\"\n            echo \"end)()\"\n            echo \"-- }}}\"\n            echo \"\"\n        done\n        echo \"return merged\"\n    } > \"$out\"\n}\nmerge_lua_sources\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pre-compile C boxes into compiled/bin/\n# The runner already lazy-compiles .c → .so on first invoke, so this\n# step is purely informational: it surfaces compile errors at compile\n# time rather than at run time, and produces artifacts the user can\n# inspect or distribute alongside the source.\nn_c_compiled=0\nn_c_failed=0\nfor box in \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json; do\n    box_lang=$(box_field \"$box\" lang)\n    if [[ \"$box_lang\" != \"c\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    ref=$(box_field \"$box\" ref)\n    if [[ -z \"$ref\" ]]; then continue; fi\n    src_path=\"$COMPILED/$ref\"\n    if [[ ! -f \"$src_path\" ]]; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: C box source missing: $ref\" >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    base=$(basename \"$ref\" .c)\n    out=\"$COMPILED/bin/$base.so\"\n    if ! gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -o \"$out\" \"$src_path\" 2>/tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log; then\n        echo \"soramech-compile: gcc failed for $ref:\" >&2\n        cat /tmp/soramech-compile-cc.log >&2\n        n_c_failed=$((n_c_failed + 1))\n        continue\n    fi\n    n_c_compiled=$((n_c_compiled + 1))\ndone\n\nif [[ $n_c_failed -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo \"soramech-compile: $n_c_failed C box(es) failed to compile\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ copy the pool runner into the compiled directory\n# A real copy (not a symlink) is intentional: the runner discovers\n# its sibling langs/ via /proc/self/exe, which follows symlinks to\n# their canonical target. A symlinked pool-runner would resolve back\n# to the project tree and pick up the project's langs/ instead of\n# the bundled compiled/langs/. Copying keeps the compiled artifact\n# self-describing and portable.\ncp \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\nchmod +x \"$COMPILED/pool-runner\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ write manifest.json\n# Hand-rolled JSON (no jq) keeps the script self-contained. The\n# fields are stable enough to grep against in tests.\nn_boxes=$(ls -1 \"$COMPILED\"/boxes/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\nn_langs=${#LANGS[@]}\nlangs_json=\"\"\nfirst=1\nfor lang in \"${LANGS[@]+\"${LANGS[@]}\"}\"; do\n    if [[ $first -eq 1 ]]; then\n        langs_json=\"\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n        first=0\n    else\n        langs_json+=\",\\\"$lang\\\"\"\n    fi\ndone\ncompiled_at=$(date -Iseconds 2>/dev/null || date)\nmap_name=$(basename \"$MAP\")\n\ncat > \"$COMPILED/manifest.json\" <<EOF\n{\n    \"name\": \"$map_name\",\n    \"compiled_at\": \"$compiled_at\",\n    \"n_boxes\": $n_boxes,\n    \"n_languages\": $n_langs,\n    \"languages\": [$langs_json],\n    \"c_boxes_precompiled\": $n_c_compiled,\n    \"source_map_dir\": \"$MAP\"\n}\nEOF\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ summary line\necho \"compiled $map_name → $COMPILED\"\necho \"  boxes:       $n_boxes\"\necho \"  languages:   $n_langs (${LANGS[*]+${LANGS[*]}})\"\necho \"  c precompiled: $n_c_compiled\"\necho\necho \"run with:\"\necho \"  $COMPILED/pool-runner $COMPILED\"\n# }}}\n",
    "replaceAll":false,

          "old_string":"# 246 — Custom translation specs per input port\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Concept",
          "new_string":"# 246 — Custom translation specs per input port\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nPer-port custom translation shims are live for Lua and C boxes:\n\n- The box JSON schema gains an optional per-input\n  `custom_translation` field that names a file under\n  `translations/<file>` relative to the map dir. Absence means\n  \"use the default decode for this port.\"\n- The graph loader (`src/010-graph-loader.{h,c}`) reads the\n  field onto `input_decl_t->custom_translation`.\n- The language spec interface (`langs/lang-spec.h`) grows a\n  `translate` callback that takes `(handle, shim_path, raw,\n  raw_size, raw_native, out_buf, out_capacity, out_size)`.\n- Lua's spec (`langs/lua/spec.c`) implements `lua_translate`:\n  loads the shim file expecting it to return a function, caches\n  the function reference per-worker in the Lua registry under\n  `LUA_SHIM_CACHE_KEY`, calls it with `(raw, raw_native)` and\n  returns the result.\n- C's spec (`langs/c/spec.c`) implements `c_translate`:\n  lazy-compiles the shim .c to .so via the existing\n  `maybe_lazy_compile` + `get_or_load` infrastructure, dlsym's\n  `sm_translate`, and calls it.\n- Bash's spec doesn't implement `translate` (its protocol needs\n  extension; deferred per the 319e/Bash pattern).\n- Dispatch (`src/012-dispatch.c`) walks each box's inputs after\n  `read_inputs`; for any port with a `custom_translation` it\n  routes the raw bytes through `spec->translate`, allocates an\n  output buffer from the unified allocator, replaces the per-port\n  data/size, and sets `input_native[i] = 1` so the spec's invoke\n  sees the translated bytes as native.\n- The HTTP backend (`src/005-http-server.lua`) gains four routes:\n  `GET /maps/<name>/translations` (list),\n  `GET /maps/<name>/translations/<file>` (read),\n  `PUT /maps/<name>/translations/<file>` (write — used by the\n  inspector's \"+xlate\" affordance to create with default content),\n  `DELETE /maps/<name>/translations/<file>` (hard delete — used\n  by the file browser, not by the inspector).\n- The editor's `API` module (`assets/js/003-api.js`) exposes\n  `list_translations` / `get_translation` / `put_translation` /\n  `delete_translation`.\n- The inspector (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`) grows three button\n  states per input port row on call boxes:\n  - **`+xlate`** (no shim) — creates a default shim file with\n    identity pass-through content matching the box's language\n    and sets `port.custom_translation`.\n  - **`xlate`** (shim present) — opens the shim in the\n    source-view window.\n  - **`×`** (shim present) — clears the box's reference to the\n    shim (file stays on disk per the issue's delete rule).\n- The source-view (`assets/js/008-source-view.js`) detects\n  `translations/` paths and routes to `API.get_translation` so\n  the `xlate` view button works.\n- The wire-color module (`assets/js/006-wires.js`, from issue\n  245) already paints shim-port wires in goldenrod because it\n  detects `port.custom_translation`.\n- The compile pipeline (`scripts/soramech-compile.sh`) copies\n  `translations/` from the map into the compiled artifact so\n  shims survive packaging.\n- The runtime self-construction path (`src/018-runtime-builtins.c`)\n  reads `custom_translation` from spec JSON in\n  `runtime_create_box`, so dynamically-created boxes can carry\n  shims too.\n\n## Validation\n\nTwo integration test fixtures pass end-to-end:\n\n- `tests/maps/246-c-shim/` — a C box whose `msg` port has a\n  shim that uppercases the input. Expected output\n  `seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED` confirms the shim ran before the\n  box's `echo` function.\n- `tests/maps/246-lua-shim/` — a Lua box whose `msg` port has\n  a shim that reverses the input and prepends `REV-`. Expected\n  output `seen:REV-fedcba` confirms the same on the Lua side.\n\nAll 16 integration tests pass. The slot store's 23 unit tests\nstill pass.\n\n## Deferred\n\n- **Bash spec `translate`** — the bash server's line protocol\n  needs extension to route shim invocation back to the C\n  runtime. Same shape of follow-on as the 319e Bash deferral.\n- **Compile-time validation** of `custom_translation` paths —\n  per the issue's open questions, easy add when the feature\n  matures.\n- **Default-content generators that match the port's declared\n  type more closely** — the current default is identity\n  pass-through. Type-aware decoders (e.g. JSON-parse for\n  `type: \"json\"` inputs) are an enhancement.\n- **Box-delete confirmation when ports have shims** — the\n  current delete path doesn't warn. Easy add when needed; the\n  files staying on disk regardless means data isn't lost,\n  the user just loses the reference.\n\n## Concept"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01Q7apSavWepWgneX3ACiS67",
        "type":"tool_use"
      }]

}

The file runs at the start of\nthe consumer's task and replaces the default decode for THAT\nport — other ports keep the default path. It earns its keep on\ninputs where the default JSON-or-native pass-through doesn't\nknow what the user means: a void* carrying a specific handle, a\nunion whose tag is on a sibling port, a number the consumer\nwants clamped, units the user wants normalised on one port but\nnot another.\n\nThe runtime shape. The graph loader reads an optional\n`custom_translation` field per input port. The language-spec\ninterface grows a `translate` callback that takes the raw bytes\nand a \"was this native\" flag and writes native bytes the spec's\ninvoke then sees. Lua's translate loads the file once per worker\n(caching the returned function in the Lua registry) and calls\nit. C's translate lazy-compiles + dlopens the shim .c, dlsyms\n`sm_translate`, and calls it. Dispatch walks the inputs after\nread_inputs; ports with a shim route through, ports without\nproceed as before.\n\nThe editor side. Inspector input-port rows on call boxes grow\nthree states: `+xlate` to create a default shim file matching\nthe box's language (identity pass-through, user edits in place),\n`xlate` to open the shim in the source-view window, and `×` to\nclear the box's reference (file stays on disk per the issue's\ndelete rule). The source-view detects translations/ paths and\nroutes to a new translation-file endpoint. The HTTP backend\ngrows list / get / put / delete routes for files under\nmaps/<name>/translations/. The wire-color module from 245\nalready paints shim-port wires in goldenrod because it\nchecks port.custom_translation — no change there.\n\nThe compile pipeline copies translations/ into the compiled\nartifact. The runtime self-construction path (319d's\ncreate_box) reads custom_translation from spec JSON, so\ndynamically-created boxes can carry shims too.\n\nTwo end-to-end fixtures verify the path. A C box with an\nuppercase shim emits `seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED` from input\n`hello-from-seed`. A Lua box with a reverse+prepend shim emits\n`seen:REV-fedcba` from input `abcdef`. 16 integration tests\nnow pass.\n\nDeferred per the issue file: Bash spec's translate callback\n(needs the bash server line protocol extended back to the C\nruntime, same shape as the 319e Bash deferral); compile-time\nvalidation that every referenced translation file exists; type-\naware default-content generators; the box-delete-confirmation\nflow.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5"
        },

        "text":"246 landed at `981b2b8`.\n\n## What shipped\n\n| Layer | Change |\n|-------|--------|\n| Schema | `input_decl_t.custom_translation` (optional path) |\n| Graph loader | parses the field |\n| Spec interface | new `translate` callback in `lang_spec_t` |\n| Lua spec | `lua_translate` — loads file once per worker, caches via Lua registry, calls `(raw, raw_native)` |\n| C spec | `c_translate` — lazy-compile + dlsym `sm_translate` |\n| Bash spec | translate left NULL (deferred — needs protocol extension) |\n| Dispatch | per-port branch routes through shim, replaces data/size, sets `input_native=1` |\n| Runtime self-construction | `runtime_create_box` accepts `custom_translation` in spec JSON |\n| HTTP backend | 4 routes: list/get/put/delete translation files |\n| Editor API | `list/get/put/delete_translation` |\n| Editor inspector | per-port `+xlate` / `xlate` / `×` buttons |\n| Source view | routes `translations/` paths to the new endpoint |\n| Compile pipeline | copies `translations/` into compiled artifact |\n| Tests | C shim fixture + Lua shim fixture, both passing |\n\n**16 integration tests pass.** Both end-to-end shim fixtures (C uppercase shim, Lua reverse+prepend shim) demonstrate the runtime → spec → translate → invoke chain working.\n\n`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\nThe 245 wire-color change from earlier was forward-compatible — it already painted goldenrod when `port.custom_translation` was set, even though no path yet wrote that field. Today the field gets written and the color comes alive automatically. That's the value of building visual signals around fields rather than around events: when the field appears, the signal turns on for free.\n\nThe Bash deferral pattern is becoming the project's recognizable shape — same shape as 319e. The bash spec gets a follow-on slice once the line-protocol extension lands; everything else ships now. That's a tidy seam.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nWhat's next? The remaining untracked issues are **247** (debug build + per-box stats lens), **249** (tap input mode with radial ports), **318** (sentinel primitives in JSON), and the deferred work pile from 319/246 (Bash bindings, exporter rewrite, box-kind refactor for create_box/connect).",

      }]

{
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"bdde754f-7b71-47e1-a225-c5b07684f794",

  "sessionId":"1228a221-1c09-4c26-94f3-172d7777b2b9",

  "promptId":"61ac4e23-446f-4a9b-9e30-d7abebde46b0",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "noOutputExpected":false,
    "stdout":"# 318 — Sentinel primitives in the cross-language JSON wire\n\n## Status\nopen — **amended 2026-05-22** to replace the in-process-FFI\n`$function_pointer` reconstruction path with a\nwrapper-binary + persistent-subprocess design. See the\nAmendment section below; the original FFI-based reconstruction\ntext in the body is retained for context but is no longer the\ntarget.\n\n## Amendment (2026-05-22) — function pointers via wrapper binaries, not FFI\n\nThe original design had the consumer's spec reconstruct a\n`$function_pointer` by FFI-casting the raw process-local\naddress (LuaJIT's `ffi.cast`, ctypes, etc.). That path is\nlanguage-pair-specific by nature: it only works for languages\nthat ship an FFI binding to the target language's ABI, which\nbiases SoraMech toward the Lua↔C corner and leaves Bash and\nany future agnostic language out in the cold. SoraMech's\ncross-language story must be agnostic — N spec implementations,\nnot N² pair-wise paths — so FFI reconstruction is the wrong\nshape.\n\n**The replacement design:**\n\n1. **At map-compile time**, when the compiler sees a\n   `$function_pointer`-shaped wire crossing a language\n   boundary, it asks the *producing* spec to compile the\n   referenced function (and its enumerable dependencies) into\n   a standalone binary on disk. The binary speaks a small\n   request/response protocol over stdin/stdout or, when\n   performance matters, a Unix domain socket the runtime\n   spawned at startup.\n2. **The compiler then asks the *consuming* spec for a\n   wrapper recipe**: \"in your language, how do I invoke a\n   subprocess with these arguments and parse the response?\"\n   Every language can answer that question — Lua via\n   `io.popen` / `socket.connect`, C via `execve` /\n   `socket(2)`, Bash via literal `$(./bin args)` or\n   `socat` / `nc`. The consuming spec stamps a wrapper\n   function on disk (or inlines it into the merged module\n   per issue 313) that the consumer's source can call as if\n   the foreign function were local.\n3. **The `$function_pointer` sentinel's payload becomes**:\n\n   ```json\n   {\"$function_pointer\": {\"binary\": \"compiled/cross-lang/<box>__<port>.bin\",\n                          \"signature\": \"int(int,int)\",\n                          \"socket\":    \"compiled/cross-lang/<box>__<port>.sock\"}}\n   ```\n\n   The `socket` field is present when the runtime started the\n   binary as a long-lived subprocess and routes calls through\n   the socket; absent when the binary is spawned per call\n   (the cheap-and-stateless fallback).\n\n4. **State preservation comes from the persistent subprocess.**\n   The threading roadmap already commits to Unix domain\n   sockets for cross-language IPC; the same mechanism is what\n   makes long-lived foreign functions work. Each cross-language\n   function pointer used by a running map gets one subprocess\n   spawned at map start (or first use), and the wrapper does\n   socket round-trips per call. Latency: tens of microseconds,\n   not the millisecond cost of fork+exec. Closure state,\n   loaded models, cached connections — all survive between\n   calls in the subprocess's own memory.\n\n5. **Argument enumeration is the user's responsibility at\n   map-compile time.** Dynamic-language closures capture\n   upvalues (Lua) and `_ENV` (Lua) and lexical scope (most);\n   statically enumerating those is the FFI problem under\n   another name. The map compiler walks what it can — declared\n   inputs and statically reachable references — and fails the\n   compile with a clear error if the function pointer's\n   closure can't be enumerated. Honest failure mode.\n\n### New spec responsibility: foreign-call wrappers\n\nThis adds one responsibility to `lang_spec_t`. Each spec\nprovides a function that emits a wrapper in its own language\ngiven a foreign-call protocol descriptor:\n\n```c\nint (*emit_foreign_call_wrapper)(void *handle,\n                                 const char *binary_path,\n                                 const char *socket_path_or_null,\n                                 const char *signature,\n                                 const char *out_wrapper_src_path);\n```\n\n- For Lua: writes a `.lua` file containing a function that\n  opens the socket (or popen's the binary) and round-trips\n  arguments / response.\n- For C: writes a `.c` file with the same logic, compiled\n  alongside the rest of the C-side merged module.\n- For Bash: writes a function definition that wraps a\n  `socat`-or-`nc`-or-`./bin` call.\n\nThe wrapper-recipe is the *only* per-language code the\nforeign-call story needs. The binaries themselves are produced\nby the producing spec's existing `compile` function. The\nprotocol on the wire is a single shared definition — not\nper-language — so the consuming spec doesn't need to know what\nlanguage wrote the binary.\n\n### What this leaves of the original sentinel design\n\nThe two other sentinels survive unchanged:\n\n- **`$ref`** — pointer + length into the large-value heap; same\n  in-process semantics as before, same cross-process inlining\n  at the UDS marshaller.\n- **`$lang_opaque`** — still a \"this language's private value,\n  consumer either understands or fails compile\" sentinel; the\n  fail-compile path stays the default.\n\n`$function_pointer`'s wire shape stays the same JSON-object\nform; only the reconstruction recipe changes. Specs that used\nto publish \"I can reconstruct `$function_pointer` via FFI\" in\ntheir capability declaration now publish \"I can emit a\nforeign-call wrapper\" instead — same capability slot, different\nmeaning.\n\n### Why agnostic wins here\n\nLuaJIT FFI is fast and would have been the easy path for\nLua↔C. But locking SoraMech's wire format to LuaJIT's ABI\nexpectations would (a) tie the project to one specific Lua\nimplementation, (b) leave Bash with no `$function_pointer`\nreconstruction at all, (c) require every future language we\nadd to either ship an FFI binding or be a second-class\ncitizen, and (d) make windows / non-POSIX targets harder than\nthey need to be. Subprocess-and-socket is slower per call than\nFFI but it works everywhere, for every language, today, and\non every OS that speaks sockets. The cost is real but bounded;\nthe agnosticism is structural and worth more.\n\n## Concept\n\nJSON's structure covers six kinds of value cleanly — object,\narray, number, string, bool, null — and the cross-language ring\nin the dual-ring slot (issue 312) carries JSON for any wire that\ncrosses a language boundary. The structural cases that don't fit\nthose six kinds — Lua closures, libcurl handles, C++ class\ninstances, file handles, function pointers, large byte buffers\nwhere serialization would be expensive — need somewhere to live\nin the JSON ring without forcing the wire format to grow new\ntop-level shapes.\n\n**Sentinel primitives** are JSON object shapes with reserved key\nnames that mean \"this isn't a structural value, it's a reference\nto something the consumer must reconstruct using language-specific\nmachinery.\"\n\nThree kinds, each solving a different structural gap:\n\n```json\n{\"$ref\":              {\"ptr\": \"0x...\",  \"len\": 1048576,\n                       \"type\": \"bytes\"}}\n{\"$function_pointer\": {\"addr\": \"0x...\", \"signature\": \"int(void*,void*)\"}}\n{\"$lang_opaque\":      {\"lang\": \"lua\",   \"tag\": 12345,\n                       \"shape\": \"coroutine\"}}\n```\n\nSentinels are **emitted by the producer's spec** when its language\nhas a value JSON can't represent structurally. They are\n**reconstructed by the consumer's spec** using whatever runtime\nmachinery that language provides (LuaJIT FFI, ctypes for Python,\ndirect cast for C, etc.). Wires whose consumer cannot reconstruct\na sentinel kind **fail at compile time** — the editor catches the\nmismatch when the user wires a function-pointer output into a\nBash input.\n\n## Why these three, not more\n\nThe three sentinels carve up the structural gap by ownership:\n\n- **`$ref`** — bytes in a shared heap. The producer wrote the\n  bytes to the large-value heap (issue 302 / `src/015-large-value-heap.c`)\n  and emits a pointer-and-length reference. The bytes are\n  immutable for the wire's lifetime; refcount tracks consumers.\n  Solves: \"I have a megabyte to share; copying it through the\n  slot would be wasteful.\"\n- **`$function_pointer`** — a callable, identified by a raw\n  address and a signature interpretable in C-function-pointer\n  syntax. The address is process-local. The signature is the\n  contract between producer and consumer. Solves: \"I have a\n  function I want my consumer to be able to call directly.\"\n- **`$lang_opaque`** — a language-private value. The producer\n  tags it with the language name and a worker-private reference\n  the producer's spec can resolve back. Solves: \"I have a value\n  with no general structural representation; only my own\n  language knows what it is.\"\n\nAnything that doesn't fit one of the three either (a) has a\nJSON-structural representation and shouldn't be a sentinel, or\n(b) is genuinely unrepresentable and the wire is wrong, not the\nformat.\n\n## Producer protocol\n\nEach language spec's `native_to_json` walks its native values and\nemits the appropriate sentinel when it encounters a non-structural\nvalue. The spec author writes the emit logic; it's not generic.\n\n### Lua\n\n`encode_value` in `langs/lua/spec.c:188` currently hard-errors on\nfunction / userdata / thread / lightuserdata. The extension:\n\n- **Function** (`LUA_TFUNCTION`) — if the function is a C function\n  registered with FFI, emit `$function_pointer` with its FFI\n  signature; if it's a Lua function, emit `$lang_opaque` with\n  `lang: \"lua\"` and a tag the spec can use to resolve the\n  function back later (a registry index, for example).\n- **Userdata** with an FFI ctype — emit `$function_pointer` if\n  the type is a function pointer; `$ref` if the type is a sized\n  buffer; `$lang_opaque` otherwise.\n- **Coroutine** (`LUA_TTHREAD`) — `$lang_opaque` with\n  `shape: \"coroutine\"`.\n- **Large strings or tables** — at the spec's discretion, the\n  producer may write the value to the large-value heap and emit\n  `$ref` instead of inlining the bytes. Decision is per-call,\n  driven by size threshold or output annotation.\n\n### C\n\nThe C spec's generated wrapper (issue 307) knows the box's\ndeclared output type. The wrapper emits the right sentinel\nshape based on the type:\n\n- A declared `function_pointer` return — `$function_pointer`\n  with the type's signature.\n- A declared `bytes` return whose size exceeds the inline\n  threshold — `$ref` with the bytes written to the heap.\n- A declared opaque struct — `$lang_opaque` if the struct's\n  shape is C-only.\n\n### Bash\n\nBash has no native values besides strings; sentinels don't apply\non the emit side. A Bash producer always emits structural JSON\nstrings.\n\n## Consumer protocol\n\nEach spec's `json_to_native` walks the JSON tree and, when it\nsees a sentinel key, reconstructs the value using its language's\nmachinery. The reconstruction is the spec author's responsibility.\n\n### Lua\n\n**Superseded by the Amendment (2026-05-22)** for the\n`$function_pointer` case — the FFI-cast reconstruction below\nis no longer the target; instead, the consumer's spec emits a\nforeign-call wrapper that round-trips through a compiled binary\nor a long-lived subprocess. `$ref` and `$lang_opaque`\nreconstruction below remains current.\n\n```c\n// inside lua_json_to_native, on seeing {\"$function_pointer\": {...}}:\nconst char *sig = json_string_value(obj, \"signature\");\nuintptr_t   addr = json_int_value(obj, \"addr\");\nlua_getglobal(L, \"ffi\");\nlua_getfield(L, -1, \"cast\");\nlua_pushstring(L, sig);                 // \"int (*)(void*, void*)\"\nlua_pushinteger(L, (lua_Integer)addr);\nlua_call(L, 2, 1);\n// stack top: an FFI callable Lua can invoke as compare_fn(a, b)\n```\n\n`$ref` reconstruction in Lua copies the bytes (`lua_pushlstring(ptr, len)`)\nsince Lua's value model needs values in Lua's heap. The\nproducer's refcount handles the lifetime.\n\n`$lang_opaque` with `lang: \"lua\"` resolves the tag through the\nworker's per-worker registry; with `lang != \"lua\"` it's a wire\ncompile error.\n\n### C\n\nDirect casts. `$function_pointer` becomes a typed function\npointer the wrapper can invoke. `$ref` is a `(void*, size_t)`\npair the wrapper hands to the user's function. `$lang_opaque`\nwith `lang: \"c\"` is a typed-struct pointer; other langs fail.\n\n### Bash\n\nBash cannot reconstruct any sentinel except possibly `$ref`\n(by reading the bytes from the file the marshaller staged at the\nprocess boundary). `$function_pointer` and `$lang_opaque` fail\nunless the producer chose the cross-process escape hatch (see\nbelow).\n\n## Compile-time validation\n\nThe compile step walks every wire and checks:\n\n- If the producer's declared output type can emit sentinel kind\n  K (per the producer language's spec capability), then\n- The consumer's language must be able to reconstruct sentinel\n  kind K (per the consumer language's spec capability).\n- If not, **the compile fails** with the specific wire and the\n  specific sentinel kind named.\n\nThis is editor-time feedback. The user fixes the wire\n(reroute it, change the consumer's language, attach a custom\ntranslation per issue 246) before the program ever runs.\n\nThe per-spec capability is a static fact each spec declares.\nAdding a new language K declares K's emit set and reconstruct\nset; the compile validator consults the declaration.\n\n## Cross-process escape hatch for `$function_pointer`\n\n**Superseded by the Amendment (2026-05-22)** — what this section\ndescribed as an opt-in escape hatch is now the *only* path. The\ndefault-is-FFI / escape-hatch-is-binary framing below is no\nlonger accurate; both cases now use a compiled binary, optionally\nbacked by a long-lived subprocess + socket. Keeping the text for\ncontext.\n\nBash (and any other process-isolated language) can't dereference\nan in-process function-pointer address. Two options when a\nfunction pointer's wire targets such a consumer:\n\n1. **Fail at compile time** (the default). Clear, honest.\n2. **Producer-side compiled binary** (opt-in). When the C spec\n   detects that a function-pointer output is wired to a\n   cross-process consumer, it compiles the function into a\n   standalone executable in `compiled/cross-process/<box>__<port>.bin`.\n   The sentinel becomes:\n\n   ```json\n   {\"$function_pointer\": {\"binary\": \"compiled/cross-process/...\",\n                          \"signature\": \"int(int,int)\"}}\n   ```\n\n   Bash invokes the binary with `$(./bin args...)` per call. Cost:\n   process spawn per invocation (1-10 ms). The escape hatch is\n   opt-in per box output — the user explicitly chooses the cost\n   in the inspector.\n\nThe default behaviour is option 1 because hiding the spawn cost\nwould mislead the user about runtime behaviour. The user picks\ntheir language; the cost follows from the choice. Option 2 is\nthe escape hatch for cases where the user genuinely needs\nC-from-Bash and accepts the cost.\n\n## Relationship to custom translation specs (issue 246)\n\nSentinels are the **spec author's tool** for representing\nnon-structural values. Custom translations are the **user's\ntool** for interpreting them (or any other value) when the\ndefault reconstruction isn't what they want.\n\nThe escalation path:\n\n1. Default spec encode / decode handles JSON-structural values\n   transparently.\n2. When the producer's value can't be encoded structurally, the\n   spec author's emit logic produces the right sentinel.\n3. When the consumer's spec can reconstruct the sentinel\n   generically (FFI cast, ctypes, direct pointer), the default\n   reconstruction runs.\n4. When the user wants a different interpretation than the\n   default (treat a function pointer as a method on a class\n   instance, dereference a `$ref` and parse its bytes as a\n   custom format, etc.), they attach a per-port custom\n   translation that overrides the default reconstruction.\n\nSo sentinels and custom translations are layered: sentinels\nprovide the *bytes that arrive at the wire* for non-structural\nvalues; custom translations decide *what to do with those bytes*\nwhen the default isn't enough.\n\n## Where in the dispatch this lives\n\nSentinels live inside the JSON ring of the dual-ring slot. The\nslot store (issue 312) doesn't know about them — it just carries\nbytes. The producer's `native_to_json` emits them when writing\nto the JSON ring; the consumer's `json_to_native` recognizes\nand reconstructs them when reading from the JSON ring.\n\nInside the native ring, sentinels don't appear — native values\nare encoded in the language's own binary form, which can\nrepresent its own callables / opaque values directly without\nneeding a JSON-side hack.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `langs/lang-spec.h` — bridges (`native_to_json`,\n  `json_to_native`) are where sentinel handling lives per spec.\n- `langs/lua/spec.c:188` (`encode_value`) — emit-side extension\n  point. Currently hard-errors on function / userdata / thread;\n  this issue replaces those errors with sentinel emission.\n- `langs/lua/spec.c:370` (`decode_node`) — reconstruct-side\n  extension point. Add sentinel recognition before generic\n  object handling.\n- `langs/c/spec.c` — C spec's `native_to_json` / `json_to_native`\n  (currently NULL); both grow when this issue lands.\n- `langs/bash/spec.c` — Bash spec; only `$ref` is reconstructable.\n- `src/015-large-value-heap.c` — `$ref` storage.\n- `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` — compile-time wire validation\n  walks producer/consumer sentinel capabilities.\n- `issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md` — dual-ring shape;\n  sentinels ride inside its JSON ring.\n- `issues/246-custom-translation-specs-per-port.md` — user-side\n  override layered on top of sentinel reconstruction.\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — wire format section; gains a brief\n  sentinel reference.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Define the canonical JSON shapes**. Three sentinel kinds,\n   exact key names, value-object schemas. Document in\n   `docs/001-architecture.md`.\n2. **Lua emit**: replace the hard-errors in `encode_value` with\n   sentinel emission per the producer protocol above. Start with\n   `$function_pointer` for FFI callables and `$lang_opaque` for\n   Lua functions / coroutines.\n3. **Lua reconstruct**: extend `decode_node` to recognize the\n   three sentinels and reconstruct them.\n4. **Per-spec capability declarations**. Each spec declares its\n   emit set (sentinel kinds it can produce) and reconstruct set\n   (sentinel kinds it can consume). Lives next to the\n   `lang_spec_t` declaration.\n5. **C spec sentinels**. Emit via the generated wrapper based on\n   declared output types; reconstruct via direct cast.\n6. **Bash spec sentinels**. Only `$ref` on the reconstruct side\n   (read bytes from the marshaller's staged file).\n7. **Compile-time validation**. Walk every wire; check the\n   producer's emit set against the consumer's reconstruct set;\n   fail with a clear message on mismatch.\n8. **Cross-process escape hatch for `$function_pointer`**.\n   Opt-in flag in the box output declaration; the C spec emits a\n   standalone binary instead of (or alongside) the in-process\n   address.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **`$ref` lifetime across iterator-fed slots**. See the\nAmendment section below; the original FFI-based reconstruction\ntext in the body is retained for context but is no longer the\ntarget.\n\n## Amendment (2026-05-22) — function pointers via wrapper binaries, not FFI\n\nThe original design had the consumer's spec reconstruct a\n`$function_pointer` by FFI-casting the raw process-local\naddress (LuaJIT's `ffi.cast`, ctypes, etc.). That path is\nlanguage-pair-specific by nature: it only works for languages\nthat ship an FFI binding to the target language's ABI, which\nbiases SoraMech toward the Lua↔C corner and leaves Bash and\nany future agnostic language out in the cold. SoraMech's\ncross-language story must be agnostic — N spec implementations,\nnot N² pair-wise paths — so FFI reconstruction is the wrong\nshape.\n\n**The replacement design:**\n\n1. **At map-compile time**, when the compiler sees a\n   `$function_pointer`-shaped wire crossing a language\n   boundary, it asks the *producing* spec to compile the\n   referenced function (and its enumerable dependencies) into\n   a standalone binary on disk. The binary speaks a small\n   request/response protocol over stdin/stdout or, when\n   performance matters, a Unix domain socket the runtime\n   spawned at startup.\n2. **The compiler then asks the *consuming* spec for a\n   wrapper recipe**: \"in your language, how do I invoke a\n   subprocess with these arguments and parse the response?\"\n   Every language can answer that question — Lua via\n   `io.popen` / `socket.connect`, C via `execve` /\n   `socket(2)`, Bash via literal `$(./bin args)` or\n   `socat` / `nc`. The consuming spec stamps a wrapper\n   function on disk (or inlines it into the merged module\n   per issue 313) that the consumer's source can call as if\n   the foreign function were local.\n3. **The `$function_pointer` sentinel's payload becomes**:\n\n   ```json\n   {\"$function_pointer\": {\"binary\": \"compiled/cross-lang/<box>__<port>.bin\",\n                          \"signature\": \"int(int,int)\",\n                          \"socket\":    \"compiled/cross-lang/<box>__<port>.sock\"}}\n   ```\n\n   The `socket` field is present when the runtime started the\n   binary as a long-lived subprocess and routes calls through\n   the socket; absent when the binary is spawned per call\n   (the cheap-and-stateless fallback).\n\n4. **State preservation comes from the persistent subprocess.**\n   The threading roadmap already commits to Unix domain\n   sockets for cross-language IPC; the same mechanism is what\n   makes long-lived foreign functions work. Each cross-language\n   function pointer used by a running map gets one subprocess\n   spawned at map start (or first use), and the wrapper does\n   socket round-trips per call. Latency: tens of microseconds,\n   not the millisecond cost of fork+exec. Closure state,\n   loaded models, cached connections — all survive between\n   calls in the subprocess's own memory.\n\n5. **Argument enumeration is the user's responsibility at\n   map-compile time.** Dynamic-language closures capture\n   upvalues (Lua) and `_ENV` (Lua) and lexical scope (most);\n   statically enumerating those is the FFI problem under\n   another name. Honest failure mode.\n\n### New spec responsibility: foreign-call wrappers\n\nThis adds one responsibility to `lang_spec_t`. Each spec\nprovides a function that emits a wrapper in its own language\ngiven a foreign-call protocol descriptor:\n\n```c\nint (*emit_foreign_call_wrapper)(void *handle,\n                                 const char *binary_path,\n                                 const char *socket_path_or_null,\n                                 const char *signature,\n                                 const char *out_wrapper_src_path);\n```\n\n- For Lua: writes a `.lua` file containing a function that\n  opens the socket (or popen's the binary) and round-trips\n  arguments / response.\n- For C: writes a `.c` file with the same logic, compiled\n  alongside the rest of the C-side merged module.\n- For Bash: writes a function definition that wraps a\n  `socat`-or-`nc`-or-`./bin` call.\n\nThe wrapper-recipe is the *only* per-language code the\nforeign-call story needs. The binaries themselves are produced\nby the producing spec's existing `compile` function. The\nprotocol on the wire is a single shared definition — not\nper-language — so the consuming spec doesn't need to know what\nlanguage wrote the binary.\n\n### What this leaves of the original sentinel design\n\nThe two other sentinels survive unchanged:\n\n- **`$ref`** — pointer + length into the large-value heap; same\n  in-process semantics as before, same cross-process inlining\n  at the UDS marshaller.\n- **`$lang_opaque`** — still a \"this language's private value,\n  consumer either understands or fails compile\" sentinel; the\n  fail-compile path stays the default.\n\n`$function_pointer`'s wire shape stays the same JSON-object\nform; only the reconstruction recipe changes. Specs that used\nto publish \"I can reconstruct `$function_pointer` via FFI\" in\ntheir capability declaration now publish \"I can emit a\nforeign-call wrapper\" instead — same capability slot, different\nmeaning.\n\n### Why agnostic wins here\n\nLuaJIT FFI is fast and would have been the easy path for\nLua↔C.
