A Bash producer always emits structural JSON\nstrings.\n\n## Consumer protocol\n\nEach spec's `json_to_native` walks the JSON tree and, when it\nsees a sentinel key, reconstructs the value using its language's\nmachinery. The reconstruction is the spec author's responsibility.\n\n### Lua\n\n**Superseded by the Amendment (2026-05-22)** for the\n`$function_pointer` case — the FFI-cast reconstruction below\nis no longer the target; instead, the consumer's spec emits a\nforeign-call wrapper that round-trips through a compiled binary\nor a long-lived subprocess. `$ref` and `$lang_opaque`\nreconstruction below remains current.\n\n```c\n// inside lua_json_to_native, on seeing {\"$function_pointer\": {...}}:\nconst char *sig = json_string_value(obj, \"signature\");\nuintptr_t   addr = json_int_value(obj, \"addr\");\nlua_getglobal(L, \"ffi\");\nlua_getfield(L, -1, \"cast\");\nlua_pushstring(L, sig);                 // \"int (*)(void*, void*)\"\nlua_pushinteger(L, (lua_Integer)addr);\nlua_call(L, 2, 1);\n// stack top: an FFI callable Lua can invoke as compare_fn(a, b)\n```\n\n`$ref` reconstruction in Lua copies the bytes (`lua_pushlstring(ptr, len)`)\nsince Lua's value model needs values in Lua's heap. The\nproducer's refcount handles the lifetime.\n\n`$lang_opaque` with `lang: \"lua\"` resolves the tag through the\nworker's per-worker registry; with `lang != \"lua\"` it's a wire\ncompile error.\n\n### C\n\nDirect casts. `$function_pointer` becomes a typed function\npointer the wrapper can invoke. `$ref` is a `(void*, size_t)`\npair the wrapper hands to the user's function. `$lang_opaque`\nwith `lang: \"c\"` is a typed-struct pointer; other langs fail.\n\n### Bash\n\nBash cannot reconstruct any sentinel except possibly `$ref`\n(by reading the bytes from the file the marshaller staged at the\nprocess boundary). `$function_pointer` and `$lang_opaque` fail\nunless the producer chose the cross-process escape hatch (see\nbelow).\n\n## Compile-time validation\n\nThe compile step walks every wire and checks:\n\n- If the producer's declared output type can emit sentinel kind\n  K (per the producer language's spec capability), then\n- The consumer's language must be able to reconstruct sentinel\n  kind K (per the consumer language's spec capability).\n- If not, **the compile fails** with the specific wire and the\n  specific sentinel kind named.\n\nThis is editor-time feedback. The user fixes the wire\n(reroute it, change the consumer's language, attach a custom\ntranslation per issue 246) before the program ever runs.\n\nThe per-spec capability is a static fact each spec declares.\nAdding a new language K declares K's emit set and reconstruct\nset; the compile validator consults the declaration.\n\n## Cross-process escape hatch for `$function_pointer`\n\n**Superseded by the Amendment (2026-05-22)** — what this section\ndescribed as an opt-in escape hatch is now the *only* path. The\ndefault-is-FFI / escape-hatch-is-binary framing below is no\nlonger accurate; both cases now use a compiled binary, optionally\nbacked by a long-lived subprocess + socket. Keeping the text for\ncontext.\n\nBash (and any other process-isolated language) can't dereference\nan in-process function-pointer address. Two options when a\nfunction pointer's wire targets such a consumer:\n\n1. **Fail at compile time** (the default). Clear, honest.\n2. **Producer-side compiled binary** (opt-in). When the C spec\n   detects that a function-pointer output is wired to a\n   cross-process consumer, it compiles the function into a\n   standalone executable in `compiled/cross-process/<box>__<port>.bin`.\n   The sentinel becomes:\n\n   ```json\n   {\"$function_pointer\": {\"binary\": \"compiled/cross-process/...\",\n                          \"signature\": \"int(int,int)\"}}\n   ```\n\n   Bash invokes the binary with `$(./bin args...)` per call. Cost:\n   process spawn per invocation (1-10 ms). The escape hatch is\n   opt-in per box output — the user explicitly chooses the cost\n   in the inspector.\n\nThe default behaviour is option 1 because hiding the spawn cost\nwould mislead the user about runtime behaviour. The user picks\ntheir language; the cost follows from the choice. Option 2 is\nthe escape hatch for cases where the user genuinely needs\nC-from-Bash and accepts the cost.\n\n## Relationship to custom translation specs (issue 246)\n\nSentinels are the **spec author's tool** for representing\nnon-structural values. Custom translations are the **user's\ntool** for interpreting them (or any other value) when the\ndefault reconstruction isn't what they want.\n\nThe escalation path:\n\n1. Default spec encode / decode handles JSON-structural values\n   transparently.\n2. When the producer's value can't be encoded structurally, the\n   spec author's emit logic produces the right sentinel.\n3. When the consumer's spec can reconstruct the sentinel\n   generically (FFI cast, ctypes, direct pointer), the default\n   reconstruction runs.\n4. When the user wants a different interpretation than the\n   default (treat a function pointer as a method on a class\n   instance, dereference a `$ref` and parse its bytes as a\n   custom format, etc.), they attach a per-port custom\n   translation that overrides the default reconstruction.\n\nSo sentinels and custom translations are layered: sentinels\nprovide the *bytes that arrive at the wire* for non-structural\nvalues; custom translations decide *what to do with those bytes*\nwhen the default isn't enough.\n\n## Where in the dispatch this lives\n\nSentinels live inside the JSON ring of the dual-ring slot. The\nslot store (issue 312) doesn't know about them — it just carries\nbytes. The producer's `native_to_json` emits them when writing\nto the JSON ring; the consumer's `json_to_native` recognizes\nand reconstructs them when reading from the JSON ring.\n\nInside the native ring, sentinels don't appear — native values\nare encoded in the language's own binary form, which can\nrepresent its own callables / opaque values directly without\nneeding a JSON-side hack.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `langs/lang-spec.h` — bridges (`native_to_json`,\n  `json_to_native`) are where sentinel handling lives per spec.\n- `langs/lua/spec.c:188` (`encode_value`) — emit-side extension\n  point. Currently hard-errors on function / userdata / thread;\n  this issue replaces those errors with sentinel emission.\n- `langs/lua/spec.c:370` (`decode_node`) — reconstruct-side\n  extension point. Add sentinel recognition before generic\n  object handling.\n- `langs/c/spec.c` — C spec's `native_to_json` / `json_to_native`\n  (currently NULL); both grow when this issue lands.\n- `langs/bash/spec.c` — Bash spec; only `$ref` is reconstructable.\n- `src/015-large-value-heap.c` — `$ref` storage.\n- `scripts/soramech-compile.sh` — compile-time wire validation\n  walks producer/consumer sentinel capabilities.\n- `issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md` — dual-ring shape;\n  sentinels ride inside its JSON ring.\n- `issues/246-custom-translation-specs-per-port.md` — user-side\n  override layered on top of sentinel reconstruction.\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — wire format section; gains a brief\n  sentinel reference.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. **Define the canonical JSON shapes**. Three sentinel kinds,\n   exact key names, value-object schemas. Document in\n   `docs/001-architecture.md`.\n2. **Lua emit**: replace the hard-errors in `encode_value` with\n   sentinel emission per the producer protocol above. Start with\n   `$function_pointer` for FFI callables and `$lang_opaque` for\n   Lua functions / coroutines.\n3. **Lua reconstruct**: extend `decode_node` to recognize the\n   three sentinels and reconstruct them.\n4. **Per-spec capability declarations**. Each spec declares its\n   emit set (sentinel kinds it can produce) and reconstruct set\n   (sentinel kinds it can consume). Lives next to the\n   `lang_spec_t` declaration.\n5. **C spec sentinels**. Emit via the generated wrapper based on\n   declared output types; reconstruct via direct cast.\n6. **Bash spec sentinels**. Only `$ref` on the reconstruct side\n   (read bytes from the marshaller's staged file).\n7. **Compile-time validation**. Walk every wire; check the\n   producer's emit set against the consumer's reconstruct set;\n   fail with a clear message on mismatch.\n8. **Cross-process escape hatch for `$function_pointer`**.\n   Opt-in flag in the box output declaration; the C spec emits a\n   standalone binary instead of (or alongside) the in-process\n   address.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **`$ref` lifetime across iterator-fed slots**. A producer's\n  output is referenced by an N-cell ring of consumer slots; each\n  cell holds the `$ref`, each pop decrements. Already supported\n  by the large-value heap's refcount, but worth verifying the\n  test coverage when sentinels land.\n- **Sentinel inside sentinel.** A `$ref` whose bytes are\n  themselves JSON containing a `$function_pointer` is legal but\n  weird. Document the recursive case; probably falls out of the\n  walker for free.\n- **Versioning the sentinel format**. The reserved key names\n  (`$ref`, `$function_pointer`, `$lang_opaque`) and the\n  value-object schemas are part of the compile-time contract.\n  Changing them is breaking. Worth a one-line stability note\n  somewhere.\n- **Cross-process `$ref` semantics**. In-process `$ref` is a raw\n  pointer + length. Cross-process (Bash via UDS), the marshaller\n  stages the bytes at the socket boundary. Decide whether the\n  Bash-side `$ref` reconstruction reads from a file path or\n  inlines the bytes in the request. The latter is simpler; the\n  former scales to bigger values.\n- **`bytes` returns on the C spec currently passthrough raw bytes\n  into the JSON ring.** The C spec's typed-output-JSON path\n  (issue 307 item 2) wraps strings in JSON quotes and passes\n  ints / doubles / bools through as valid JSON fragments — but for\n  a declared `bytes` return it writes the raw payload verbatim,\n  which is *not* valid JSON in the general case (non-UTF-8 bytes\n  break parsers; embedded quotes / backslashes mangle the wire).\n  The proper resolution belongs here, not in 307: small `bytes`\n  outputs should be base64-wrapped into a JSON string (or its own\n  sentinel kind), and large `bytes` outputs should follow the\n  `$ref` path already described for the heap. Until that lands,\n  cross-language `bytes` wires from C producers are an honest\n  hazard — flag in the compile-time validator if possible, or at\n  minimum document the gap so users don't wire a `bytes`\n  C-output into a Lua / Bash consumer expecting clean JSON.",
        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01CKNyZxEKBL9RcJfw9EJqxy",
        "type":"tool_result"
      }],
    "role":"user"
  }
}

    "content":"/* src/020-sentinels.c — sentinel primitives implementation.\n *\n * Three sentinel kinds, three responsibilities each (detect, emit,\n * for two of them also reconstruct via the per-spec json_to_native\n * path). This file is the spec-independent machinery; per-spec\n * emission and reconstruction lives in each language's spec.c.\n *\n * Slice-1 scope (issue 318): $lang_opaque and $ref are end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases respectively;\n * $function_pointer is parsed and rejected pending the amendment's\n * wrapper-binary subsystem.\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ sentinel_detect()\n *\n * Single-key match against the three reserved key names. We accept\n * any value type for the sentinel's payload — checking the inner\n * shape is the reconstructor's job, not the detector's. */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const struct json_node *node)\n{\n    if (!node) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    json_node_t *n = (json_node_t *)node;\n    if (json_kind(n) != JSON_OBJECT) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (json_object_size(n) != 1) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    const char *key = json_object_key(n, 0);\n    if (!key) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$ref\") == 0)              return SENTINEL_REF;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$lang_opaque\") == 0)      return SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$function_pointer\") == 0) return SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER;\n    return SENTINEL_NONE;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission writers */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref(json_writer_t *w, uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len)\n{\n    /* The pointer is rendered as hex inside a JSON string so it\n     * survives JSON-string-canonicalisation regardless of platform\n     * pointer width. Decoders parse via strtoull. */\n    char ptr_buf[32];\n    snprintf(ptr_buf, sizeof ptr_buf, \"0x%lx\", (unsigned long)chunk_ptr);\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$ref\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"chunk_ptr\"); json_writer_string(w, ptr_buf);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"len\");       json_writer_int   (w, len);\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque(json_writer_t *w,\n                                const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                const char *shape)\n{\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$lang_opaque\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key (w, \"lang\"); json_writer_string(w, lang ? lang : \"\");\n        json_writer_key (w, \"tag\");  json_writer_int   (w, (long long)tag);\n        if (shape && *shape) {\n            json_writer_key(w, \"shape\"); json_writer_string(w, shape);\n        }\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(json_writer_t *w,\n                                          const char *signature)\n{\n    /* Per the amendment: the wrapper-binary subsystem hasn't landed,\n     * so this writer emits a self-describing stub that the\n     * consumer's json_to_native is expected to reject with a clear\n     * \"not yet implemented\" message. Keeping the shape stable lets\n     * future wrapper-binary work migrate fixture data without\n     * rewriting the producer side. */\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$function_pointer\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key(w, \"signature\");\n        json_writer_string(w, signature ? signature : \"void(void)\");\n        json_writer_key(w, \"status\");\n        json_writer_string(w, \"wrapper-binary system not yet implemented\");\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide hash-less append-only table. We don't need fast\n * lookup; producers and consumers reference chunks by raw pointer,\n * which IS the lookup key. Keeping a table at all lets us\n * (a) own the lifetime explicitly and (b) bulk-free at run end\n * via sentinel_ref_store_clear so memory doesn't leak across\n * fresh invocations of the runner in long-lived tests.\n *\n * Concurrency: single mutex guards both append and clear. The\n * lookup path returns a stable pointer (the chunks themselves\n * never move) so reads outside the mutex are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void  *bytes;\n    int    len;\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t  *ref_table;\nstatic int           ref_count;\nstatic int           ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n        int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n        ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                     (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n        if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); free(copy); return 0; }\n        ref_table    = grown;\n        ref_capacity = new_cap;\n    }\n    ref_table[ref_count].bytes = copy;\n    ref_table[ref_count].len   = len;\n    ref_count++;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    return (uintptr_t)copy;\n}\n\nconst void *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if ((uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return ref_table[i].bytes;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nunsigned int sentinel_validate(unsigned int producer_mask,\n                               unsigned int consumer_mask)\n{\n    unsigned int gap = producer_mask & ~consumer_mask;\n    if (gap == 0) return 0;\n    /* Return the lowest-numbered offending bit so callers can name\n     * one specific kind in their diagnostic. */\n    for (unsigned int b = 1; b != 0; b <<= 1) {\n        if (gap & b) return b;\n    }\n    return gap;   /* unreachable in practice */\n}\n\nconst char *sentinel_kind_name(sentinel_kind_t k)\n{\n    switch (k) {\n        case SENTINEL_NONE:             return \"(none)\";\n        case SENTINEL_REF:              return \"$ref\";\n        case SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE:      return \"$lang_opaque\";\n        case SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER: return \"$function_pointer\";\n        default:                        return \"(unknown)\";\n    }\n}\n/* }}} */\n"

          "content":"/* src/020-sentinels.h — cross-language JSON sentinel primitives.\n *\n * Three reserved JSON object shapes for values JSON can't represent\n * structurally (issue 318):\n *\n *   {\"$ref\":              {\"chunk_ptr\": \"0x...\", \"len\": N}}\n *   {\"$function_pointer\": {...}}    -- amendment: wrapper-binary path\n *   {\"$lang_opaque\":      {\"lang\": \"lua\", \"tag\": N, \"shape\": \"...\"}}\n *\n * The producer's spec emits the appropriate sentinel when its\n * encode walker hits a value JSON can't carry. The consumer's spec\n * detects sentinels in the parsed JSON tree and reconstructs the\n * value using language-specific machinery. Wires whose producer\n * may emit a sentinel kind the consumer can't reconstruct surface\n * at compile time as a wire-validation warning.\n *\n * This header exposes:\n *  - the sentinel kind enum + capability bitmask\n *  - JSON shape detection (parse a node, return the kind)\n *  - JSON shape writers (emit canonical bytes for each kind)\n *  - a process-wide $ref bytes store (allocate, lookup, release)\n *  - capability validation helpers used by the compile-time wire\n *    walker\n *\n * Designed and amended in issue 318. Sliced down for one-shot\n * implementation: $lang_opaque and $ref are functional end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases; $function_pointer is\n * parsed and rejected with a clear \"wrapper-binary system not yet\n * implemented\" error until the amendment's design lands.\n */\n#ifndef SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H\n#define SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\nstruct json_node;\nstruct json_writer;\n\n/* {{{ Sentinel kinds and capability bitmask */\ntypedef enum {\n    SENTINEL_NONE             = 0,\n    SENTINEL_REF              = 1,\n    SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE      = 2,\n    SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER = 3,\n} sentinel_kind_t;\n\n/* Capability bits combined into a per-spec mask. A spec's\n * `sentinel_emit_mask` says which kinds its native_to_json may\n * produce; its `sentinel_reconstruct_mask` says which kinds its\n * json_to_native can rebuild. */\n#define SENTINEL_BIT(K)            (1u << (unsigned)(K))\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_REF          SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_REF)\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE  SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE)\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_FN_POINTER   SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Detection — parse-side\n *\n * Returns the sentinel kind for a JSON object that has exactly one\n * top-level key matching a sentinel name, or SENTINEL_NONE for\n * anything else (including arrays / scalars / multi-key objects). */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const struct json_node *node);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission — write-side helpers\n *\n * Each writer emits the canonical bytes for the kind. The producing\n * spec calls these from inside its encode walker; the writer leaves\n * the cursor where any surrounding context expects it. */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref         (struct json_writer *w,\n                                 uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len);\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque (struct json_writer *w,\n                                 const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                 const char *shape);\n\n/* The function-pointer shape lands when the amendment's wrapper-\n * binary system is implemented. Until then this writer emits a\n * sentinel that will refuse to reconstruct, with a self-describing\n * stub payload that future fixture data can be migrated from. */\nvoid sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(struct json_writer *w,\n                                          const char *signature);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref bytes store (process-wide, leak-per-run)\n *\n * `sentinel_ref_alloc` copies `bytes` into a process-wide pool and\n * returns a chunk pointer that the producer embeds in its sentinel.\n * The consumer's `sentinel_ref_lookup` returns the same byte\n * pointer.\n *\n * Slice-1 lifetime model: bytes live until process exit (or until\n * `sentinel_ref_store_clear()` is called by the test harness).\n * Proper refcount-driven release tied to consumer reads is a\n * follow-on — the issue documents the lifetime concern but the\n * simpler shape unblocks end-to-end testing today. */\nuintptr_t        sentinel_ref_alloc (const void *bytes, int len);\nconst void      *sentinel_ref_lookup(uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int *out_len);\nvoid             sentinel_ref_store_clear(void);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation\n *\n * Returns 0 if every emit bit set on `producer_mask` also appears\n * in `consumer_mask`; returns the offending bit (>0) if any kind\n * the producer may emit is unreconstructable by the consumer.     "originalFile":"/* src/020-sentinels.h — cross-language JSON sentinel primitives.\n *\n * Three reserved JSON object shapes for values JSON can't represent\n * structurally (issue 318):\n *\n *   {\"$ref\":              {\"chunk_ptr\": \"0x...\", \"len\": N}}\n *   {\"$function_pointer\": {...}}    -- amendment: wrapper-binary path\n *   {\"$lang_opaque\":      {\"lang\": \"lua\", \"tag\": N, \"shape\": \"...\"}}\n *\n * The producer's spec emits the appropriate sentinel when its\n * encode walker hits a value JSON can't carry. The consumer's spec\n * detects sentinels in the parsed JSON tree and reconstructs the\n * value using language-specific machinery. Wires whose producer\n * may emit a sentinel kind the consumer can't reconstruct surface\n * at compile time as a wire-validation warning.\n *\n * This header exposes:\n *  - the sentinel kind enum + capability bitmask\n *  - JSON shape detection (parse a node, return the kind)\n *  - JSON shape writers (emit canonical bytes for each kind)\n *  - a process-wide $ref bytes store (allocate, lookup, release)\n *  - capability validation helpers used by the compile-time wire\n *    walker\n *\n * Designed and amended in issue 318. Sliced down for one-shot\n * implementation: $lang_opaque and $ref are functional end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases; $function_pointer is\n * parsed and rejected with a clear \"wrapper-binary system not yet\n * implemented\" error until the amendment's design lands.\n */\n#ifndef SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H\n#define SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H\n\n#include <stddef.h>\n#include <stdint.h>\n\nstruct json_node;\nstruct json_writer;\n\n/* {{{ Sentinel kinds and capability bitmask */\ntypedef enum {\n    SENTINEL_NONE             = 0,\n    SENTINEL_REF              = 1,\n    SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE      = 2,\n    SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER = 3,\n} sentinel_kind_t;\n\n/* Capability bits combined into a per-spec mask. A spec's\n * `sentinel_emit_mask` says which kinds its native_to_json may\n * produce; its `sentinel_reconstruct_mask` says which kinds its\n * json_to_native can rebuild. */\n#define SENTINEL_BIT(K)            (1u << (unsigned)(K))\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_REF          SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_REF)\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE  SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE)\n#define SENTINEL_MASK_FN_POINTER   SENTINEL_BIT(SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Detection — parse-side\n *\n * Returns the sentinel kind for a JSON object that has exactly one\n * top-level key matching a sentinel name, or SENTINEL_NONE for\n * anything else (including arrays / scalars / multi-key objects). */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const struct json_node *node);\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission — write-side helpers\n *\n * Each writer emits the canonical bytes for the kind. The producing\n * spec calls these from inside its encode walker; the writer leaves\n * the cursor where any surrounding context expects it. */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref         (struct json_writer *w,\n                                 uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len);\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque (struct json_writer *w,\n                                 const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                 const char *shape);\n\n/* The function-pointer shape lands when the amendment's wrapper-\n * binary system is implemented. The\n * compile-time wire walker uses this to surface mismatches. */\nunsigned int sentinel_validate(unsigned int producer_mask,\n                               unsigned int consumer_mask);\n\n/* Human-readable name of a sentinel kind for diagnostics. */\nconst char *sentinel_kind_name(sentinel_kind_t k);\n/* }}} */\n\n#endif /* SORAMECH_020_SENTINELS_H */\n",

    "originalFile":"/* src/020-sentinels.c — sentinel primitives implementation.\n *\n * Three sentinel kinds, three responsibilities each (detect, emit,\n * for two of them also reconstruct via the per-spec json_to_native\n * path). This file is the spec-independent machinery; per-spec\n * emission and reconstruction lives in each language's spec.c.\n *\n * Slice-1 scope (issue 318): $lang_opaque and $ref are end-to-end\n * for intra-language and in-process cases respectively;\n * $function_pointer is parsed and rejected pending the amendment's\n * wrapper-binary subsystem.\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <pthread.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ sentinel_detect()\n *\n * Single-key match against the three reserved key names. We accept\n * any value type for the sentinel's payload — checking the inner\n * shape is the reconstructor's job, not the detector's. */\nsentinel_kind_t sentinel_detect(const struct json_node *node)\n{\n    if (!node) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    json_node_t *n = (json_node_t *)node;\n    if (json_kind(n) != JSON_OBJECT) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (json_object_size(n) != 1) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    const char *key = json_object_key(n, 0);\n    if (!key) return SENTINEL_NONE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$ref\") == 0)              return SENTINEL_REF;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$lang_opaque\") == 0)      return SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE;\n    if (strcmp(key, \"$function_pointer\") == 0) return SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER;\n    return SENTINEL_NONE;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Emission writers */\nvoid sentinel_write_ref(json_writer_t *w, uintptr_t chunk_ptr, int len)\n{\n    /* The pointer is rendered as hex inside a JSON string so it\n     * survives JSON-string-canonicalisation regardless of platform\n     * pointer width. Decoders parse via strtoull. */\n    char ptr_buf[32];\n    snprintf(ptr_buf, sizeof ptr_buf, \"0x%lx\", (unsigned long)chunk_ptr);\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$ref\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"chunk_ptr\"); json_writer_string(w, ptr_buf);\n        json_writer_key   (w, \"len\");       json_writer_int   (w, len);\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_lang_opaque(json_writer_t *w,\n                                const char *lang, uint64_t tag,\n                                const char *shape)\n{\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$lang_opaque\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key (w, \"lang\"); json_writer_string(w, lang ? lang : \"\");\n        json_writer_key (w, \"tag\");  json_writer_int   (w, (long long)tag);\n        if (shape && *shape) {\n            json_writer_key(w, \"shape\"); json_writer_string(w, shape);\n        }\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(json_writer_t *w,\n                                          const char *signature)\n{\n    /* Per the amendment: the wrapper-binary subsystem hasn't landed,\n     * so this writer emits a self-describing stub that the\n     * consumer's json_to_native is expected to reject with a clear\n     * \"not yet implemented\" message. Keeping the shape stable lets\n     * future wrapper-binary work migrate fixture data without\n     * rewriting the producer side. */\n    json_writer_object(w);\n      json_writer_key(w, \"$function_pointer\");\n      json_writer_object(w);\n        json_writer_key(w, \"signature\");\n        json_writer_string(w, signature ? signature : \"void(void)\");\n        json_writer_key(w, \"status\");\n        json_writer_string(w, \"wrapper-binary system not yet implemented\");\n      json_writer_end(w);\n    json_writer_end(w);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref bytes store\n *\n * Process-wide hash-less append-only table. We don't need fast\n * lookup; producers and consumers reference chunks by raw pointer,\n * which IS the lookup key. Keeping a table at all lets us\n * (a) own the lifetime explicitly and (b) bulk-free at run end\n * via sentinel_ref_store_clear so memory doesn't leak across\n * fresh invocations of the runner in long-lived tests.\n *\n * Concurrency: single mutex guards both append and clear. The\n * lookup path returns a stable pointer (the chunks themselves\n * never move) so reads outside the mutex are safe. */\ntypedef struct ref_entry {\n    void  *bytes;\n    int    len;\n} ref_entry_t;\n\nstatic ref_entry_t  *ref_table;\nstatic int           ref_count;\nstatic int           ref_capacity;\nstatic pthread_mutex_t ref_mu = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;\n\nuintptr_t sentinel_ref_alloc(const void *bytes, int len)\n{\n    if (len < 0) return 0;\n    void *copy = malloc((size_t)len);\n    if (!copy && len > 0) return 0;\n    if (len > 0) memcpy(copy, bytes, (size_t)len);\n\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    if (ref_count == ref_capacity) {\n        int new_cap = ref_capacity == 0 ? 16 : ref_capacity * 2;\n        ref_entry_t *grown = realloc(ref_table,\n                                     (size_t)new_cap * sizeof *ref_table);\n        if (!grown) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu); i < ref_count; i++) {\n        if ((uintptr_t)ref_table[i].bytes == chunk_ptr) {\n            if (out_len) *out_len = ref_table[i].len;\n            pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n            return ref_table[i].bytes;\n        }\n    }\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n    if (out_len) *out_len = 0;\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nvoid sentinel_ref_store_clear(void)\n{\n    pthread_mutex_lock(&ref_mu);\n    for (int i = 0; i < ref_count; i++) free(ref_table[i].bytes);\n    free(ref_table);\n    ref_table    = NULL;\n    ref_count    = 0;\n    ref_capacity = 0;\n    pthread_mutex_unlock(&ref_mu);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nunsigned int sentinel_validate(unsigned int producer_mask,\n                               unsigned int consumer_mask)\n{\n    unsigned int gap = producer_mask & ~consumer_mask;\n    if (gap == 0) return 0;\n    /* Return the lowest-numbered offending bit so callers can name\n     * one specific kind in their diagnostic. */\n    for (unsigned int b = 1; {
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2baedbcc-ddb4-404a-b302-be37cf0eb28f",

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/scripts/run-tests.sh",
    "newString":"    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi",
    "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]];     "originalFile":"#!/bin/bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh — phase 3 integration tests.\n#\n# Runs every fixture map under tests/maps/ through `soramech-pool`\n# and asserts that the captured outputs match a hardcoded\n# expectation per map. The point is to catch regressions\n# end-to-end — past the spec interface, past the dispatch action,\n# past JSONL writing — rather than via the in-process unit tests.\n#\n# Per the project convention: scripts run from any directory via a\n# hard-coded ${DIR} path with an override argument; all paths are\n# relative to ${DIR}.\n\nset -u\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\nif [[ $# -ge 1 ]]; then\n    DIR=\"$1\"\nfi\n\ncd \"$DIR\"\n\npass=0\nfail=0\nfailures=()\n\n# {{{ check_map() — run one fixture, verify expected substrings\ncheck_map() {\n    local map=\"$1\"\n    shift\n    local expected=(\"$@\")\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"$map\"\n\n    local output\n    # Per-map env opt-in: a map may set SORAMECH_TEST_WORKERS to\n    # pin worker count for tests that depend on per-worker state\n    # (e.g. issue 318's $lang_opaque, which lives in the producer's\n    # Lua registry and can only be reconstructed by a consumer on\n    # the same worker).\n    local workers_env=\"\"\n    if [[ -f \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\" ]]; then\n        workers_env=$(cat \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map/.test_workers\")\n    fi\n    if [[ -n \"$workers_env\" ]]; then\n        output=$(SORAMECH_WORKERS=\"$workers_env\" \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    else\n        output=$(\"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/$map\" 2>&1)\n    fi\n    local rc=$?\n\n    local missing=\"\"\n    if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then\n        missing=\"exit=$rc\"\n    fi\n    for e in \"${expected[@]}\"; do\n        if [[ \"$output\" != *\"$e\"* ]]; then\n            missing+=\"${missing:+; }missing '$e'\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    if [[ -z \"$missing\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — %s\\n\" \"$missing\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"$map: $missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ pipeline_output_check() — additional: the pipeline writes to disk\npipeline_output_check() {\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    \"$DIR/soramech-pool\" \"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\" > /dev/null 2>&1\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"pipeline write output\"\n    if [[ -f \"$file\" ]]; then\n        local content\n        content=$(cat \"$file\")\n        if [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL — expected '11!', got '%s'\\n\" \"$content\"\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"pipeline file: $content\")\n        fi\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output file missing\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"pipeline: $file missing\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ compile_pipeline_check() — soramech-compile produces a portable artifact\n# Verifies issue 309's compile pipeline: bundles all spec.so + sources\n# into compiled/, then runs the artifact from /tmp (i.e. with no\n# dependency on the project's cwd) and verifies it produces the same\n# output as the source map.\ncompile_pipeline_check() {\n    local map=\"$DIR/tests/maps/pipeline\"\n    local compiled=\"$map/compiled\"\n    local file=\"/tmp/soramech-pipeline-out.txt\"\n\n    printf \"  %-44s \" \"compile pipeline (portable run)\"\n\n    rm -rf \"$compiled\"\n    if ! \"$DIR/scripts/soramech-compile.sh\" \"$map\" --dir \"$DIR\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"FAIL — soramech-compile failed\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: script returned non-zero\")\n        return\n    fi\n    if [[ ! -x \"$compiled/pool-runner\" ]]; then\n        printf \"FAIL — compiled/pool-runner missing or not executable\\n\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: pool-runner missing\")\n        return\n    fi\n\n    rm -f \"$file\"\n    local output\n    output=$(cd /tmp && \"$compiled/pool-runner\" \"$compiled\" 2>&1)\n\n    local content=\"\"\n    [[ -f \"$file\" ]] && content=$(cat \"$file\")\n\n    if [[ \"$output\" == *\"addone → 11\"* ]] && [[ \"$content\" == \"11!\" ]]; then\n        printf \"ok\\n\"\n        pass=$((pass + 1))\n    else\n        printf \"FAIL — output='%s' file='%s'\\n\" \"$output\" \"$content\"\n        fail=$((fail + 1))\n        failures+=(\"compile: bad output\")\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ run all fixtures\necho \"integration tests (fixture maps):\"\n\ncheck_map \"calc\" \\\n    \"add → 42\"\n\ncheck_map \"hello\" \\\n    \"greet → Hello, World!\"\n\ncheck_map \"comparator\" \\\n    \"classify → 8\" \\\n    \"high → HIGH:8\" \\\n    \"low → (no output)\" \\\n    \"mid → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"iter-route\" \\\n    \"iter → hi\" \\\n    \"a → A:hi\" \\\n    \"b → (no output)\" \\\n    \"c → (no output)\"\n\ncheck_map \"pipeline\" \\\n    \"double → 10\" \\\n    \"addone → 11\" \\\n    \"shout → 11!\"\n\ncheck_map \"read-literal\" \\\n    \"echo → hello, world!\"\n\ncheck_map \"319a-many-inputs\" \\\n    \"combine → count=20 sum=210\"\n\ncheck_map \"319d-runtime-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"auto_\" \\\n    \"echo_dyn-received:trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"319e-c-create\" \\\n    \"trigger → c-trigger-fired:auto_\" \\\n    \"c-echo-received:c-trigger-fired:auto_\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-c-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:HELLO-FROM-SEED\"\n\ncheck_map \"246-lua-shim\" \\\n    \"echo → seen:REV-fedcba\"\n\npipeline_output_check\ncompile_pipeline_check\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ parser_tests() — issue 232: unit tests for langs/<lang>/parser.js\n# Run Node's built-in test runner over each per-language parser test\n# file and fold the result into the surrounding pass/fail counters.\n# Each .mjs file is one logical \"test\" from this script's perspective;\n# Node prints its own subtest breakdown on failure for the diagnostic.\nparser_tests() {\n    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        printf \"  %-44s SKIP — node not installed\\n\" \"parser tests (lua, bash)\"\n        return\n    fi\n    for tf in \"$DIR/tests/232-lua-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/233-bash-parser-test.mjs\" \\\n              \"$DIR/tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs\"; do\n        local label\n        label=$(basename \"$tf\")\n        printf \"  %-44s \" \"$label\"\n        local out\n        out=$(SORAMECH_DIR=\"$DIR\" node --test \"$tf\" 2>&1)\n        local rc=$?\n        if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then\n            printf \"ok\\n\"\n            pass=$((pass + 1))\n        else\n            printf \"FAIL\\n\"\n            echo \"$out\" | sed 's/^/      /'\n            fail=$((fail + 1))\n            failures+=(\"$label: node --test exit=$rc\")\n        fi\n    done\n}\nparser_tests\n# }}}\n\necho\necho \"  $pass passed, $fail failed\"\n\nif [[ $fail -gt 0 ]]; then\n    echo\n    echo \"  failures:\"\n    for f in \"${failures[@]}\"; do\n        echo \"    - $f\"\n    done\nfi\n\nexit $fail\n",

          "content":"/* tests/020-sentinels-test.c — unit tests for src/020-sentinels.\n *\n * Covers the spec-independent sentinel machinery:\n *  - kind detection on parsed JSON\n *  - emit writers produce parseable JSON whose round-trip detects\n *    as the expected kind\n *  - $ref store: alloc / lookup / clear\n *  - capability validation: gap detection across emit / reconstruct\n *    masks\n */\n#include \"020-sentinels.h\"\n#include \"json.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n/* {{{ Tiny test harness */\n#define ASSERT(cond) do { \\\n    if (!(cond)) { \\\n        printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #cond); \\\n        return 0; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n\nstatic int tests_run = 0, tests_passed = 0;\n#define RUN(name) do { \\\n    tests_run++; \\\n    printf(\"  %-44s \", #name); \\\n    fflush(stdout); \\\n    if (test_##name()) { \\\n        printf(\"ok\\n\"); \\\n        tests_passed++; \\\n    } \\\n} while (0)\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ detect_round_trip — emit then re-detect */\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_ref(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_ref(&w, 0xCAFEBABE, 1024);\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(a, buf, &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(root != NULL);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(root) == SENTINEL_REF);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_lang_opaque(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_lang_opaque(&w, \"lua\", 42, \"function\");\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(a, buf, &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(root != NULL);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(root) == SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int test_detect_round_trip_function_pointer_stub(void)\n{\n    char buf[256];\n    json_writer_t w;\n    json_writer_init(&w, buf, sizeof buf);\n    sentinel_write_function_pointer_stub(&w, \"int(int,int)\");\n    int n = json_writer_finish(&w);\n    ASSERT(n > 0);\n\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n    json_node_t *root = json_parse(a, buf, &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(root != NULL);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(root) == SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER);\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Non-sentinel objects don't false-positive */\nstatic int test_detect_skips_plain_objects(void)\n{\n    json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n\n    /* Plain object — multiple keys. */\n    json_node_t *n1 = json_parse(a, \"{\\\"a\\\":1,\\\"b\\\":2}\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n1) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n\n    /* Single-key object whose key isn't a sentinel name. */\n    json_node_t *n2 = json_parse(a, \"{\\\"foo\\\":1}\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n2) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n\n    /* Arrays / scalars / null. */\n    json_node_t *n3 = json_parse(a, \"[1,2,3]\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n3) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n    json_node_t *n4 = json_parse(a, \"42\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n4) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n    json_node_t *n5 = json_parse(a, \"null\", &eo, &em);\n    ASSERT(sentinel_detect(n5) == SENTINEL_NONE);\n\n    json_arena_destroy(a);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ $ref store round-trip */\nstatic int test_ref_store(void)\n{\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    const char *payload = \"0123456789ABCDEF\";\n    int len = (int)strlen(payload);\n    uintptr_t p = sentinel_ref_alloc(payload, len);\n    ASSERT(p != 0);\n    int got_len = 0;\n    const void *got = sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &got_len);\n    ASSERT(got != NULL);\n    ASSERT(got_len == len);\n    ASSERT(memcmp(got, payload, (size_t)len) == 0);\n\n    /* Lookup with a wrong pointer returns NULL. */\n    int dummy = 0;\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p + 1, &dummy) == NULL);\n\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    /* After clear, the pointer is no longer valid (and may be freed\n     * memory — we only assert lookup miss, not dereferencing). */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &dummy) == NULL);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nstatic int test_validate(void)\n{\n    /* No emission → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(0, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* Identical capabilities → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Consumer covers producer's emit set → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Producer emits something consumer can't reconstruct → gap. */\n    unsigned int gap = sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF);\n    ASSERT(gap == SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Kind names */\nstatic int test_kind_names(void)\n{\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_NONE),             \"(none)\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_REF),              \"$ref\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_LANG_OPAQUE),      \"$lang_opaque\") == 0);\n    ASSERT(strcmp(sentinel_kind_name(SENTINEL_FUNCTION_POINTER), \"$function_pointer\") == 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\nint main(void)\n{\n    printf(\"020-sentinels-test:\\n\");\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_ref);\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_lang_opaque);\n    RUN(detect_round_trip_function_pointer_stub);\n    RUN(detect_skips_plain_objects);\n    RUN(ref_store);\n    RUN(validate);\n    RUN(kind_names);\n    printf(\"\\n  %d passed, %d failed\\n\",\n           tests_passed, tests_run - tests_passed);\n    return tests_run == tests_passed ? 0 : 1;\n}\n"

json_arena_t *a = json_arena_create();\n    int eo; const char *em;\n\n    /* Plain object — multiple keys. */\n    json_node_t *n1 = json_parse(a, \"{\\\"a\\\":1,\\\"b\\\":2}\", &eo, &em);\n *payload = \"0123456789ABCDEF\";\n    int len = (int)strlen(payload);\n    uintptr_t p = sentinel_ref_alloc(payload, len);\n    ASSERT(p != 0);\n    int got_len = 0;\n    const void *got = sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &got_len);\n    ASSERT(got != NULL);\n    ASSERT(got_len == len);\n    ASSERT(memcmp(got, payload, (size_t)len) == 0);\n\n    /* Lookup with a wrong pointer returns NULL. */\n    int dummy = 0;\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p + 1, &dummy) == NULL);\n\n    sentinel_ref_store_clear();\n    /* After clear, the pointer is no longer valid (and may be freed\n     * memory — we only assert lookup miss, not dereferencing). */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_ref_lookup(p, &dummy) == NULL);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ Capability validation */\nstatic int test_validate(void)\n{\n    /* No emission → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(0, 0) == 0);\n\n    /* Identical capabilities → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Consumer covers producer's emit set → no gap. */\n    ASSERT(sentinel_validate(\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF,\n        SENTINEL_MASK_REF | SENTINEL_MASK_LANG_OPAQUE) == 0);\n\n    /* Producer emits something consumer can't reconstruct → gap. */\n     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test: {
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"582fc87e-d8e1-4e46-8873-dc19593aa947",
  "gitBranch":"master",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "parentUuid":"582fc87e-d8e1-4e46-8873-dc19593aa947",

  "sessionId":"1228a221-1c09-4c26-94f3-172d7777b2b9",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-24T01:39:53.869Z",
  "promptId":"61ac4e23-446f-4a9b-9e30-d7abebde46b0",
  "userType":"external",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "type":"user",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/Makefile",
    "newString":"# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). The\n# pool runner pulls them in through POOL_SOURCES' wildcard; tests\n# name them explicitly.\nSPEC_LOADER_DEPS = $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/011-spec-registry-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                           $(SPEC_LOADER_DEPS)",
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test:     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.).     "originalFile":"# SoraMech — top-level build orchestration.\n#\n# What it does, in a sentence: builds the phase 3 pool runner binary\n# plus one shared library per language spec. Release by default;\n# DEBUG=1 keeps symbols and disables optimization, STRICT=1 promotes\n# warnings to errors. `make clean` removes everything that was built.\n#\n# Invokable from any directory: `make -C /path/to/soramech` works,\n# and the DIR variable can be overridden if needed (e.g. for an\n# out-of-tree checkout). All paths in this Makefile are relative to\n# $(DIR) per the project convention.\n#\n# Designed in issue 309. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. Implementation of the runner's runtime is\n# split across issues 301–308; this Makefile builds whatever sources\n# exist under src/, libs/task-pool/, and libs/json/, so it scales as\n# those issues land.\n\n# {{{ Resolve project root\nDIR ?= $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Toolchain & flags\nCC      ?= gcc\n\n# Shared header search path: every C source can find langs/lang-spec.h\n# and any future libs/<name>/ headers via -I flags below.\nCPPFLAGS = -I$(DIR)/langs -I$(DIR)/libs/task-pool -I$(DIR)/libs/json -I$(DIR)/src\n\n# Default to release; DEBUG and STRICT toggle alternates.\nifeq ($(DEBUG),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nelse ifeq ($(STRICT),1)\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -pthread -fPIC\nelse\n  CFLAGS = -O2 -Wall -pthread -fPIC\nendif\n\nLDFLAGS = -ldl -pthread -rdynamic\n# -rdynamic exports the runner's symbols to dlopen'd spec.so\n# plugins. Specs need this for the issue-319d self-construction\n# builtins (runtime_create_box / runtime_connect) — those live in\n# src/018-runtime-builtins.c, owned by the runner, and the Lua /\n# C / Bash spec.so binaries call back into them at runtime.\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Paths and source discovery\nBUILD_DIR = $(DIR)/build\nPOOL_BIN  = $(DIR)/soramech-pool\n\n# Wildcards: empty subdirs return empty lists, which is fine. As\n# issues 301/302/303/304/305 land their C sources here, they get\n# compiled automatically — no Makefile edit required.\nPOOL_SOURCES = \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/src/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/task-pool/*.c) \\\n  $(wildcard $(DIR)/libs/json/*.c)\n\nPOOL_OBJECTS = $(POOL_SOURCES:$(DIR)/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)\n\n# Test sources live in tests/ as C files named to match the source\n# they exercise (e.g. tests/009-slot-store-test.c exercises\n# src/009-slot-store.c). Each builds to a separate executable that\n# `make test` runs in turn.\nTEST_SOURCES = $(wildcard $(DIR)/tests/*.c)\nTEST_BINS    = $(TEST_SOURCES:$(DIR)/tests/%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%)\n\nLANGS = lua c bash\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Public targets\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test help\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: $(POOL_BIN)\n\nspecs:\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  echo \"  → langs/$$lang\"; \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) || exit 1; \\\n\tdone\n\nclean:\n\trm -f $(POOL_BIN)\n\trm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)\n\t@for lang in $(LANGS); do \\\n\t  $(MAKE) -s -C $(DIR)/langs/$$lang DIR=$(DIR) clean || true; \\\n\tdone\n\ntest: all $(TEST_BINS)\n\t@echo\n\t@fail=0; \\\n\tfor t in $(TEST_BINS); do \\\n\t  $$t || fail=1; \\\n\t  echo; \\\n\tdone; \\\n\tif [ -x $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh ]; then \\\n\t  $(DIR)/scripts/run-tests.sh $(DIR) || fail=1; \\\n\tfi; \\\n\texit $$fail\n\nhelp:\n\t@echo \"SoraMech build:\"\n\t@echo \"  make          — build runner + specs (release)\"\n\t@echo \"  make DEBUG=1  — debug info, no optimization\"\n\t@echo \"  make STRICT=1 — promote warnings to errors\"\n\t@echo \"  make clean    — remove every built artifact\"\n\t@echo \"  make test     — run integration tests (when 311 lands)\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ Build rules\n$(POOL_BIN): $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t@echo \"  → $(notdir $@)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDFLAGS)\n\n$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: $(DIR)/%.c\n\t@mkdir -p $(dir $@)\n\t@echo \"  → $(patsubst $(DIR)/%,%,$<)\"\n\t@$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(CPPFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<\n\n# Per-test dependency lines. A test binary needs its own .o plus\n# the .o files for the source(s) it exercises. As each test lands,\n# add one line here naming the dependencies (no globbing — explicit\n# is clearer than clever for tests).\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/009-slot-store-test:    $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                           $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/015-large-value-heap-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/015-large-value-heap.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/016-unified-allocator-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o\n$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/010-graph-loader-test: $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/009-slot-store.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/016-unified-allocator.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/src/011-spec-registry.o \\\n                                          $(BUILD_DIR)/libs/json/json.o\n# Every test binary that loads a language spec via dlopen needs the\n# runner-side symbols the specs call back into (issue 318's\n# sentinel_*, issue 319d's runtime_set_active_context, etc.). The\n# pool runner pulls them in through POOL_SOURCES' wildcard; tests\n# name them explicitly.\nSPEC_LOADER_DEPS = $(BUILD_DIR)/src/020-sentinels.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/018-runtime-builtins.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/017-box-id.o \\\n                   $(BUILD_DIR)/src/010-graph-loader.o \\\n
